relationships.keywords: Entamoeba trophozoites, erythrophagocytosis, stool microscopy, amoebic confirmation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by microscopic trophozoites in stool showing ingested red blood cells, which establishes acute amoebiasis and accounts for concomitant hepatic lesions.

relationships.keywords: seronegative status, triple negative serology, immunocompetent host, negative rule out
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Echinococcosis is ruled out by seronegative immunocompetent status across three distinct serological platforms in a patient with a multivesicular hepatic mass, pointing to biliary cystadenoma.

relationships.keywords: simple liver cyst, congenital cyst, thin wall, anechoic, non-parasitic
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a simple hepatic cyst, which exhibits a paper-thin wall (<1 mm), completely anechoic fluid, no internal septa, and negative serology, whereas Echinococcosis exhibits double-contour walls, daughter vesicles, hydatid sand, or calcifications.

relationships.keywords: Entamoeba histolytica, amoebic abscess, anchovy pus, acute fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from an amoebic liver abscess, which presents acutely with high spiking fever, right upper quadrant pain, absence of eosinophilia, and anchovy-paste pus, whereas Echinococcosis presents with chronic latency, intact parasitic membranes, and eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: pyogenic liver abscess, bacterial abscess, septic shock, toxic bandemia, purulent cavity
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a pyogenic liver abscess, which causes acute septic fevers, marked toxic neutrophilia, rapid cavity liquefaction, and response to antibiotics, whereas uncomplicated Echinococcosis is afebrile, encapsulated, and antibiotic-refractory.

relationships.keywords: hepatocellular carcinoma, HCC, arterial wash-in, venous wash-out, elevated AFP
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from hepatocellular carcinoma, which demonstrates characteristic arterial phase hyperenhancement with venous wash-out, markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein, and absence of the dense calcific matrix seen in alveolar echinococcosis.

relationships.keywords: cholangiocarcinoma, biliary cancer, CA19-9, rim enhancement, central necrosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, which displays progressive peripheral rim enhancement on dynamic imaging, elevated serum CA19-9, and absence of pathognomonic geographic microcalcifications and Em2+ seropositivity.

relationships.keywords: biliary cystadenoma, mucinous cyst, internal septa, mural nodules, ovarian stroma
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from biliary cystadenoma, which features irregular internal septations, enhancing mural nodules, ovarian-like stroma on histology, and negative Echinococcus serology without daughter cysts or protoscolices.

relationships.keywords: hepatic hemangioma, cavernous hemangioma, nodular puddling, centripetal fill-in
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from hepatic hemangioma, which demonstrates peripheral nodular discontinuous puddling with progressive centripetal fill-in on dynamic contrast imaging, unlike non-enhancing avascular echinococcal lesions.

relationships.keywords: hepatic metastases, liver mets, target lesions, elevated CEA, primary cancer
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from hepatic metastatic carcinoma, which features multiple ring-enhancing target lesions with central necrosis, elevated tumor markers (CEA, CA19-9), and known primary extrahepatic malignancy.

relationships.keywords: hepatic hematoma, liver hematoma, blunt abdominal trauma, resolving blood
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a hepatic abscessed hematoma, which presents with an antecedent history of acute abdominal trauma, evolving fluid density on CT, and total absence of parasitic membranes or scolices.

relationships.keywords: polycystic liver, adult polycystic kidney disease, diffuse liver cysts, thin walls
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from polycystic liver disease, which displays diffuse replacement of the liver parenchyma by hundreds of thin-walled non-calcified cysts without internal daughter vesicles, accompanied by polycystic kidneys.

relationships.keywords: choledochal cyst, bile duct dilatation, Todani classification, biliary cyst
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a congenital choledochal cyst, which presents with direct congenital communication with the bile ducts on cholangiography, lacking an encapsulated parasitic pericyst or hydatid sand.

relationships.keywords: lung abscess, pulmonary abscess, foul sputum, aspiration, necrotic cavity
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a pulmonary abscess, which presents acutely with high fever, foul-smelling purulent sputum, and thick irregular cavitary margins with fluid levels, whereas unruptured pulmonary hydatids are smooth-walled spherical water-density cysts.

relationships.keywords: pulmonary tuberculosis, TB cavity, acid-fast bacilli, apical infiltrates, night sweats
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from pulmonary tuberculosis, which presents with chronic fever, night sweats, apical cavitary infiltrates, and acid-fast bacilli on sputum smear, whereas pulmonary hydatid cysts are basilar spherical lesions with intact ectocysts.

relationships.keywords: bronchogenic cyst, foregut cyst, subcarinal mass, ciliated epithelium
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a bronchogenic cyst, which is a benign congenital subcarinal or paratracheal fluid-filled lesion lined by respiratory epithelium without daughter cysts, membranes, or Echinococcus seropositivity.

relationships.keywords: cystic renal cell carcinoma, RCC, hypervascular septa, mural nodule
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from cystic renal cell carcinoma, which features hypervascular enhancing septa, solid mural nodules, and early contrast enhancement on CT, whereas renal hydatids are avascular cystic masses with hydatid sand or calcified walls.

relationships.keywords: splenic epidermoid cyst, congenital splenic cyst, squamous lining, non-parasitic
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a splenic epidermoid cyst, which is a congenital thin-walled unilocular cyst in young patients with negative serology and squamoid epithelial lining, lacking hydatid pericysts or daughter vesicles.

relationships.keywords: neurocysticercosis, Taenia solium, scolex dot sign, parenchymal ring lesion
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from neurocysticercosis, which causes small (1–2 cm) ring-enhancing parenchymal cysts with a visible eccentric scolex (dot sign), whereas cerebral echinococcosis produces giant (>4–8 cm) unilocular cysts lacking contrast enhancement.

relationships.keywords: cystic astrocytoma, glioma, vasogenic edema, enhancing mural nodule
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Echinococcosis is differentiated from a cystic cerebral astrocytoma, which features an enhancing solid mural nodule and marked surrounding vasogenic edema on MRI, whereas cerebral hydatid cysts are spherical, sharply demarcated, and non-enhancing with minimal edema.

entities.name: Foodborne Trematodes
entities.description: A diverse group of zoonotic helminthic infections caused by digenetic flukes (liver flukes: Clonorchis, Opisthorchis, Fasciola; lung flukes: Paragonimus; intestinal flukes: Fasciolopsis, Heterophyes) acquired via ingestion of raw or undercooked freshwater fish, crustaceans, or aquatic plants.

entities.name: Biliary Colic
entities.description: Episodic, severe right upper quadrant or epigastric cramping pain resulting from mechanical irritation, obstruction, or migration of adult flukes within bile ducts.

entities.name: Acute Invasive Fascioliasis
entities.description: Acute clinical syndrome occurring during the 6 to 12 weeks of juvenile Fasciola migration through the peritoneal cavity and hepatic parenchyma.

entities.name: Chronic Biliary Fascioliasis
entities.description: Chronic hepatobiliary phase occurring when adult Fasciola flukes mature within major intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts, leading to biliary obstruction and fibrosis.

entities.name: Recurrent Pyogenic Cholangitis
entities.description: Repeated bacterial superinfections of the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree associated with chronic Clonorchis sinensis or Opisthorchis viverrini colonization and biliary stasis.

entities.name: Cholangiocarcinoma
entities.description: Malignant neoplasm of the biliary epithelium strongly driven by chronic Clonorchis sinensis and Opisthorchis viverrini infection, recognized as an IARC Group 1 definitive biological carcinogen.

entities.name: Pulmonary Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Indolent pulmonary disease caused by Paragonimus flukes encapsulated in lung parenchyma, causing chronic cough, chest pain, and hemoptysis.

entities.name: Chocolate-Sauce Sputum Hemoptysis
entities.description: Pathognomonic expectoration of thick, brownish-rusty or gelatinous sputum composed of clotted blood, necrotic lung tissue, and masses of Paragonimus operculated eggs.

entities.name: Cerebral Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Severe extrapulmonary ectopic disease resulting from juvenile Paragonimus migration through the jugular foramen into the cranial cavity and brain parenchyma.

entities.name: Acalculous Cholecystitis
entities.description: Acute gallbladder inflammation in the absence of gallstones, induced by adult fluke migration, mechanical trauma, or mucosal irritation within the cystic duct and gallbladder.

entities.name: Secondary Biliary Cirrhosis
entities.description: End-stage chronic hepatic parenchymal destruction and micronodular cirrhosis secondary to protracted biliary obstruction and chronic periductal inflammation.

entities.name: Biliary Ductal Strictures
entities.description: Focal and segmental fibrous narrowing of the intrahepatic and common bile ducts caused by chronic fluke attachment, mechanical abrasion, and mucosal scarring.

entities.name: Intrahepatic Ductal Ectasia
entities.description: Saccular and diffuse dilation of the medium and small peripheral intrahepatic bile ducts upstream of fluke-induced mucosal inflammation and periductal fibrosis.

entities.name: Mechanical Biliary Obstruction
entities.description: Physical impaction of living adult flukes, dead worm remnants, and surrounding biliary sludge within the biliary tree leading to cholestasis and jaundice.

entities.name: Chronic Productive Cough
entities.description: Persistent, debilitating cough lasting months to years caused by the bronchial communication of Paragonimus cyst cavities in the lung parenchyma.

entities.name: Pleuritic Chest Pain
entities.description: Sharp, respiration-dependent thoracic pain caused by juvenile fluke penetration across the diaphragm and parietal pleura into the pleural space.

entities.name: Parasitic Pleural Effusion
entities.description: Accumulation of exudative, eosinophil-rich fluid within the pleural cavity triggered by migrating Paragonimus larvae crossing pleural surfaces.

entities.name: Spontaneous Pneumothorax
entities.description: Acute accumulation of air in the pleural cavity caused by the rupture of subpleural necrotic Paragonimus cysts into the pleural space.

entities.name: Extrapulmonary Ectopic Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Aberrant larval migration of Paragonimus juvenile flukes into non-pulmonary tissues including the brain, spinal cord, abdominal wall, and scrotum.

entities.name: Subcutaneous Migratory Nodules
entities.description: Painful, pruritic, slow-moving subcutaneous swellings and inflammatory nodules produced by aberrantly migrating flukes in the subcutaneous fat and connective tissue.

entities.name: Ectopic Hepatic Migration
entities.description: Aberrant tracking of Paragonimus larvae through the liver capsule and parenchyma prior to breaching the diaphragm into the thoracic cavity.

entities.name: Intestinal Fasciolopsiasis
entities.description: Intestinal mucosal infection caused by the giant intestinal fluke Fasciolopsis buski adhering to the duodenal and jejunal mucosa.

entities.name: Chronic Mucous Diarrhea
entities.description: Frequent, loose, mucus-laden stools caused by extensive mechanical attachment and toxic secretome of intestinal flukes like Fasciolopsis buski and Heterophyes heterophyes.

entities.name: Protein-Losing Enteropathy
entities.description: Profound enteric loss of serum proteins across ulcerated, inflamed intestinal mucosa colonized by giant intestinal flukes.

entities.name: Periductal Fibrosis
entities.description: Concentric, dense fibrous thickening of the peribiliary stroma and intrahepatic connective tissue sheath induced by chronic fluke mechanical injury and secretome.

entities.name: Biliary Epithelial Hyperplasia
entities.description: Marked adenomatous proliferation, mucinous metaplasia, and goblet cell hyperplasia of the bile duct epithelial lining exposed to chronic liver fluke contact.

entities.name: Suppurative Bacterial Cholangitis
entities.description: Acute life-threatening purulent bacterial infection of the biliary conduits occurring when fluke-induced ductal obstruction facilitates rapid enteric bacterial multiplication.

entities.name: Hepatic Parenchymal Burrows
entities.description: Linear and serpentine necrotic hemorrhagic tracks created mechanically by juvenile Fasciola flukes tunneling through the liver parenchyma toward bile ducts.

entities.name: Glisson Capsule Perforation
entities.description: Direct mechanical puncture and erosion of the hepatic peritoneal covering (Glisson capsule) by migrating juvenile Fasciola flukes crossing from the peritoneum.

entities.name: Adult-Onset Parasitic Epilepsy
entities.description: New-onset focal or generalized seizures in an adult resident of an endemic region, triggered by intracranial Paragonimus fluke granulomas.

entities.name: Intracranial Space-Occupying Lesions
entities.description: Intracerebral granulomatous masses and cystic nodules produced by Paragonimus flukes, provoking intracranial hypertension.

entities.name: Intracerebral Hemorrhage
entities.description: Cerebral parenchymal bleeding resulting from parasite erosion of intracranial blood vessels or surrounding necrotic cavitation during cerebral paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Heterophyid Cardiac Embolization
entities.description: Aberrant hematogenous dissemination of minute Heterophyes or Metagonimus eggs into coronary vessels and myocardium, causing parasitic myocarditis.

entities.name: Spinal Cord Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Extradural or subdural granulomatous fluke lesions in the spinal canal producing progressive spinal cord compression and myelopathy.

entities.name: Eosinophilic Peritonitis
entities.description: Peritoneal exudative inflammation with abundant eosinophils caused by juvenile Fasciola flukes actively transiting across the peritoneal cavity.

entities.name: Hepatic Subcapsular Hematoma
entities.description: Subcapsular accumulation of blood beneath Glisson's capsule resulting from extensive parenchymal burrowing and laceration of intrahepatic microvessels.

entities.name: Acute Cholecystitis Mimic
entities.description: Severe episodic right upper quadrant pain, Murphy-like tenderness, and fever mimicking acute calculus cholecystitis, caused by fluke impaction in the cystic duct.

entities.name: Recurrent Pancreatitis
entities.description: Episodes of acute pancreatic inflammation triggered by fluke migration into the ampulla of Vater or main pancreatic duct.

entities.name: Biliary Microabscesses
entities.description: Multiple small parenchymal and periductal suppurative microabscesses developing along obstructed, colonized intrahepatic biliary branches.

entities.name: Chronic Cachexia
entities.description: Profound systemic wasting, muscle loss, and chronic asthenia resulting from long-standing biliary inflammation, anorexia, and malabsorption.

entities.name: Severe Anasarca
entities.description: Generalized, massive soft-tissue edema and third-space fluid accumulation resulting from extreme hypoalbuminemia in intestinal fluke disease.

entities.name: Rusty Sputum Expectoration
entities.description: Physical expectoration of viscous, chocolate-brown to rusty sputum containing blood, Charcot-Leyden crystals, and operculated eggs, pathognomonic of pulmonary paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Tender Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlarged, tender liver palpable below the right costal margin resulting from intense parenchymal inflammation, burrowing tracks, or biliary distension.

entities.name: Right Upper Quadrant Tenderness
entities.description: Exquisite focal tenderness on deep palpation over the right hypochondrium corresponding to Glisson capsule stretching or biliary inflammation.

entities.name: Intermittent Jaundice
entities.description: Fluctuating icterus of the skin and mucous membranes reflecting transient mechanical obstruction of major bile ducts by migrating flukes or biliary sludge.

entities.name: Urticarial Allergic Rash
entities.description: Pruritic, transient erythematous wheals and hives triggered by systemic hypersensitivity reactions to migrating fluke excretory-secretory antigens.

entities.name: Facial Angioedema
entities.description: Episodic, non-pitting edema of the periorbital and facial soft tissues caused by acute IgE-mediated hypersensitivity to circulating parasite antigens.

entities.name: Crepitant Pulmonary Rales
entities.description: Auscultatory crackles and crepitations over mid- and lower lung zones indicating alveolar inflammation and fluid surrounding fluke cavitary lesions.

entities.name: Decreased Breath Sounds
entities.description: Diminished vesicular breath sounds on auscultation over thoracic regions affected by parasitic pleural effusion or pleural thickening.

entities.name: Dullness to Percussion
entities.description: Stony percussion dullness over dependent hemithoraces indicating moderate to large exudative parasitic pleural fluid collections.

entities.name: Pleural Friction Rub
entities.description: Grating auscultatory sound heard during inspiration and expiration reflecting direct mechanical friction between inflamed, roughened pleural surfaces.

entities.name: Subcutaneous Crepitant Swellings
entities.description: Subcutaneous, doughy or crepitant migratory soft-tissue nodules that change anatomical location over days, pathognomonic of ectopic fluke tracking.

entities.name: Focal Neurological Deficits
entities.description: Hemiparesis, localized motor weakness, or sensory loss caused by cerebral fluke granulomas compressing cortical and subcortical pathways.

entities.name: Papilledema on Fundoscopy
entities.description: Bilateral optic disc swelling with blurred margins observed on ophthalmoscopy, indicating chronic intracranial hypertension from cerebral granulomas.

entities.name: Meningismus and Photophobia
entities.description: Nuchal rigidity, Kernig sign, and marked light sensitivity reflecting intense meningeal inflammation triggered by subarachnoid fluke antigens.

entities.name: Tender Epigastric Mass
entities.description: Palpable, ill-defined tender inflammatory mass in the epigastrium or left lobe of the liver representing confluent fluke burrows or omental wrapping.

entities.name: Palpable Distended Gallbladder
entities.description: Enlarged, smooth, tense gallbladder palpable in the right hypochondrium (Courvoisier-like sign) resulting from distal common bile duct fluke obstruction.

entities.name: Ascites With Shifting Dullness
entities.description: Demonstrable abdominal fluid shift and fluid wave indicating exudative eosinophilic ascites or secondary decompensation in biliary cirrhosis.

entities.name: Spiking High Fever
entities.description: High continuous or intermittent fevers reaching 39 to 40 degrees Celsius accompanied by shaking chills during acute fluke tissue invasion or cholangitis.

entities.name: Persistent Biliary Colic
entities.description: Unrelenting, severe right hypochondrial spasms and pain unresponsive to simple antispasmodics, caused by active fluke muscular contractions within bile ducts.

entities.name: Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Yellowish pigmentation of the sclerae detectable when serum total bilirubin exceeds 2.5 to 3.0 mg/dL due to biliary outflow obstruction.

entities.name: Excoriations From Pruritus
entities.description: Linear scratch marks and skin abrasions secondary to intense generalized pruritus provoked by circulating bile salts and parasite antigens.

entities.name: Peripheral Pitting Edema
entities.description: Bilateral lower extremity edema that pits on pressure, caused by marked hypoalbuminemia resulting from intestinal fluke malabsorption.

entities.name: Abdominal Distension
entities.description: Diffuse swelling of the abdomen with tympany or fluid waves resulting from paralytic ileus, bowel wall edema, or eosinophilic ascites.

entities.name: Cachectic Temporal Wasting
entities.description: Loss of bitemporal fat pads and prominent facial bone contours indicating advanced protein-calorie malnutrition in long-standing disease.

entities.name: Halitosis With Putrid Sputum
entities.description: Offensive, foul breath odor accompanying copious expectoration of necrotic brownish sputum from long-standing secondarily infected lung fluke cysts.

entities.name: Hyperactive Bowel Sounds
entities.description: Frequent, loud, high-pitched borborygmi heard throughout the abdomen reflecting intestinal hypermotility and mucosal irritation.

entities.name: Cervical Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlarged, firm, non-tender or mildly tender lymph nodes in the anterior and posterior cervical triangles responding to upper respiratory and pleural inflammation.

entities.name: Splenomegaly on Palpation
entities.description: Palpable enlargement of the spleen below the left costal margin secondary to reticuloendothelial hyperplasia or non-cirrhotic portal hypertension.

entities.name: Extreme Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Profound elevation of absolute eosinophil count (often >40-80% of differential, absolute count 10,000-35,000/uL), universal in acute invasive trematodiasis.

entities.name: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
entities.description: Marked elevation of serum alkaline phosphatase (ALP >3-5x ULN) reflecting intense chronic biliary epithelial irritation and cholestasis.

entities.name: Marked GGT Elevation
entities.description: Substantial rise in serum gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT >4-6x ULN) confirming biliary epithelial injury and cholestatic stress.

entities.name: Elevated Serum IgE
entities.description: Astronomical elevation of total serum immunoglobulin E (frequently >1,000-5,000 IU/mL) provoked by strong Th2 immune responses to fluke antigens.

entities.name: Direct Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Predominant elevation of conjugated bilirubin (direct bilirubin >2.0 mg/dL) reflecting mechanical bile duct occlusion by adult flukes or ductal strictures.

entities.name: Mild Transaminitis
entities.description: Mild to moderate elevations of serum AST and ALT (2-4x ULN) reflecting parenchymal hepatocellular necrosis during larval burrowing or secondary cholangitis.

entities.name: Marked Leukocytosis
entities.description: Elevated total white blood cell count (WBC 15,000-40,000/uL) driven primarily by massive absolute eosinophilia and reactive neutrophilia.

entities.name: Elevated C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: High serum CRP levels (>50-100 mg/L) indicating active acute-phase systemic inflammation during fluke tissue migration and secondary cholangitis.

entities.name: Elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
entities.description: Significantly accelerated ESR (>60-100 mm/hr) resulting from intense polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia and systemic inflammation.

entities.name: Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
entities.description: Decreased hemoglobin and hematocrit with low MCV and MCH resulting from chronic gastrointestinal blood loss, hemoptysis, or bone marrow suppression.

entities.name: Branching Subcapsular Hepatic Tracks
entities.description: Linear, branching, serpentine hypoechoic or hypodense parenchymal tunnels ('tunnels and burrows') on ultrasound and CT, pathognomonic of migrating Fasciola flukes.

entities.name: Peripheral Intrahepatic Ductal Dilation
entities.description: Diffuse, uniform, non-tapering dilation of peripheral intrahepatic bile ducts with normal extrahepatic ducts on ultrasound/CT, pathognomonic of clonorchiasis.

entities.name: Increased Periductal Echogenicity
entities.description: Thickened, brightly hyperechoic cuffs encircling intrahepatic bile ducts on abdominal ultrasound, representing periductal collagenous fibrosis.

entities.name: Mobile Gallbladder Sludge
entities.description: Floating, non-shadowing echogenic material within the gallbladder lumen that shifts with patient repositioning, representing living flukes and desquamated mucosa.

entities.name: Acalculous Biliary Sludge
entities.description: Accumulation of echogenic particulate matter in bile ducts without acoustic shadowing or true stone formation, causing mechanical ductal distension.

entities.name: Ring-Shadow Pulmonary Cavities
entities.description: Thin- or thick-walled round cystic lesions (1-3 cm) with surrounding ground-glass opacity on chest radiograph, pathognomonic of pulmonary paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Migratory Pulmonary Infiltrates
entities.description: Patchy, non-segmental alveolar consolidations and nodular opacities on serial chest X-rays that spontaneously shift anatomical location over weeks.

entities.name: Multilocular Soap-Bubble Brain Calcifications
entities.description: Clustered, round, calcified multilocular cystic lesions resembling soap bubbles on head CT, pathognomonic of chronic cerebral paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Exudative Eosinophilic Pleural Fluid
entities.description: Thoracentesis fluid demonstrating high protein, elevated LDH, and marked eosinophil predominance (>10-50% of nucleated cells) with Charcot-Leyden crystals.

entities.name: Pleural Fluid Low Glucose
entities.description: Markedly depressed glucose concentration (<10-60 mg/dL) in pleural effusion fluid resulting from intense local parasite metabolism and cellular turnover.

entities.name: Operculated Eggs in Sputum
entities.description: Golden-brown, thick-shelled operculated eggs measuring 80-120 um by 45-65 um with a prominent opercular rim, definitive on unstained sputum wet mounts.

entities.name: Pitcher-Shaped Operculated Stool Eggs
entities.description: Small, yellowish-brown operculated eggs measuring 25-35 um by 12-19 um with an expanded shoulder collar and tiny abopercular knob, diagnostic of Clonorchis/Opisthorchis.

entities.name: Large Unembryonated Operculated Eggs
entities.description: Large, golden-yellow unembryonated operculated eggs measuring 130-150 um by 65-90 um detected in feces or duodenal aspirate, diagnostic of Fasciola/Fasciolopsis.

entities.name: Positive Fasciola Coproantigen ELISA
entities.description: Detection of Fasciola excretory-secretory antigens in stool using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, positive weeks before microscopic egg shedding.

entities.name: Serum IgG Parasite Antibodies
entities.description: High titers of parasite-specific IgG antibodies detected by ELISA against excretory-secretory fluke antigens, highly sensitive during acute invasive disease.

entities.name: Charcot-Leyden Sputum Crystals
entities.description: Slender, hexagonal bipyramidal crystals derived from eosinophil lysophospholipase breakdown, abundant in sputum wet mounts.

entities.name: Subcapsular Hepatic Hypodense Clusters
entities.description: Clustered or branching hypodense lesions in the peripheral subcapsular liver parenchyma on contrast-enhanced abdominal CT during acute invasion.

entities.name: Normal Extrahepatic Bile Duct
entities.description: Preservation of normal common bile duct caliber (<6-7 mm) despite marked peripheral intrahepatic duct dilatation, characteristic of Clonorchis infection.

entities.name: Thickened Gallbladder Wall
entities.description: Diffuse gallbladder wall thickening (>3 mm) without gallstones on abdominal ultrasound, indicating chronic fluke cholecystitis.

entities.name: Pleural Thickening and Blunting
entities.description: Blunting of the costophrenic sulcus and pleural rind formation on chest radiography resulting from chronic Paragonimus pleurisy.

entities.name: Linear Tunnel Ultrasound Lesions
entities.description: Serpentine, branching hypoechoic linear parenchymal tracks visible on bedside liver ultrasound representing active mechanical larval burrows.

entities.name: Intracranial Ring-Enhancing Nodules
entities.description: Multiple round or conglomerate ring-enhancing granulomatous nodules with surrounding vasogenic edema on contrast brain MRI.

entities.name: Periventricular White Matter Edema
entities.description: Extensive hyperintense T2/FLAIR signal abnormalities in periventricular white matter surrounding cerebral fluke lesions.

entities.name: Eosinophilic Ascitic Fluid
entities.description: Paracentesis revealing peritoneal exudate with marked eosinophilia (>10-40% of leukocytes) during acute peritoneal migration.

entities.name: Serum Amylase and Lipase
entities.description: Acute elevations of serum pancreatic enzymes (amylase and lipase >3x ULN) resulting from fluke impaction at the pancreatic ampullary sphincter.

entities.name: Hypoalbuminemia
entities.description: Severe depression of serum albumin (<2.5-3.0 g/dL) resulting from mucosal ulceration, lymphatic weeping, and protein-losing enteropathy.

entities.name: Elevated CA19-9 Tumor Marker
entities.description: Marked elevation of serum carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (>100-1,000 U/mL) in patients with liver fluke-associated cholangiocarcinoma.

entities.name: Kato-Katz Microscopic Stool Smear
entities.description: Standard quantitative parasitological thick smear revealing characteristic operculated eggs per gram of feces for disease staging.

entities.name: Raw Freshwater Cyprinid Fish
entities.description: Dietary ingestion of raw, pickled, fermented, or undercooked freshwater carp or cyprinid fish harboring encysted metacercariae of Clonorchis sinensis or Opisthorchis species.

entities.name: Raw Freshwater Crustaceans
entities.description: Consumption of raw, undercooked, salted, wine-soaked, or marinated freshwater river crabs or crayfish harboring encysted Paragonimus metacercariae.

entities.name: Raw Watercress Ingestion
entities.description: Ingestion of unwashed wild aquatic watercress (Nasturtium officinale) harboring encysted Fasciola metacercariae attached to stems and leaves.

entities.name: Raw Water Spinach Ingestion
entities.description: Consumption of raw, unwashed aquatic plants such as water spinach, water caltrops, or water chestnuts bearing Fasciola or Fasciolopsis metacercariae.

entities.name: Untreated Surface Grazing Water
entities.description: Drinking unboiled surface water or canal water in pastoral areas contaminated with floating Fasciola metacercariae detached from vegetation.

entities.name: Raw Paratenic Wild Boar
entities.description: Consumption of raw or undercooked meat from paratenic mammalian hosts such as wild boars that harbor viable Paragonimus juvenile larvae in muscle tissue.

entities.name: Freshwater Aquatic Snail Habitats
entities.description: Proximity to freshwater bodies harboring specific hydrobiid, bithyniid, or lymnaeid snails serving as mandatory first intermediate hosts.

entities.name: Endemic East Asian Residence
entities.description: Residence in or travel to highly endemic foci of Clonorchis sinensis in China, South Korea, northern Vietnam, and far eastern Russia.

entities.name: Lower Mekong Basin Resident
entities.description: Residence along the Mekong river basin in northeast Thailand, Laos, or Cambodia with hyperendemic Opisthorchis viverrini transmission.

entities.name: Andean Highlands Pastoralist
entities.description: Inhabitants of high-altitude pastoral valleys in Bolivia and Peru where human fascioliasis hyperendemicity reaches up to 70% in school-age children.

entities.name: Sheep and Cattle Husbandry
entities.description: Occupational engagement in raising ruminant livestock (sheep, goats, cattle) that serve as primary definitive reservoir hosts for Fasciola hepatica.

entities.name: Consumption of Thai Koi-Pla
entities.description: Traditional cultural consumption of raw, spiced freshwater fish salad (koi pla) in northeast Thailand, driving intense Opisthorchis transmission.

entities.name: Chinese Drunken Crab Dishes
entities.description: Traditional culinary ingestion of live freshwater river crabs steeped in rice wine or brine without thermal cooking, harboring Paragonimus metacercariae.

entities.name: Fish-Eating Carnivore Reservoir
entities.description: Sympatric populations of wild carnivores (otters, badgers, minks) maintaining zoonotic transmission cycles of liver and lung flukes.

entities.name: Canine and Feline Reservoirs
entities.description: Domestic dogs and cats that consume raw fish and crab waste, shedding viable trematode eggs into community waterways.

entities.name: Freshwater Aquaculture Workers
entities.description: Fish farmers and fish processing workers handling untreated freshwater aquaculture ponds fertilized with untreated human or animal manure.

entities.name: Acute Fascioliasis Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation timeline of 1 to 6 weeks post-ingestion before acute hepatic migration symptoms emerge, followed by patency at 3 to 4 months.

entities.name: Chronic Clonorchiasis Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation period of 3 to 4 weeks to egg patency, with clinical cholangiopathy and carcinogenesis evolving insidiously over 10 to 30 years.

entities.name: Paragonimiasis Incubation Period
entities.description: Incubation latency of 2 to 12 weeks from raw crustacean ingestion to pulmonary cyst formation, with adult worms surviving up to 20 years.

entities.name: Inadequate Food Thermal Processing
entities.description: Culinary practices utilizing smoking, pickling, salting, or drying without boiling or thorough cooking, failing to inactivate encysted metacercariae.

entities.name: Substandard Agricultural Sanitation
entities.description: Use of night soil (untreated human feces) as fertilizer in freshwater fish ponds and aquatic vegetable patches, perpetuating transmission.

entities.name: Raw Wild Vegetable Foraging
entities.description: Foraging and consuming wild freshwater greens, marsh grasses, or wild watercress from pastures grazed by livestock.

entities.name: Absent Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Normal peripheral blood eosinophil count (<3% or <500/uL) during an acute febrile hepatic or pulmonary illness, strongly excluding acute fluke invasion.

entities.name: Zero Dietary Freshwater Exposure
entities.description: Complete lifelong absence of consumption of raw or undercooked freshwater fish, crustaceans, aquatic vegetables, or unboiled grazing surface water.

entities.name: Acute Rice-Water Watery Diarrhea
entities.description: Profuse, voluminous, non-inflammatory secretory watery diarrhea without eosinophilia, characteristic of Vibrio cholerae.

entities.name: High Procalcitonin Sepsis Syndrome
entities.description: Hyperacute septic shock with procalcitonin >10 ng/mL and prominent neutrophilic left shift without eosinophilia, indicating fulminant bacterial sepsis.

entities.name: Massive Acid-Fast Bacilli Smear
entities.description: Strongly positive sputum smear for acid-fast bacilli (3+ or 4+ AFB) or positive GeneXpert MTB/RIF in a patient with cavitary lung disease.

entities.name: Rapid Response to Ceftriaxone
entities.description: Prompt clinical defervescence and complete resolution of hepatic or pulmonary infiltrates within 48 to 72 hours of starting third-generation cephalosporins.

entities.name: Solitary Liquefactive Amebic Cavity
entities.description: Demonstration of a solitary large round liquefactive hepatic cavity with anchovy-paste aspirate and positive Entamoeba histolytica serology.

entities.name: Normal Serum Alkaline Phosphatase
entities.description: Completely normal serum alkaline phosphatase and GGT in a patient with suspected long-standing chronic liver fluke infection.

entities.name: Acalculous Cholecystectomy Cure
entities.description: Complete curative resolution of biliary pain following cholecystectomy with pathology showing uncomplicated acalculous cholecystitis devoid of flukes or eggs.

entities.name: Strict Urban Cooked Diet
entities.description: Strict dietary adherence to thoroughly boiled, commercially prepared food without any raw freshwater products in a non-endemic metropolis.

entities.name: Pure Segmental Pneumonic Consolidation
entities.description: Dense, homogeneous lobar or segmental consolidation with air bronchograms resolving rapidly on ampicillin-sulbactam.

entities.name: Non-Eosinophilic Sputum Purulence
entities.description: Expectoration of yellow-green purulent sputum containing exclusively degenerate neutrophils and bacterial cocci without Charcot-Leyden crystals or eggs.

entities.name: Negative Clonorchis Coproantigen Test
entities.description: Repeatedly negative enzyme immunoassay for Clonorchis or Opisthorchis coproantigen alongside negative concentrated stool egg examinations.

entities.name: Zero Hepatic Parenchymal Lesions
entities.description: Completely normal triphasic contrast abdominal CT and ultrasound showing pristine liver parenchyma without tunnels, burrows, or ductal dilatation.

entities.name: High-Grade Neutrophilic Leukemoid Reaction
entities.description: WBC >35,000/uL with >90% toxic granulated neutrophils and zero eosinophils, indicating severe pyogenic bacterial infection or leukemoid reaction.

entities.name: Rapid Defervescence on Chloroquine
entities.description: Complete defervescence and parasite clearance within 24 to 48 hours of starting antimalarial therapy, confirming Plasmodium infection.

entities.name: Absence of Snail Habitats
entities.description: Lifelong residence in arid desert or alpine environments lacking freshwater snail intermediate hosts and aquatic food chains.

entities.name: Isolated Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Elevated total bilirubin with normal direct fraction (<15%), normal ALP, normal GGT, and normal transaminases, indicating Gilbert syndrome or hemolysis.

entities.name: Persistent Symptoms After Triclabendazole
entities.description: Lack of clinical, radiologic, or eosinophilic improvement after two adequate weight-based doses of triclabendazole in a patient suspected of fascioliasis.

entities.name: Normal Total Serum IgE
entities.description: Serum total IgE levels strictly within normal baseline reference limits (<20-50 IU/mL) during acute invasive multi-organ symptoms.

entities.name: Hyperacute Neurological Coma
entities.description: Sudden catastrophic loss of consciousness within minutes to hours without antecedent headaches or pulmonary symptoms, indicating acute thromboembolism.

entities.name: Negative Parasite Wet Mount
entities.description: Repeatedly negative direct microscopic wet mounts and formal concentration exams of sputum and stool in a patient with chronic respiratory complaints.

entities.name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
entities.description: Chronic granulomatous mycobacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, presenting with cough, fever, cavitations, and hemoptysis.

entities.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Suppurative hepatic cavity caused by Entamoeba histolytica presenting with right upper quadrant pain, high fever, and liquefactive necrosis.

entities.name: Choledocholithiasis
entities.description: Calculus obstruction of the common bile duct causing biliary colic, jaundice, and potential ascending cholangitis.

entities.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
entities.description: Hepatotropic viral infection (HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV) causing diffuse hepatocellular necrosis, profound transaminitis, and jaundice.

entities.name: Schistosomiasis
entities.description: Waterborne blood fluke infection acquired via percutaneous penetration of cercariae, causing urogenital or intestinal/hepatosplenic disease.

entities.name: Pyogenic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Bacterial collection in hepatic parenchyma causing fever, septic leukocytosis, and right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness.

entities.name: Echinococcosis
entities.description: Larval cestode infection caused by Echinococcus granulosus or multilocularis forming well-defined hydatid cysts in the liver and lungs.

entities.name: Ascariasis
entities.description: Large intestinal nematode infection caused by Ascaris lumbricoides, with larvae migrating through lungs and adult worms invading bile ducts.

entities.name: Bacterial Cholangitis
entities.description: Acute infection of the biliary conduits classically manifesting as Charcot triad (RUQ pain, jaundice, fever) and septic shock.

entities.name: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
entities.description: Chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive inflammation and obliterative fibrosis of intra- and extrahepatic bile ducts.

entities.name: Neurocysticercosis
entities.description: Central nervous system infection caused by the larval stage of the pork tapeworm Taenia solium, causing seizures and cystic brain lesions.

entities.name: Lung Adenocarcinoma
entities.description: Primary malignant epithelial tumor of the lung arising from bronchial mucous glands, presenting with cough, hemoptysis, and peripheral nodules.

entities.name: Celiac Disease
entities.description: Autoimmune enteropathy triggered by dietary gluten ingestion leading to villous atrophy, chronic diarrhea, and malabsorption.

entities.name: Strongyloidiasis
entities.description: Intestinal nematode infection caused by Strongyloides stercoralis capable of autoinfection and persistent larval cutaneous migration.

entities.name: Loeffler Syndrome
entities.description: Transient pulmonary eosinophilia caused by transpulmonary larval migration of nematodes such as Ascaris or hookworms.

entities.name: Hepatocellular Carcinoma
entities.description: Primary malignancy of hepatocytes arising almost exclusively in the setting of chronic cirrhosis, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection presenting with biphasic high fever, conjunctival suffusion, acute kidney injury, and jaundice (Weil disease).

entities.name: Chronic Pancreatitis
entities.description: Progressive fibro-inflammatory disease of the pancreas causing permanent morphological damage, pain, and loss of exocrine/endocrine function.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, biliary tract
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as recurrent biliary colic caused by adult Fasciola or Clonorchis worms mechanically occluding intrahepatic bile ducts and the common bile duct.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, invasive fascioliasis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as acute invasive fascioliasis characterized by high spiking fever, severe right upper quadrant pain, tender hepatomegaly, urticaria, and profound peripheral eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, biliary fascioliasis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as chronic biliary fascioliasis presenting with intermittent right upper quadrant abdominal pain, obstructive jaundice, recurrent cholangitis, and biliary ductal fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, cholangitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as recurrent pyogenic cholangitis due to chronic mechanical obstruction by adult liver flukes, dead parasite debris, and secondary ascending enteric bacterial infections.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, oncogenesis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as cholangiocarcinoma arising from persistent chronic periductal inflammation, parasite excretory-secretory mitogens like granulin, and biliary epithelial hyperplasia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, pulmonary parenchyma
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as pulmonary paragonimiasis presenting with chronic indolent productive cough, pleuritic chest pain, and recurrent hemoptysis mimicking tuberculosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, respiratory hallmark
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as chocolate-sauce sputum hemoptysis resulting from the rupture of subcortical pulmonary fluke cysts into adjacent bronchioles.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, central nervous system
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as cerebral paragonimiasis producing chronic focal epilepsy, intracranial hypertension, visual defects, and clustered intracranial cystic lesions.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, gallbladder
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as acalculous cholecystitis when juvenile or adult Fasciola or Clonorchis flukes invade the gallbladder lumen causing secondary chemical and bacterial inflammation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, hepatic fibrosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as secondary biliary cirrhosis following decades of uneradicated Clonorchis or Fasciola colonization and recurrent ascending cholangiohepatitis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, biliary stricture
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as biliary ductal strictures that obstruct normal bile drainage and promote recurrent pyogenic cholangiohepatitis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, intrahepatic bile ducts
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as intrahepatic ductal ectasia characteristically involving the peripheral liver parenchyma while sparing extrahepatic ducts in chronic clonorchiasis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, mechanical obstruction
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as mechanical biliary obstruction when high worm burdens of Fasciola or Clonorchis physically occlude bile conduits.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, respiratory tract
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as chronic productive cough frequently accompanied by copious gelatinous expectoration in pulmonary paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, pleurisy
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as pleuritic chest pain reflecting pleural inflammation, mechanical parietal peritoneal perforation, or subpleural cyst erosion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, pleural effusion
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as parasitic pleural effusion that is often unilateral, exudative, and characterized by low glucose and prominent eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, pneumothorax
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as spontaneous pneumothorax or hydropneumothorax due to transmural cavitation and cystic perforation of the lung surface.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, ectopic migration
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as extrapulmonary ectopic paragonimiasis when migrating juvenile flukes deviate into somatic tissues and viscera.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, cutaneous manifestation
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as subcutaneous migratory nodules in both ectopic fascioliasis and ectopic paragonimiasis as worms track through fascial planes.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, ectopic liver involvement
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as ectopic hepatic migration causing transient right upper quadrant pain, transaminitis, and subcapsular inflammatory nodules.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, intestinal tract
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as intestinal fasciolopsiasis causing localized mucosal ulcerations, persistent abdominal pain, and intestinal malabsorption.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, gastrointestinal
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as chronic mucous diarrhea accompanied by abdominal cramping, tenesmus, and nutrient wasting in heavy intestinal fluke infections.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, malabsorption
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as protein-losing enteropathy in children with heavy Fasciolopsis buski burdens, causing severe hypoalbuminemia and anasarca.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, periductal fibrosis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as periductal fibrosis surrounding medium and small intrahepatic bile ducts in chronic clonorchiasis and opisthorchiasis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, adenomatous hyperplasia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as biliary epithelial hyperplasia, an essential precancerous lesion promoting malignant transformation to cholangiocarcinoma.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, bacterial superinfection
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as suppurative bacterial cholangitis with toxic bacteremia, high fever, chills, and purulent biliary stasis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, parenchymal destruction
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as hepatic parenchymal burrows during acute fascioliasis, eliciting intense localized eosinophilic necrosis and microabscesses.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, capsular perforation
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as Glisson capsule perforation causing acute localized peritoneal irritation, subcapsular hematoma, and right upper quadrant guarding.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, neurological
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as adult-onset parasitic epilepsy in patients with cerebral paragonimiasis as cortical fluke granulomas trigger epileptogenic foci.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, intracranial mass
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as intracranial space-occupying lesions causing progressive morning headaches, projectile vomiting, and papilledema.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, cerebrovascular
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as intracerebral hemorrhage or subarachnoid hemorrhage due to mechanical vascular injury from migrating Paragonimus flukes.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, cardiac embolization
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as heterophyid cardiac embolization when tiny intestinal fluke eggs enter mesenteric venules, leading to heart failure and arrhythmias.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, spinal cord
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as spinal cord paragonimiasis causing sensory levels, lower extremity weakness, and progressive spastic paraparesis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, peritoneal cavity
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as eosinophilic peritonitis during the early invasive phase of acute fascioliasis, with peritoneal signs and eosinophilic ascites.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, hepatic hematoma
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as hepatic subcapsular hematoma during acute fascioliasis, occasionally culminating in spontaneous hemoperitoneum.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, cholecystitis mimic
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as an acute cholecystitis mimic when flukes occlude the cystic duct, prompting urgent surgical consults for acalculous inflammation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, pancreatitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as recurrent pancreatitis when adult Clonorchis, Opisthorchis, or Fasciola flukes temporarily obstruct the pancreatic duct orifice.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, hepatic microabscesses
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as biliary microabscesses surrounding chronically parasitized bile ducts in severe clonorchiasis and opisthorchiasis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, cachexia
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as chronic cachexia in advanced liver fluke or giant intestinal fluke infections with protracted catabolic states.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, clinical manifestation, anasarca
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as severe anasarca in pediatric patients suffering from heavy Fasciolopsis buski-induced protein-losing enteropathy.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, respiratory hallmark
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Foodborne trematodiasis features rusty sputum expectoration as a pathognomonic hallmark distinguishing active pulmonary paragonimiasis from other chronic lung infections.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal palpation, hepatomegaly
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits tender hepatomegaly during acute invasive fascioliasis and recurrent pyogenic cholangitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal exam, right upper quadrant
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates right upper quadrant tenderness with voluntary guarding during acute hepatic migration and acute cholangitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam, jaundice
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis presents with intermittent jaundice as living flukes temporarily occlude and clear biliary channels.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, dermatological sign, urticaria
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis presents with an acute urticarial allergic rash during the early invasive parenchymal migration phase of Fasciola flukes.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam, angioedema
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis displays facial angioedema in acute invasive fascioliasis alongside high spiking fevers and urticaria.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, pulmonary auscultation, rales
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates crepitant pulmonary rales upon chest auscultation in patients with active pulmonary paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, chest exam, breath sounds
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates decreased breath sounds unilaterally over the lung base in patients with Paragonimus pleural effusions.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, chest percussion, pleural fluid
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis produces dullness to percussion over the posterior lung bases in pleural paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, auscultation, pleural rub
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis generates a pleural friction rub during active larval crossing of parietal and visceral pleura in early paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, smoking gun, ectopic hallmark
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Foodborne trematodiasis features subcutaneous crepitant swellings as a pathognomonic physical hallmark of aberrantly migrating flukes in superficial fascia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, neurological exam, focal deficit
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates focal neurological deficits in patients presenting with cerebral paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, fundoscopic exam, papilledema
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis presents with papilledema on fundoscopy in patients suffering from intracranial mass effects of cerebral paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, neurological exam, meningismus
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits meningismus and photophobia when Paragonimus larvae transit into the subarachnoid space or rupture cysts.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal palpation, epigastric mass
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis presents with a tender epigastric mass during severe invasive fascioliasis with subcapsular inflammatory conglomeration.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal exam, gallbladder distension
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis produces a palpable distended gallbladder when living flukes or cholangiocarcinoma obstruct the distal biliary conduit.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal exam, ascites
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates ascites with shifting dullness during acute eosinophilic peritonitis or late secondary biliary cirrhosis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, vital signs, pyrexia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as spiking high fever during acute invasive fascioliasis and during acute episodes of ascending pyogenic cholangitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, clinical examination, biliary colic
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis presents with persistent biliary colic as flukes migrate through the ampullary sphincter and irritate ductal mechanoreceptors.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, physical exam, icterus
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits prominent scleral icterus during acute obstructive episodes in chronic clonorchiasis and fascioliasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, skin examination, pruritus
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis displays excoriations from pruritus on the trunk and limbs due to severe cholestatic pruritus and systemic allergic responses.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, extremity exam, pitting edema
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits peripheral pitting edema in heavy intestinal fasciolopsiasis with extensive protein-losing enteropathy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal exam, distension
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis manifests as marked abdominal distension in children with heavy intestinal fluke colonization and mucosal edema.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, nutritional exam, cachexia
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits cachectic temporal wasting in chronic neglected clonorchiasis, opisthorchiasis, or cholangiocarcinoma.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, clinical examination, putrid sputum
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis produces halitosis with putrid sputum when pulmonary Paragonimus cavities develop secondary anaerobic bacterial colonization.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal auscultation, bowel sounds
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates hyperactive bowel sounds in active intestinal fluke infections caused by Fasciolopsis buski.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, lymphatic exam, lymphadenopathy
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis presents with reactive cervical lymphadenopathy in children and young adults with active pulmonary paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN, abdominal palpation, splenomegaly
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates splenomegaly on palpation in chronic liver fluke cases that develop secondary biliary cirrhosis and portal hypertension.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, CBC, eosinophilia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits extreme peripheral eosinophilia (>40-80% differential) as the single most striking triage laboratory marker in acute fascioliasis and active paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, liver function, ALP
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits elevated alkaline phosphatase indicating chronic mechanical irritation of intrahepatic biliary ducts by resident liver flukes.

relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits marked GGT elevation in chronic clonorchiasis and opisthorchiasis, serving as a sensitive marker of fluke-induced cholangiopathy.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, immunology, IgE
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits elevated serum IgE levels reflecting robust systemic allergic and anti-helminthic immune activation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, bilirubin, cholestasis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits direct hyperbilirubinemia during acute obstructive biliary episodes in Clonorchis or Fasciola infections.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, transaminases, AST ALT
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits mild transaminitis during juvenile Fasciola migration through the liver parenchyma.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, CBC, leukocytosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits marked leukocytosis accompanying severe acute invasive fascioliasis and active pulmonary paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, inflammatory marker, CRP
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits elevated C-reactive protein during the acute invasive hepatic phase and bacterial cholangitis superinfections.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, inflammatory marker, ESR
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate in active fascioliasis and chronic paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, anemia, CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits microcytic hypochromic anemia in severe intestinal fasciolopsiasis and chronic pulmonary paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, CT, hepatic tunnels
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates branching subcapsular hepatic tracks on abdominal CT and ultrasound as a pathognomonic hallmark of acute invasive fascioliasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, CT, ductal dilation
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates peripheral intrahepatic ductal dilation on ultrasound and CT reflecting selective distal biliary colonization by Clonorchis sinensis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, periductal cuffing
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates increased periductal echogenicity on ultrasound as a distinctive sign of chronic Clonorchis-induced periductal fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, gallbladder sludge
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates mobile gallbladder sludge without acoustic shadowing on ultrasound during chronic Fasciola gallbladder colonization.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, acalculous sludge
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates acalculous biliary sludge on bedside POCUS ultrasound in acute obstructive fluke episodes.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, chest X-ray, pulmonary cavity
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates ring-shadow pulmonary cavities on chest radiography representing mature encapsulated Paragonimus fluke cysts.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, chest radiograph, migratory infiltrates
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates migratory pulmonary infiltrates reflecting ongoing parenchymal tracking of juvenile lung flukes before final encapsulation.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, head CT, soap-bubble appearance
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates multilocular soap-bubble brain calcifications on head CT as a pathognomonic neuroimaging hallmark of cerebral paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, thoracentesis, pleural fluid analysis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits exudative eosinophilic pleural fluid on thoracentesis in patients with Paragonimus-induced pleurisy.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, pleural fluid, glucose depletion
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits pleural fluid low glucose on admission pleural analysis, a characteristic feature of Paragonimus pleural exudates.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, sputum microscopy, operculated eggs
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits operculated eggs in sputum wet mounts providing definitive microbiological proof of active pulmonary paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, stool microscopy, Clonorchis eggs
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits pitcher-shaped operculated stool eggs on Kato-Katz smear, confirming patency in clonorchiasis and opisthorchiasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, stool microscopy, Fasciola eggs
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits large unembryonated operculated eggs on stool sedimentation examination in patent chronic biliary fascioliasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, coproantigen ELISA, early diagnosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits a positive Fasciola coproantigen ELISA, enabling early diagnostic confirmation during the pre-patent invasive phase.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, serology, IgG ELISA
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits serum IgG parasite antibodies on admission serology, securing the diagnosis when stool or sputum egg shedding is absent.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, sputum cytology, Charcot-Leyden
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits Charcot-Leyden sputum crystals upon cytological smear evaluation in patients with pulmonary paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, contrast CT, subcapsular lesions
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates subcapsular hepatic hypodense clusters on contrast abdominal CT representing focal necrosis from penetrating Fasciola flukes.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, normal CBD caliber
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates a normal extrahepatic bile duct on ultrasound while peripheral intrahepatic ducts are extensively dilated in clonorchiasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, gallbladder wall thickening
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates a thickened gallbladder wall on POCUS ultrasound in chronic biliary fascioliasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, chest radiograph, pleural thickening
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates pleural thickening and blunting on chest radiography in patients with resolved or chronic pleural paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, ultrasound, linear burrows
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates linear tunnel ultrasound lesions in the liver parenchyma during acute Fasciola migration.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, brain MRI, ring-enhancing lesions
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates intracranial ring-enhancing nodules on contrast-enhanced brain MRI in active cerebral paragonimiasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING, brain MRI, vasogenic edema
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Foodborne trematodiasis demonstrates periventricular white matter edema on brain MRI reflecting severe surrounding neuroinflammation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, paracentesis, eosinophilic ascites
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits eosinophilic ascitic fluid upon peritoneal tap analysis in acute invasive fascioliasis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, amylase lipase, pancreatitis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits elevated serum amylase and lipase during acute fluke-induced obstructive pancreatitis episodes.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, admission lab, albumin, malnutrition
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits severe hypoalbuminemia in heavy Fasciolopsis buski infection and advanced biliary cirrhosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, tumor marker, CA19-9, cholangiocarcinoma
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits an elevated CA19-9 tumor marker when chronic Clonorchis or Opisthorchis infection progresses to cholangiocarcinoma.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, parasitology, Kato-Katz smear
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits characteristic fluke eggs on Kato-Katz microscopic stool smear, confirming patent hepatobiliary or intestinal infection.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, dietary risk, freshwater fish, metacercariae
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to raw freshwater cyprinid fish contaminated with infectious metacercariae of Clonorchis or Opisthorchis.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, dietary risk, crustaceans, Paragonimus
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to raw freshwater crustaceans containing viable Paragonimus metacercariae.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, dietary risk, aquatic plants, watercress
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to raw watercress ingestion harvested from livestock-grazing wetland habitats.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, dietary risk, aquatic vegetables
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to raw water spinach ingestion contaminated with encysted trematode metacercariae.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, waterborne risk, surface water
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to untreated surface grazing water in livestock farming regions.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, paratenic host, wild game meat
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to raw paratenic wild boar meat harboring transmissible juvenile Paragonimus flukes.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental risk, intermediate snail host
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis requires ecological exposure to freshwater aquatic snail habitats where cercariae develop and shed.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, geography, East Asia, Clonorchis
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Foodborne trematodiasis identifies endemic East Asian residence as a high-risk host profile for chronic clonorchiasis and cholangiocarcinoma.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, geography, Mekong basin, Opisthorchis
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Foodborne trematodiasis designates lower Mekong basin resident populations as high-risk hosts where Opisthorchis prevalence exceeds 50-80%.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, geography, Andes, Fasciola
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Foodborne trematodiasis designates Andean highlands pastoralist communities as high-risk hosts for hyperendemic childhood fascioliasis.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, occupation, pastoral livestock
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Foodborne trematodiasis designates individuals engaged in sheep and cattle husbandry as high-risk hosts for occupational fascioliasis.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, dietary practice, koi pla, Opisthorchis
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to consumption of Thai koi-pla containing viable Opisthorchis metacercariae.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, culinary exposure, drunken crab, Paragonimus
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to Chinese drunken crab dishes transmitting viable Paragonimus metacercariae.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, animal reservoir, wild carnivores
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Foodborne trematodiasis involves a fish-eating carnivore reservoir maintaining sylvatic transmission cycles independent of human control.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, domestic reservoir, dogs cats
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Foodborne trematodiasis involves domestic canine and feline reservoirs that perpetuate environmental contamination in endemic villages.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, occupation, aquaculture
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Foodborne trematodiasis designates freshwater aquaculture workers as high-risk hosts due to frequent occupational contact with contaminated ponds.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, disease latency, fascioliasis timeline
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits an acute fascioliasis incubation period of 1 to 6 weeks for acute parenchymal migration, reaching egg patency at 3 to 4 months.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, incubation timeline, clonorchiasis latency
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits a chronic clonorchiasis incubation period of 3 to 4 weeks until stool egg shedding, with severe chronic disease emerging over decades.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD, incubation timeline, paragonimiasis
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Foodborne trematodiasis exhibits a paragonimiasis incubation period of 2 to 12 weeks for pulmonary cyst maturation, persisting for decades if untreated.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, food safety, inadequate cooking
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to inadequate food thermal processing that leaves metacercariae fully infectious.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, environmental hygiene, night soil
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is promoted by exposure to substandard agricultural sanitation where untreated feces enter snail-inhabited waters.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, foraging, wild aquatic plants
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Foodborne trematodiasis is acquired via exposure to raw wild vegetable foraging in wetlands adjacent to livestock herds.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, normal eosinophils
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Foodborne trematodiasis is ruled out by absent peripheral eosinophilia during acute febrile right upper quadrant pain or hemoptysis, as invasive trematodes provoke universal marked eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, zero dietary exposure
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Foodborne trematodiasis is ruled out by zero dietary freshwater exposure, as humans can only contract these parasites by ingesting encysted metacercariae.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, secretory diarrhea
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Foodborne trematodiasis is ruled out by acute rice-water watery diarrhea with severe dehydration, which confirms acute secretory cholera rather than fluke disease.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, bacterial sepsis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Foodborne trematodiasis is ruled out by a high procalcitonin sepsis syndrome without antecedent biliary symptoms or eosinophilia, pointing to primary bacterial bloodstream infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusion criterion, acid-fast bacilli, TB
