relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets individuals with Down syndrome as a recognized high-risk host demographic for crusted scabies, attributed to intrinsic abnormalities in cutaneous T-cell immunity, xerotic skin barrier changes, and altered sensory awareness.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, severe dementia, Alzheimer disease, cognitive impairment, lack of itch reporting
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets elderly patients with severe dementia as a high-risk host population, because impaired cognitive awareness prevents patients from recognizing or reporting pruritus, allowing unchecked mite proliferation and unnoticed institutional spread.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, bedridden debilitated patients, physical disability, stroke, immobility, grooming failure
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets bedridden debilitated patients with stroke, spinal injury, or severe neuromuscular weakness, who cannot physically scratch or groom themselves to mechanically dislodge mites, leading to extensive hyperkeratotic plaques.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, pediatric age under 2, infants, neonates, immature skin barrier, severe disease
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets infants of pediatric age under two years as a uniquely susceptible host group with thin stratum corneum and immature cellular immunity, resulting in widespread acral and cephalic lesions and high secondary infection risk.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, elderly care residents, nursing home seniors, immunosenescence, outbreak epicenter
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Scabies targets elderly care residents in assisted living facilities as a high-risk host demographic characterized by immunosenescence, fragile skin barriers, and frequent caregiver physical contact.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO, household cluster itch, family contacts, nocturnal pruritus in family, epidemiologic anchor
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Scabies is confirmed by exposure to household cluster itch, where history of identical severe nocturnal pruritus or typical papular rashes in close domestic contacts or bed partners provides a definitive epidemiologic anchor (2020 IACS Level B3).

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, total absence of pruritus, no itching, non-pruritic rash, immunocompetent host
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by the total absence of pruritus in an alert, immunocompetent adolescent or adult host, as delayed-type hypersensitivity to mite proteins almost universally generates severe, distressing itch.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, adult facial involvement, facial and scalp rash, adult cephalic sparing, exclusion rule
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by adult facial involvement and scalp eruption in an immunocompetent adult, because the adult Circle of Hebra strictly spares the head, neck, face, and scalp (unlike infantile scabies).

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, sparing of finger webs, clear web spaces, interdigital sparing, negative boundary
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by complete sparing of finger webs and interdigital spaces in a patient presenting with generalized diffuse pruritic excoriations, which makes common scabies extraordinarily improbable.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, sparing of flexor wrists, clear volar wrists, absence of wrist lesions, negative boundary
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by total sparing of flexor wrists and volar wrist skin creases in a patient with a widespread pruritic symmetrical eruption, strongly pointing toward alternative inflammatory dermatoses.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, high fever at onset, acute pyrexia, chills and rigors, absence of pyoderma
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated primary scabies is ruled out by high fever at onset (>38.5 C) accompanied by chills and rigors in the absence of obvious secondary bacterial pyoderma, cellulitis, or bacteremia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, systemic toxicity at onset, acute prostration, hemodynamic instability, non-superinfected host
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated scabies is ruled out by acute systemic toxicity at onset, including hypotension, altered mental status, and prostration, which indicates invasive sepsis, toxic shock, or an alternative systemic infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, non-pruritic palmoplantar macules, copper-red spots, painless palms and soles, secondary syphilis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by non-pruritic palmoplantar macules, presenting as painless, copper-red or ham-colored macules on the palms and soles with generalized lymphadenopathy, which pathognomonically defines secondary syphilis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, isolated extensor plaque sparing, extensor knees and elbows, sparing flexures, psoriasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by isolated extensor plaque distribution with complete sparing of flexural creases, web spaces, and genitalia, which strongly indicates plaque psoriasis rather than an ectoparasitic infestation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, Auspitz sign positivity, punctate bleeding, silvery scale removal, plaque psoriasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Crusted scabies is ruled out by Auspitz sign positivity, where mechanical scraping of a thick silvery scale reveals pinpoint bleeding points from elongated dermal papillae without a single mite on microscopy, confirming psoriasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusive sun-exposed distribution, photo-distributed rash, sparing covered skin, photodermatitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by an exclusive sun-exposed distribution, where a pruritic eruption is strictly confined to the face, V of the neck, and dorsal forearms with complete sparing of clothed areas, indicating photodermatosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, pure mucosal ulceration, oral aphthae, genital mucous erosions, non-epidermal involvement
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by pure mucosal ulceration involving oral or genital mucous membranes without epidermal burrows, papules, or web-space lesions, as Sarcoptes mites cannot burrow into non-cornified mucous membranes.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, targetoid iris lesions, concentric rings, three-zone targets, erythema multiforme
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by classic targetoid iris lesions consisting of three concentric concentric color zones with central dusky purpura, which definitively characterizes erythema multiforme.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, flaccid bullae with Nikolsky, positive Nikolsky sign, intraepidermal acantholysis, pemphigus
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by flaccid bullae with positive Nikolsky sign (epidermal sheet detachment upon lateral mechanical pressure), indicating intraepidermal acantholytic disease such as pemphigus vulgaris rather than scabies.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, rapid day-one rash resolution, evanescent lesions, resolution under 24 hours, allergic urticaria
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Active scabies is ruled out by rapid day-one rash resolution, where individual pruritic lesions spontaneously resolve completely within 24 hours without scabicidal therapy, identifying evanescent acute urticaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, lack of household itch, chronic solitary pruritus, zero transmission to bed partner, chronic pruritus
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by lack of household itch in the context of chronic severe nocturnal pruritus persisting for more than 1 to 2 years with zero transmission to sleeping partners or family members.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal serum IgE Norwegian, normal IgE, normal eosinophils, pseudo-crusted lesion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Suspected crusted (Norwegian) scabies is ruled out by normal serum IgE and normal eosinophil counts in a patient with extensive psoriasiform hyperkeratotic crusts, as true crusted scabies drives massive IgE and eosinophil surges.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, ceftriaxone monotherapy response, cephalosporin clearance, antibiotic rash cure, bacterial mimic
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Primary scabies is ruled out by prompt cure on ceftriaxone monotherapy, where the entire pruritic eruption clears completely on standard cephalosporins without topical or oral scabicides, proving an exclusive bacterial etiology.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, burrow and mite absence, negative serial scrapings, negative dermoscopy, high pretest certainty
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by definitive burrow and mite absence on serial high-resolution videodermoscopy and multiple deep mineral oil scrapings performed by expert dermatologists across multiple typical anatomical sites.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, wheals resolving under 24h, transient edematous plaques, evanescent hives, urticaria
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by transient pruritic edematous wheals resolving under 24 hours without residual epidermal scaling or excoriations, characteristic of common urticaria rather than an intraepidermal mite infestation.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, exclusive scalp folliculitis, follicular pustules, head-only lesions, bacterial folliculitis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Classical scabies is ruled out by exclusive scalp folliculitis where inflammatory pustules are confined strictly to hair follicles on the scalp and face with zero lesions on the body, wrists, or genitalia in an adult.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, unilateral dermatomal vesicles, grouped blisters, single dermatome, herpes zoster
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by unilateral dermatomal vesicles presenting as painful grouped fluid-filled blisters strictly confined within a single sensory dermatome respecting the midline, definitively diagnostic of herpes zoster.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, petechial non-blanching purpura, palpable purpura, leukocytoclastic vasculitis, extravasation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scabies is ruled out by widespread petechial non-blanching purpura and palpable purpuric papules on dependent lower extremities, indicating cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis rather than ectoparasitosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, atopic dermatitis, eczema, look-alike, flexural crease distribution, lack of burrows
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from atopic dermatitis because atopic dermatitis primarily involves flexural creases (antecubital and popliteal fossae), face, and neck with chronic personal or family atopic diathesis, whereas scabies features pathognomonic intraepidermal burrows, interdigital web lesions, pruritic male genital nodules, and rapid transmission to household contacts.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, bullous pemphigoid, autoimmune blistering, look-alike, tense subepidermal bullae, DIF linear IgG
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from bullous pemphigoid because bullous pemphigoid produces tense, large subepidermal bullae on normal or erythematous skin with linear IgG and C3 deposition along the dermal-epidermal junction on direct immunofluorescence and elevated anti-BP180/BP230 antibodies, whereas bullous scabies reveals intraepidermal burrows, delta-wing sign on dermoscopy, and mites on mineral oil scraping.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, insect bites, arthropod bites, flea bites, breakfast lunch dinner pattern, exposed extremities
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from insect bites (arthropod assault) because insect bites typically present with grouped, pruritic wheals or papules with a central punctum distributed in asymmetric clusters on exposed limbs (the 'breakfast, lunch, and dinner' sign), lacking intraepidermal burrows, web space involvement, or genital nodules.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, plaque psoriasis, psoriasis vulgaris, look-alike, extensor plaques, Auspitz sign, Norwegian mimic
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies (specifically crusted Norwegian scabies) is differentiated from plaque psoriasis because psoriasis features well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery micaceous scales on extensor surfaces (elbows, knees), positive Auspitz sign, nail pitting, and zero mites on skin scraping, whereas crusted scabies scrapings yield millions of living mites, eggs, and scybala.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, secondary syphilis, Treponema pallidum, look-alike, non-pruritic macules, condyloma lata
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from secondary syphilis because secondary syphilis presents with painless, non-pruritic copper-colored macules on the palms and soles, generalized non-tender lymphadenopathy, condyloma lata, mucosal patches, and reactive treponemal serology (RPR/VDRL and TPPA), whereas scabies presents with severe nocturnal itch, linear burrows, and negative treponemal tests.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, papular urticaria, pediatric hypersensitivity, look-alike, recurrent wheals, absence of burrows
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from papular urticaria because papular urticaria represents a chronic pediatric hypersensitivity to sporadic insect stings manifesting as recurrent crops of evanescent pruritic wheals and excoriated central papules without intraepidermal burrows, interdigital localization, or simultaneous infestation of family co-habitants.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, folliculitis, bacterial folliculitis, look-alike, hair-pierced pustules, absence of tunnels
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from bacterial folliculitis because folliculitis lesions are strictly centered around hair follicles, each pierced by a central hair shaft, distributed on friction-bearing hairy skin (thighs, buttocks, beard) without linear burrows or interdigital web tracks.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, contact dermatitis, allergic contact dermatitis, look-alike, geometric pattern, exposure history
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from allergic or irritant contact dermatitis because contact dermatitis lesions are sharply demarcated and correspond geometrically to exogenous chemical or allergen contact boundaries (e.g., waistband elastic, nickel snaps, poison ivy lines) and completely lack linear burrows, male genital nodules, or contagion to bed partners.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff, look-alike, greasy scales, sebaceous area predilection
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from seborrheic dermatitis because seborrheic dermatitis produces greasy, yellowish scales overlying mild erythema confined strictly to sebum-rich regions (scalp, nasolabial folds, eyebrows, central chest) with minimal itch, whereas classical adult scabies strictly spares the face and scalp.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Darier disease, keratosis follicularis, look-alike, autosomal dominant, greasy warty papules
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies (specifically crusted Norwegian scabies) is differentiated from Darier disease because Darier disease (keratosis follicularis) is an autosomal dominant genodermatosis presenting with firm, greasy, hyperkeratotic, warty papules in seborrheic distributions, distinctive nail V-nicks, corps ronds and grains on biopsy, and absence of parasites.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, dermatitis herpetiformis, celiac-associated, look-alike, extensor grouped vesicles, granular IgA
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from dermatitis herpetiformis because dermatitis herpetiformis produces intensely pruritic grouped polymorphous papulovesicles symmetrically distributed over extensor surfaces (elbows, knees, buttocks, scalp), strongly associates with gluten-sensitive enteropathy, and shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae on direct immunofluorescence.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, pityriasis rosea, herald patch, look-alike, Christmas tree pattern, Langer lines
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from pityriasis rosea because pityriasis rosea begins with an initial solitary 'herald patch' followed by an eruption of oval, salmon-colored macules with collarette scaling oriented along skin cleavage lines ('Christmas-tree distribution'), sparing the hands, feet, and genitalia, and resolving spontaneously in 6 to 8 weeks.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, cutaneous larva migrans, hookworm, look-alike, rapid advancing tracks, sandy soil exposure
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from cutaneous larva migrans (creeping eruption) because larva migrans causes rapidly advancing, intensely erythematous, tortuous serpiginous tracks progressing 1 to 2 cm daily, typically on the feet or buttocks following tropical sandy soil contact, whereas scabies burrows progress much slower (0.5 to 5 mm/day), cluster in web spaces and flexures, and spread from person to person.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, delusional parasitosis, Ekbom syndrome, look-alike, matchbox sign, lack of true lesions
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from delusional parasitosis (Ekbom syndrome) because delusional parasitosis presents with a fixed false belief of insect or mite infestation in the complete absence of objective burrows, papules, or microscopic findings, frequently accompanied by the 'matchbox sign' where patients present containers of epidermal lint, fibers, or dried skin flakes.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, dyshidrotic eczema, pompholyx, look-alike, tapioca-like vesicles, lateral fingers
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from dyshidrotic eczema (pompholyx) because dyshidrotic eczema produces deep-seated, intensely pruritic 'tapioca-like' microvesicles restricted strictly to the lateral aspects of fingers, palms, and soles without linear burrows, male genital lesions, or contagious spread to family contacts.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, lichen planus, 6 Ps, look-alike, Wickham striae, mucosal lacy plaques, volar wrists
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from lichen planus because lichen planus presents with the classic '6 Ps' (pruritic, planar, polygonal, purple, papules, and plaques) exhibiting fine reticular surface white lines (Wickham striae) on volar wrists and lacy oral mucosal plaques, completely lacking intraepidermal burrow tracks or mites.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, varicella zoster virus, chickenpox, look-alike, dewdrops on rose petal, acute fever
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Scabies is differentiated from varicella zoster virus (chickenpox) because varicella presents acutely with fever, malaise, and a rapid cephalocaudal progression of polymorphic pruritic vesicles in various stages ('dewdrops on a rose petal') resolving over 7 to 10 days with positive viral PCR or Tzanck smear, whereas scabies is an unremitting afebrile ectoparasitosis lacking systemic viremia.

entities.name: Schistosomiasis
entities.description: A major neglected tropical parasitic disease caused by blood-dwelling digenetic trematodes of the genus Schistosoma (S. haematobium, S. mansoni, S. japonicum, S. mekongi, S. intercalatum), manifesting as acute Katayama fever syndrome, chronic urogenital bilharzia with terminal hematuria and squamous bladder cancer, or chronic intestinal and hepatosplenic disease with Symmers pipestem periportal fibrosis and noncirrhotic portal hypertension.

entities.name: Katayama Fever Syndrome
entities.description: Acute systemic immune-complex hypersensitivity syndrome occurring 2 to 8 weeks after cercarial penetration during schistosomula maturation and initial oviposition, marked by high spiking fevers, chills, diaphoresis, and severe prostration.

entities.name: Terminal Hematuria
entities.description: Painless bright red blood voided selectively at the termination of micturition due to detrusor contraction against friable, egg-infiltrated bladder mucosa in Schistosoma haematobium infection.

entities.name: Colonic Polyposis
entities.description: Granulomatous inflammatory pseudopolyps of the colon and rectum triggered by dense submucosal egg deposition of Schistosoma mansoni or Schistosoma intercalatum.

entities.name: Symmers Pipestem Fibrosis
entities.description: Distinctive concentric periportal fibrosis forming dense collagenous sleeves around intrahepatic portal branches without true regenerative nodular cirrhosis, characteristic of S. mansoni and S. japonicum.

entities.name: Noncirrhotic Portal Hypertension
entities.description: Severe portal hypertension of presinusoidal etiology caused by periportal fibrosis in the presence of preserved hepatic parenchyma and intact lobular architecture.

entities.name: Esophageal Varices
entities.description: Markedly engorged, tortuous submucosal venous plexuses in the lower esophagus developing secondary to high portal pressures from schistosomal periportal fibrosis.

entities.name: Gastric Varices
entities.description: Dilated submucosal collateral vessels in the gastric fundus prone to severe rupture and catastrophic gastrointestinal hemorrhage in schistosomal portal hypertension.

entities.name: Variceal Upper GI Bleeding
entities.description: Catastrophic hematemesis and melena following the rupture of elevated-pressure gastroesophageal varices in patients with schistosomal Symmers fibrosis.

entities.name: Congestive Splenomegaly
entities.description: Substantial enlargement of the spleen extending across the abdominal quadrants secondary to chronic passive presinusoidal portal venous pooling.

entities.name: Bladder Wall Calcification
entities.description: Extensive dystrophic calcification of millions of nonviable Schistosoma haematobium eggs embedded within the urinary bladder wall.

entities.name: Squamous Cell Bladder Carcinoma
entities.description: Primary squamous malignancy of the urinary bladder arising from chronic epithelial irritation, squamous metaplasia, and nitrosamine exposure driven by S. haematobium eggs.

entities.name: Hydroureteronephrosis
entities.description: Unilateral or bilateral dilation of the ureters and renal collecting systems caused by granulomatous inflammatory strictures and distal ureteric scarring.

entities.name: Secondary Bacterial Pyelonephritis
entities.description: Ascending bacterial infection of the renal parenchyma facilitated by schistosomal obstructive uropathy, urinary stasis, and bladder distortion.

entities.name: Chronic Renal Failure
entities.description: Irreversible loss of excretory renal function secondary to chronic bilateral obstructive uropathy, reflux nephropathy, or schistosomal glomerulonephritis.

entities.name: Transverse Myelitis
entities.description: Acute inflammation and swelling across the spinal cord caused by ectopic egg migration via Batson's vertebral plexus, commonly seen with Schistosoma mansoni.

entities.name: Lumbosacral Myeloradiculopathy
entities.description: Subacute compression of lower spinal cord segments and cauda equina nerve roots by schistosomal granulomas, producing flaccid paraplegia and sphincter disturbances.

entities.name: Cerebral Granulomas
entities.description: Intracranial space-occupying granulomatous lesions formed around small, round Schistosoma japonicum eggs that bypass portal filters to enter cerebral vasculature.

entities.name: Jacksonian Focal Epilepsy
entities.description: Focal motor seizures marching sequentially across anatomical muscle groups, triggered by schistosomal granulomatous cortical irritation in S. japonicum infection.

entities.name: Increased Intracranial Pressure
entities.description: Elevation of intracranial pressure manifesting with intense headaches, papilledema, vomiting, and altered consciousness due to cerebral schistosomal mass effect.

entities.name: Female Genital Schistosomiasis
entities.description: Urogenital bilharzia affecting the vulva, vagina, and cervix, characterized by mucosal sandy patches, contact bleeding, and pelvic pain.

entities.name: Contact Postcoital Bleeding
entities.description: Vaginal bleeding occurring after sexual intercourse due to mechanical disruption of friable, egg-infiltrated, hypervascular cervical mucosa.

entities.name: Pelvic Dyspareunia
entities.description: Severe pain during sexual intercourse caused by chronic granulomatous inflammation and fibrosis involving the cervix, upper vagina, and pelvic organs.

entities.name: Primary Female Infertility
entities.description: Inability to achieve pregnancy secondary to fallopian tube occlusion, uterine inflammation, or ovarian granulomas caused by Schistosoma haematobium eggs.

entities.name: Male Genital Schistosomiasis
entities.description: Schistosoma haematobium egg deposition within the seminal vesicles, prostate, testes, and spermatic cord leading to chronic genitourinary morbidity.

entities.name: Recurrent Hematospermia
entities.description: Grossly visible blood in the seminal fluid caused by schistosomal granulomatous ulceration and vascular disruption within the seminal vesicles and prostate.

entities.name: Ejaculatory Pain
entities.description: Severe sharp or aching pain during ejaculation caused by chronic inflammatory obstruction and granulomas of the ejaculatory ducts and seminal vesicles.

entities.name: Cercarial Dermatitis
entities.description: Transient pruritic maculopapular cutaneous eruption occurring at sites of percutaneous penetration by free-swimming cercariae ('swimmer's itch').

entities.name: Nocturnal Dry Cough
entities.description: Persistent hacking nonproductive cough developing during schistosomula pulmonary migration and systemic immune-complex hypersensitivity.

entities.name: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension
entities.description: Elevated pulmonary vascular resistance caused by egg embolization through portosystemic collaterals into the pulmonary arterial bed.

entities.name: Schistosomal Cor Pulmonale
entities.description: Right ventricular hypertrophy and right heart failure secondary to chronic severe pulmonary vascular obliteration by schistosome egg granulomas.

entities.name: Glomerulonephritis
entities.description: Renal glomerular injury mediated by circulating schistosomal antigen-antibody immune complexes deposited in subendothelial and mesangial spaces.

entities.name: Protein-Losing Enteropathy
entities.description: Severe enteral protein loss and profound hypoalbuminemia resulting from massive diffuse colonic pseudopolyposis and mucosal exudation.

entities.name: Chronic Dysenteric Diarrhea
entities.description: Recurrent passage of loose, watery stools mixed with visible blood and mucus secondary to mucosal ulceration caused by egg extrusion.

entities.name: Tenesmus
entities.description: Painful, recurrent, ineffective straining at stool provoked by inflammatory granulomatous pseudopolyps in the rectosigmoid junction.

entities.name: Colonic Stenosis
entities.description: Fibrotic narrowing and stricture formation of the colonic lumen secondary to chronic transmural granulomatous scarring.

entities.name: Pediatric Growth Stunting
entities.description: Impaired linear growth and delayed developmental milestones in children with high chronic schistosome worm and egg burdens.

entities.name: Childhood Cognitive Impairment
entities.description: Reduced scholastic achievement, attention deficits, and memory impairment in infected school-age children reversible with anti-helminthic therapy.

entities.name: Generalized Urticaria
entities.description: Widespread pruritic wheals and cutaneous erythema appearing as part of the systemic serum sickness-like response in acute Katayama fever.

entities.name: Tender Hepatosplenomegaly
entities.description: Painful, tender enlargement of both liver and spleen occurring during the acute immune-complex hypersensitivity stage.

entities.name: Caput Medusae
entities.description: Prominent, engorged subcutaneous collateral veins radiating from the umbilicus across the abdominal wall due to recanalization of the umbilical vein.

entities.name: Painless Terminal Hematuria
entities.description: Pathognomonic hallmark in >80% of children with S. haematobium, consisting of bright red blood passed exclusively at the end of micturition.

entities.name: Colposcopic Sandy Patches
entities.description: Pathognomonic mucosal appearance in female genital schistosomiasis, showing rough, yellowish, sandy areas on cervical and vaginal colposcopy.

entities.name: Cystoscopic Sandy Patches
entities.description: Pathognomonic bladder mucosal lesion displaying rough, yellow-brown granular mucosal plaques resembling beach sand upon cystoscopy.

entities.name: Preserved Hepatic Synthesis
entities.description: Pathognomonic preservation of normal serum albumin, PT/INR, and absence of jaundice or encephalopathy despite massive portal hypertension.

entities.name: Batson Plexus Myelopathy
entities.description: Hallmark acute flaccid paraplegia and sharp sensory level at T11-L1 resulting from retrograde egg embolization via valveless vertebral venous plexus.

entities.name: Cercarial Maculopapular Rash
entities.description: Discrete erythematous, pruritic papules 1 to 3 cm in diameter developing at freshwater cercarial penetration sites on the skin.

entities.name: Massive Splenomegaly
entities.description: Physical exam finding of an extraordinarily enlarged, firm spleen extending into the left lower quadrant or past the umbilicus.

entities.name: Firm Nodular Splenomegaly
entities.description: Palpation of a hard, blunt splenic border without splenic tenderness, reflecting chronic fibrocongestive splenic tissue remodeling.

entities.name: Prominent Caput Medusae
entities.description: Conspicuous physical exam sign of engorged, tortuous collateral veins radiating centrifugally from the umbilicus across the abdominal wall.

entities.name: Bladder Suprapubic Tenderness
entities.description: Direct physical exam pain or discomfort elicited upon deep palpation over the hypogastrium and urinary bladder.

entities.name: Tender Left Hepatic Lobe
entities.description: Preferential enlargement and tenderness of the left liver lobe on physical palpation in acute and subacute schistosomiasis.

entities.name: Generalized Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Symmetrical, nontender enlargement of superficial lymph node chains (cervical, axillary, epitrochlear, inguinal) during Katayama fever.

entities.name: Pulmonary Basilar Rales
entities.description: Auscultatory crackles and rhonchi heard over lung bases during the acute migratory and hypersensitivity phases of schistosomiasis.

entities.name: Periorbital Angioedema
entities.description: Bilateral facial and periorbital subcutaneous swelling developing acutely alongside urticaria in Katayama syndrome.

entities.name: Flaccid Paraplegia
entities.description: Acute bilateral lower extremity motor paralysis with loss of deep tendon reflexes reflecting spinal schistosomal cord compression.

entities.name: Sensory Level T11-L1
entities.description: Sharp demarcation of pinprick and light touch sensation loss below the lower thoracic and upper lumbar dermatomes on neurological exam.

entities.name: Neurogenic Urinary Retention
entities.description: Palpable, dull suprapubic abdominal mass corresponding to an acutely overdistended, non-emptying urinary bladder due to spinal lesion.

entities.name: Vulvar Granulomatous Nodules
entities.description: Physical inspection finding of firm, indurated, or ulcerated granulomatous mucosal nodules on the labia majora and vulva.

entities.name: Cervical Contact Friability
entities.description: Immediate bleeding of the uterine cervix upon light swab contact or speculum insertion during gynecological examination.

entities.name: Testicular Granulomatous Swelling
entities.description: Palpable unilateral or bilateral firm, nodular, non-transilluminating mass of the testis or epididymis mimicking malignancy.

entities.name: Papilledema
entities.description: Bilateral blurring of optic disc margins, disc hyperemia, and loss of venous pulsations seen on fundoscopic examination.

entities.name: Nystagmus
entities.description: Involuntary rhythmic oscillatory movement of the eyes observed on cranial nerve examination in cerebellar schistosomal involvement.

entities.name: Jacksonian Seizure March
entities.description: Observed physical progression of focal clonic muscular twitches from the distal extremity upward across proximal muscle groups.

entities.name: Severe Conjunctival Pallor
entities.description: Extreme blanching of the palpebral conjunctivae indicating advanced microcytic iron deficiency anemia from chronic blood loss.

entities.name: Fever Rigors Paroxysms
entities.description: Physical observation of violent shaking chills followed by high-spiking pyrexia during acute Katayama fever presentations.

entities.name: Right Upper Quadrant Tenderness
entities.description: Sharp tenderness elicited by subcostal palpation over the hepatic edge reflecting active inflammatory capsular distension.

entities.name: Peripheral Edema
entities.description: Pitting subcutaneous swelling of bilateral pretibial regions and ankles resulting from schistosomal nephropathy or protein-losing bowel.

entities.name: Smooth Liver Margin
entities.description: Palpation of a sharp, smooth, non-nodular liver edge on deep inspiration, contrasting against the irregular nodularity of cirrhosis.

entities.name: Terminal-Spined Urine Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic identification of 110-170 x 40-70 µm transparent oval ova bearing a distinct, sharp terminal spine on midday urine filtration.

entities.name: Lateral-Spined Stool Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic identification of 114-180 x 45-70 µm golden-brown oval eggs bearing a prominent, sharp lateral spine on Kato-Katz fecal smears.

entities.name: Lateral-Knobbed Stool Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic finding of 70-100 x 50-70 µm rounded subglobular eggs with an inconspicuous lateral knob on stool exam in S. japonicum.

entities.name: High Peripheral Eosinophilia
entities.description: Profound elevation of circulating eosinophils (>20-50% of differential, absolute count >3,000-8,000/µL) on admission CBC in Katayama fever.

entities.name: Persistent Chronic Eosinophilia
entities.description: Mild-to-moderate persistent elevation of eosinophils (5-15% of differential) on routine blood counts in chronic active schistosomiasis.

entities.name: Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
entities.description: Reduced hemoglobin with low mean corpuscular volume and low mean corpuscular hemoglobin due to chronic gastrointestinal or urinary blood loss.

entities.name: Hypersplenism-Induced Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Substantial reduction in circulating platelet count (<100,000/µL) caused by splenic sequestration in massive schistosomal splenomegaly.

entities.name: Hypersplenism-Induced Leukopenia
entities.description: Mild-to-moderate leukopenia (WBC 2,500-4,000/µL) with intact bone marrow cellularity secondary to splenic reticuloendothelial pooling.

entities.name: Urinalysis Microscopic Hematuria
entities.description: Positive chemical dipstick for blood and high numbers of intact erythrocytes on urine microscopic sediment analysis.

entities.name: Urinalysis Proteinuria
entities.description: Detection of urinary protein on reagent strip testing reflecting egg-induced urothelial ulceration or immune-complex glomerulopathy.

entities.name: Urine POC-CCA Positivity
entities.description: Rapid lateral flow urine dipstick detecting regurgitated circulating cathodic antigen of living adult Schistosoma mansoni within 20 minutes.

entities.name: Normal Serum Albumin
entities.description: Serum albumin levels maintained within normal limits (>3.5 g/dL) demonstrating intact liver synthetic function despite severe portal hypertension.

entities.name: Normal Prothrombin Time
entities.description: Normal prothrombin time and international normalized ratio (INR <1.2) indicating intact coagulation factor synthesis by hepatocytes.

entities.name: Normal Serum Bilirubin
entities.description: Absence of direct or indirect hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin <1.2 mg/dL) confirming preserved hepatobiliary clearance.

entities.name: Polyclonal Hypergammaglobulinemia
entities.description: Significant elevation of serum total globulins and IgG on protein electrophoresis reflecting chronic antigenic stimulation by eggs.

entities.name: Elevated Serum IgE
entities.description: Massive elevation of total circulating immunoglobulin E levels on admission chemistry reflecting a robust Th2 antiparasitic response.

entities.name: Circulating Immune Complexes
entities.description: High levels of circulating antigen-antibody complexes detected in serum during the acute Katayama hypersensitivity stage.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Increased serum creatinine and reduced estimated GFR resulting from chronic bilateral obstructive hydronephrosis.

entities.name: Elevated Blood Urea
entities.description: Elevated blood urea nitrogen (BUN) indicating post-renal obstructive uropathy secondary to fibrotic schistosomal ureteral strictures.

entities.name: Positive Schistosome Serology
entities.description: Detection of anti-schistosomal IgG/IgM antibodies by ELISA or indirect hemagglutination in acute infection or returned travelers.

entities.name: Positive Stool Miracidial Hatching
entities.description: Macroscopic observation of motile hatched miracidia swimming in distilled water following fecal concentration in a nylon flask.

entities.name: Rectal Snip Egg Granulomas
entities.description: Microscopic visualization of viable or calcified schistosome eggs in crushed fresh rectal mucosal biopsy pressed between glass slides.

entities.name: Bladder Biopsy Egg Granulomas
entities.description: Histopathological demonstration of viable or calcified Schistosoma haematobium eggs and granulomatous inflammation in cystoscopic biopsy.

entities.name: Ultrasound Periportal Cuffing
entities.description: Echogenic fibrous sleeves surrounding intrahepatic portal branches (wall thickness >4-6 mm) on WHO Niamey protocol ultrasound.

entities.name: Ultrasound Pipestem Sign
entities.description: Classic ultrasound cross-sectional appearance of echogenic circular rings ('doughnut' or 'bullseye' sign) around portal branches.

entities.name: Main Portal Vein Dilation
entities.description: Main portal vein caliber exceeding 12 to 14 mm on abdominal ultrasonography reflecting elevated presinusoidal venous pressure.

entities.name: Patent Hepatic Veins
entities.description: Preserved normal caliber and physiological Doppler flow waveforms in hepatic veins on ultrasound, excluding postsinusoidal obstruction.

entities.name: Ultrasound Bladder Wall Thickening
entities.description: Irregular, asymmetric, or concentric thickening of the urinary bladder wall exceeding 5 mm on bedside pelvic ultrasound.

entities.name: Ultrasound Bladder Pseudopolyps
entities.description: Exophytic granulomatous soft-tissue masses protruding into the bladder lumen on transabdominal pelvic ultrasound.

entities.name: Sonographic Hydroureter
entities.description: Dilation of the distal and proximal ureteric lumen visualized on abdominal and pelvic sonography due to fibrotic strictures.

entities.name: Sonographic Hydronephrosis
entities.description: Dilation and blunting of the renal pelvis and calyces on renal ultrasound secondary to chronic downstream schistosomal obstruction.

entities.name: Bladder Rim Calcification
entities.description: Fine curvilinear radio-opaque line delineating the contour of the urinary bladder ('fetal head' calcification) on plain radiography.

entities.name: Chest X-Ray Reticulonodular Infiltrates
entities.description: Diffuse bilateral micronodular or reticular pulmonary parenchymal shadows on chest radiography during Katayama fever.

entities.name: Spinal MRI Cord Enlargement
entities.description: Focal expansion and T2-hyperintense intramedullary signal of the lower thoracic cord or conus medullaris on spinal MRI.

entities.name: Spinal MRI Nodular Enhancement
entities.description: Heterogeneous nodular, patchy, or flame-shaped contrast enhancement of the spinal cord and nerve roots on T1 gadolinium MRI.

entities.name: Brain CT Hyperdense Granulomas
entities.description: Focal hyperdense intracranial lesions with extensive surrounding hypodense vasogenic edema on non-contrast cerebral CT.

entities.name: Brain MRI Ring Enhancement
entities.description: Clustered ring-enhancing or nodular lesions with prominent surrounding vasogenic edema on contrast-enhanced cerebral MRI.

entities.name: Barium Enema Mucosal Granularity
entities.description: Fine irregular granular mucosal mucosal surface and multiple polypoid filling defects on double-contrast barium fluoroscopy.

entities.name: Infested Freshwater Immersion
entities.description: Direct skin contact with natural freshwater bodies harboring infected snail intermediate hosts shedding infective cercariae.

entities.name: Freshwater Recreational Swimming
entities.description: Recreational bathing, swimming, or diving in endemic freshwater lakes and streams, a major infection route for children and travelers.

entities.name: Occupational Agricultural Wading
entities.description: Agricultural activities in flooded irrigation networks and rice fields without waterproof protective garments.

entities.name: Freshwater Artisanal Fishing
entities.description: Submersion during artisanal net-casting, boat launching, and fish sorting in endemic lacustrine and riverine habitats.

entities.name: Domestic Water Washing
entities.description: Daily domestic activities including laundry washing and water collection in infested surface freshwater sources.

entities.name: Sub-Saharan Africa Endemicity
entities.description: Residence or travel within sub-Saharan African countries, which harbor >90% of global schistosomiasis disease burden.

entities.name: Nile River Basin
entities.description: Historical and contemporary high-transmission freshwater basin in Egypt and Sudan supporting S. haematobium and S. mansoni.

entities.name: Yangtze River Basin
entities.description: Major zoonotic transmission ecosystem in central and eastern China (Poyang and Dongting Lakes) sustaining Schistosoma japonicum.

entities.name: Mekong River Basin
entities.description: Focal geographic riverine transmission zone in southern Laos and northern Cambodia supporting Schistosoma mekongi.

entities.name: Lake Malawi Immersion
entities.description: High-risk recreational freshwater exposure site where international tourists frequently contract Schistosoma haematobium.

entities.name: Lake Victoria Exposure
entities.description: Major East African freshwater reservoir exhibiting intense transmission of both Schistosoma mansoni and Schistosoma haematobium.

entities.name: Biomphalaria Snail Host
entities.description: Obligate freshwater planorbid snail intermediate host (e.g., B. glabrata, B. pfeifferi) required for Schistosoma mansoni.

entities.name: Bulinus Snail Host
entities.description: Obligate aquatic gastropod intermediate host (e.g., B. globosus, B. truncatus) required for Schistosoma haematobium.

entities.name: Oncomelania Snail Host
entities.description: Amphibious prosobranch snail intermediate host (Oncomelania hupensis) required for Schistosoma japonicum life cycle.

entities.name: Percutaneous Cercarial Penetration
entities.description: Direct transdermal entry of free-swimming fork-tailed cercariae through intact human skin within seconds to minutes of contact.

entities.name: Water Buffalo Reservoir
entities.description: Major domestic ungulate reservoir in Asia excreting high volumes of viable Schistosoma japonicum eggs into aquatic habitats.

entities.name: School-Age Children
entities.description: Primary demographic cohort (ages 5 to 15) with the highest frequency of recreational water contact and peak infection intensities.

entities.name: Non-Immune International Travelers
entities.description: Immunologically naive travelers and eco-tourists visiting endemic areas who lack acquired immunity and develop Katayama fever.

entities.name: Irrigation Canal Workers
entities.description: Agricultural and municipal laborers maintaining rural irrigation ditches experiencing intense daily cercarial exposure.

entities.name: Cercarial Dermatitis Incubation
entities.description: Rapid incubation window of hours up to 48 hours following freshwater cercarial penetration before swimmer's itch erupts.

entities.name: Katayama Syndrome Incubation
entities.description: Latent clinical incubation period of 2 to 8 weeks between cercarial penetration and the sudden onset of acute Katayama fever.

entities.name: Chronic Bilharzia Incubation
entities.description: Prolonged insidious incubation period of several months to years (often 5 to 15 years) required for cumulative fibro-obstructive pathology.

entities.name: Zero Freshwater Contact
entities.description: Absolute lack of lifetime or travel-associated physical contact with natural freshwater lakes, rivers, or canals.

entities.name: Exclusively Saltwater Immersion
entities.description: History confined entirely to ocean, sea, or hyper-chlorinated swimming pool exposure without freshwater contact.

entities.name: Hyperacute 24-Hour Fever
entities.description: Onset of systemic febrile illness within 24 hours of freshwater immersion, incompatible with the 2-8 week incubation of Katayama fever.

entities.name: Absence of Eosinophilia
entities.description: Complete lack of peripheral eosinophilia (<1-2% of differential, absolute count <100/µL) during acute febrile post-immersion illness.

entities.name: Negative Urinalysis Microhematuria
entities.description: Repeated chemical reagent dipsticks demonstrating zero blood and completely negative microscopic urinary sediment.

entities.name: Normal Bladder Ultrasound
entities.description: Completely smooth, thin bladder wall (<3 mm) without pseudopolyps, calcifications, or distal ureteral dilation on ultrasound.

entities.name: Purulent Urethral Discharge
entities.description: Copious thick, yellow-green purulent discharge from the urethral meatus typical of gonococcal or chlamydial urethritis.

entities.name: Early Micturition Hematuria
entities.description: Blood passed exclusively during the initial stream of urination, localized to the anterior urethra.

entities.name: Continuous Painful Hematuria
entities.description: Continuous gross hematuria throughout the entire urinary stream accompanied by acute severe radiating flank colic.

entities.name: Severe Hepatocellular Failure
entities.description: Early profound jaundice, hepatic asterixis, marked coagulopathy (INR >2.0), and encephalopathy inconsistent with presinusoidal block.

entities.name: Cirrhotic Hepatic Nodularity
entities.description: Diffuse micronodular or macronodular parenchymal distortion with small shrunken liver lobes on ultrasound or biopsy.

entities.name: Negative Schistosome Serology
entities.description: Completely negative anti-schistosome IgG ELISA and indirect hemagglutination assays performed >=3 months post-exposure.

entities.name: Negative Kato-Katz Exams
entities.description: Repeated serial negative Kato-Katz thick smears (>=3 to 4 distinct stool specimens prepared on separate days).

entities.name: Negative Midday Urine Filtrations
entities.description: Repeated serial negative 10 mL daytime urine filtrations (>=3 specimens collected between 10:00 and 14:00).

entities.name: Rapid Antibiotic Response
entities.description: Prompt clinical defervescence and complete symptom resolution within 24 to 48 hours of starting standard antibacterial therapy.

entities.name: Positive Blood Bacterial Culture
entities.description: Isolation of pathogenic bacterial organisms (e.g., Salmonella enterica, Escherichia coli bacteremia) on admission blood cultures.

entities.name: Absence of Splenomegaly
entities.description: Entirely normal splenic size and absence of splenomegaly on ultrasound in a patient presenting with bleeding esophageal varices.

entities.name: Isolated Unilateral Nephrolithiasis
entities.description: Solitary discrete radio-dense calcium oxalate calculus on CT without mucosal bladder calcification or terminal hematuria.

entities.name: Diffuse Intrahepatic Duct Dilation
entities.description: Widespread dilatation of the intrahepatic biliary tree on ultrasound or CT without periportal fibrous cuffing.

entities.name: Severe Primary Thrombocytosis
entities.description: Markedly elevated circulating platelet count (>600,000/µL) inconsistent with schistosomal portal hypertension.

entities.name: Marked Absolute Neutrophilia
entities.description: Marked left-shifted neutrophilia (>85% neutrophils, >15,000/µL) with toxic granulations and zero eosinophils.

entities.name: Acute Watery Secretory Diarrhea
entities.description: Profuse painless rice-water diarrhea without blood, mucus, tenesmus, or fever, typical of Vibrio cholerae infection.

entities.name: Bacterial Urinary Infection
entities.description: Acute bacterial cystitis or pyelonephritis caused by uropathogenic coliform bacteria presenting with dysuria throughout urination and pyuria.

entities.name: Urothelial Bladder Carcinoma
entities.description: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder arising in older tobacco-exposed patients presenting with painless continuous hematuria.

entities.name: Decompensated Hepatic Cirrhosis
entities.description: End-stage parenchymal liver disease marked by diffuse architectural distortion, regenerative nodules, and severe hepatocellular synthetic failure.

entities.name: Acute Malaria
entities.description: Life-threatening intraerythrocytic protozoan infection caused by Plasmodium species presenting with cyclical fever paroxysms and hemolysis.

entities.name: Visceral Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Disseminated protozoan infection caused by Leishmania donovani presenting with chronic undulating fever, pancytopenia, and wasting.

entities.name: Enteric Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Invasive systemic salmonellosis caused by Salmonella Typhi presenting with step-ladder fever, relative bradycardia, and rose spots.

entities.name: Acute Viral Hepatitis
entities.description: Acute necroinflammatory liver infection caused by hepatotropic viruses (HAV, HBV, HCV, HEV) presenting with jaundice and extreme transaminitis.

entities.name: Amebic Colitis
entities.description: Invasive intestinal infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica causing flask-shaped ulcers, dysentery, and amebic trophozoites with ingested RBCs.

entities.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
entities.description: Focal liquified necrotic hepatic abscess caused by Entamoeba histolytica containing anchovy-sauce-like fluid with high fever.

entities.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
entities.description: Chronic idiopathic autoimmune colonic inflammation (ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease) presenting with mucosal ulcerations and bloody stools.

entities.name: Renal Tuberculosis
entities.description: Urinary tract Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection presenting with sterile pyuria, acidic urine, and ureteric strictures.

entities.name: Acute Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection caused by Leptospira interrogans presenting with conjunctival suffusion, severe calf pain, and jaundice.

entities.name: Acute Dengue Fever
entities.description: Arboviral infection caused by Dengue virus presenting with retro-orbital headache, breakbone arthralgias, and plasma leakage.

entities.name: Eosinophilic Granulomatosis Polyangiitis
entities.description: Systemic necrotizing vasculitis (Churg-Strauss syndrome) affecting small vessels, presenting with asthma, sinusitis, and eosinophilia.

entities.name: Fascioliasis
entities.description: Zoonotic liver fluke infection caused by Fasciola hepatica acquired via wild watercress ingestion, presenting with branching hepatic tunnels.

entities.name: Clonorchiasis
entities.description: Biliary trematodiasis caused by Clonorchis sinensis acquired by eating raw freshwater fish, causing intrahepatic duct dilatation.

entities.name: Multiple Sclerosis
entities.description: Chronic demyelinating autoimmune disease of the central nervous system featuring neurological deficits disseminated in time and space.

entities.name: Cerebral High-Grade Glioma
entities.description: Primary intracranial malignant neoplasm (glioblastoma) presenting as a solitary infiltrating enhancing cerebral mass lesion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute schistosomiasis (Katayama fever syndrome) manifests 2 to 8 weeks following primary freshwater cercarial penetration, presenting as a severe immune-complex hypersensitivity reaction with abrupt high spiking fever, rigors, diaphoresis, and profound constitutional prostration.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Urogenital schistosomiasis manifests with painless terminal hematuria, where bright red blood is passed at the very end of micturition due to vigorous contraction of the urinary bladder detrusor muscle against friable submucosal egg granulomas.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Intestinal schistosomiasis manifests as colonic polyposis, where chronic intramural deposition of Schistosoma mansoni eggs triggers extensive granulomatous mucosal hyperplasia, inflammatory pseudopolyps, and friable ulcerations throughout the rectosigmoid colon.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Advanced hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests as Symmers pipestem fibrosis, characterized by dense fibrous collars wrapping intrahepatic portal vein branches in response to millions of embolized eggs, leading to severe presinusoidal vascular occlusion while sparing hepatocytes.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests as noncirrhotic portal hypertension, where presinusoidal mechanical obstruction to portal flow drives extreme venous hypertension while preserving normal lobular architecture and intact baseline hepatocyte synthetic function.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Advanced hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests with esophageal varices, resulting from massive retrograde blood flow through coronary and esophageal collaterals driven by extreme presinusoidal portal venous hypertension.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests with gastric fundal varices, forming prominent subepithelial vascular cushions vulnerable to sudden erosive rupture and life-threatening upper gastrointestinal bleeding.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Advanced hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests as variceal upper GI bleeding, presenting with acute massive hematemesis and melena due to rupture of high-pressure esophageal or gastric varices, often with preserved liver function until hemorrhagic shock intervenes.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests as massive congestive splenomegaly, where chronic retrograde presinusoidal hypertension induces red pulp hyperplasia, reticuloendothelial proliferation, and splenic enlargement frequently reaching the pelvic brim.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Chronic urogenital schistosomiasis manifests as bladder wall calcification, where dead trapped Schistosoma haematobium eggs undergo dense dystrophic mural calcification, creating a rigid, contracted, non-compliant urinary bladder.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Chronic Schistosoma haematobium infection manifests as squamous cell bladder carcinoma, developing through long-term egg-induced urothelial injury, squamous metaplasia, oxidative DNA damage, and chronic endogenous nitrosamine exposure.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Urogenital schistosomiasis manifests as progressive hydroureteronephrosis, where egg-induced granulomas and mural fibrosis at the ureterovesical junctions produce severe functional and mechanical urinary outflow obstruction.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Urogenital schistosomiasis manifests with secondary bacterial pyelonephritis, where urinary stasis behind fibrotic ureteral strictures and calcified bladder walls promotes persistent secondary colonization by uropathogenic Gram-negative bacteria.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Late-stage urogenital schistosomiasis manifests as chronic renal failure, resulting from years of uncorrected bilateral obstructive hydronephrosis, recurrent pyelonephritis, and progressive renal parenchymal atrophy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Ectopic neuroschistosomiasis manifests as acute transverse myelitis, where schistosome eggs embolize through Batson's valveless vertebral venous plexus into the spinal cord, evoking intense Th2 granulomatous cord necrosis and swelling.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Spinal neuroschistosomiasis manifests as lumbosacral myeloradiculopathy, presenting with acute or subacute lower extremity motor deficits, sensory level loss from T11 to L1, and loss of sphincter control due to conus and cauda equina granulomas.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Neuroschistosomiasis manifests as cerebral granulomas, primarily caused by Schistosoma japonicum eggs whose small size allows passage into intracranial arterioles, creating multifocal brain granulomatous masses and surrounding vasogenic edema.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cerebral neuroschistosomiasis manifests as Jacksonian focal epilepsy, where granulomas located in the motor cortex provoke recurrent focal motor seizures that march progressively across unilateral extremities or facial muscles.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cerebral schistosomiasis manifests with increased intracranial pressure, characterized by severe intractable headache, projectile vomiting, papilledema, and obtundation due to cerebral edema and space-occupying egg granulomas.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Urogenital schistosomiasis manifests as female genital schistosomiasis (FGS), where egg entrapment in the lower genital tract causes mucosal sandy patches, contact bleeding, chronic pelvic pain, and marked biological susceptibility to HIV acquisition.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Female genital schistosomiasis manifests as contact postcoital bleeding, caused by friable, inflamed cervical mucosal granulomas and neovascularization that bleed easily during sexual intercourse or clinical examination.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Female genital schistosomiasis manifests as chronic pelvic dyspareunia, resulting from chronic granulomatous inflammation, ulceration, and fibrous scarring across the cervix, vaginal vault, and pelvic connective tissues.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Female genital schistosomiasis manifests as primary female infertility and increased risk of ectopic pregnancy, secondary to schistosomal granulomatous salpingitis, fallopian tube fibrosis, and chronic endometritis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Urogenital schistosomiasis manifests as male genital schistosomiasis (MGS), characterized by granulomatous egg deposition within the seminal vesicles, prostate gland, and epididymis, resulting in local inflammation, swelling, and subfertility.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Male genital schistosomiasis manifests as recurrent hematospermia, presenting with frank blood in the ejaculate due to granulomatous erosion of capillary vessels in the seminal vesicles and prostatic parenchyma.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Male genital schistosomiasis manifests as ejaculatory pain and discomfort, resulting from egg-induced inflammatory strictures, granulomatous induration, and ductal distension in the seminal vesicles and prostate gland.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute early infection manifests as cercarial dermatitis ('swimmer's itch'), presenting with intense cutaneous pruritus, erythema, and maculopapular lesions at the sites of cercarial transdermal penetration within hours of freshwater exposure.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute Katayama schistosomiasis manifests as nocturnal dry cough, triggered by the mechanical migration of schistosomula through pulmonary capillary beds combined with generalized Th2 immune-complex hypersensitivity pneumonitis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests as pulmonary arterial hypertension, where portosystemic collateral shunts allow schistosome eggs to bypass hepatic sinusoids and lodge in pulmonary pre-capillary arterioles, inciting obliterative granulomatous arteritis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Advanced cardiopulmonary schistosomiasis manifests as schistosomal cor pulmonale, marked by right ventricular dilation, tricuspid regurgitation, and peripheral edema secondary to long-standing precapillary pulmonary arterial hypertension.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Chronic schistosomiasis manifests as immune-mediated glomerulonephritis, driven by circulating schistosomal gut antigens (CAA, CCA) forming immune complexes that deposit within glomerular basements, provoking mesangioproliferative or membranoproliferative injury.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Severe intestinal schistosomiasis manifests as protein-losing enteropathy, where diffuse mucosal ulceration, hyperplastic pseudopolyps, and chronic capillary leakage in the colon cause massive enteric loss of serum albumin and refractory peripheral edema.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Intestinal schistosomiasis manifests as chronic dysenteric diarrhea, characterized by frequent loose stools mixed with gross blood and mucus resulting from active mechanical and enzymatic extrusion of schistosome eggs through the gut mucosa.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Intestinal schistosomiasis manifests with severe rectal tenesmus, provoked by inflammatory egg granulomas, mucosal thickening, and polypoid masses in the lower rectosigmoid stimulating persistent pelvic defecatory reflexes.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Chronic intestinal schistosomiasis manifests as colonic stenosis, where intense recurrent transmural granulomatous inflammation and progressive cicatricial fibrosis cause circumferential luminal narrowing and partial mechanical bowel obstruction.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pediatric schistosomiasis manifests as growth stunting and physical wasting, resulting from chronic systemic immune activation, elevated circulating pro-inflammatory cytokines, micronutrient malabsorption, and unremitting gastrointestinal or urinary blood loss.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pediatric schistosomiasis manifests as childhood cognitive impairment, where chronic iron deficiency anemia and sustained cytokine-mediated fatigue lead to documented deficits in memory, cognition, school performance, and executive function.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute Katayama schistosomiasis manifests as generalized urticaria, presenting with sudden crops of itchy, erythematous wheals and vasomotor flushing secondary to high levels of circulating parasite-specific immune complexes and histamine release.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute schistosomiasis manifests as tender hepatosplenomegaly, where sudden intense reticuloendothelial stimulation and hepatic sinus infiltration by eosinophils and macrophages cause acute capsular distension and tenderness.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Advanced hepatosplenic schistosomiasis manifests as caput medusae, visible as tortuous, engorged collateral veins radiating across the abdominal wall secondary to recanalization of the umbilical vein under severe presinusoidal portal pressure.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Painless terminal hematuria is the pathognomonic clinical hallmark of active urogenital Schistosoma haematobium infection, characterized by bright red blood voided specifically at the final conclusion of urination as detrusor contraction compresses egg-studded mucosa.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Colposcopic sandy patches represent a pathognomonic physical hallmark of female genital schistosomiasis, visible on colposcopic examination as distinct, rough, yellow-sand-like mucosal lesions corresponding to submucosal clusters of calcified ova.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Cystoscopic sandy patches provide a pathognomonic visual hallmark of chronic urinary schistosomiasis, presenting on cystoscopy as clusters of calcified degenerating eggs in the submucosa that resemble grains of sand along the bladder floor.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Preserved hepatic synthesis is a cardinal pathognomonic hallmark of hepatosplenic schistosomiasis, where normal hepatocellular function (normal albumin, normal coagulation, no jaundice or asterixis) persists despite massive splenomegaly and bleeding varices.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Batson plexus myelopathy is a pathognomonic neuroschistosomal hallmark, characterized by acute flaccid paraplegia and an abrupt T11-L1 sensory level resulting from retrograde migration of Schistosoma mansoni eggs through the valveless vertebral venous network.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Cercarial maculopapular rash presents on physical examination as discrete, itchy, raised erythematous papules measuring 1 to 3 cm, localized to cutaneous surfaces directly submerged in cercariae-infested water.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Massive splenomegaly is palpable on abdominal physical exam as a huge, firm, non-tender spleen crossing the umbilical midline, secondary to long-standing presinusoidal portal venous pooling.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Firm nodular splenomegaly is detected on abdominal palpation as a hard, blunt splenic edge that descends with inspiration, reflecting sustained reticuloendothelial hypertrophy and chronic portal congestion.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Prominent caput medusae is visible on physical inspection of the abdomen as tortuous, dilated periumbilical subcutaneous veins carrying collateral blood away from the recanalized umbilical vein.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Bladder suprapubic tenderness is elicited upon deep palpation of the lower midline abdomen, reflecting active transmural granulomatous cystitis and inflammatory distension of the bladder wall.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Tender left hepatic lobe is a classic physical examination anchor in early schistosomiasis, where preferential left portal venous flow causes marked early left hepatic lobe enlargement and capsular stretch tenderness.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Generalized lymphadenopathy is palpable on physical examination during acute Katayama fever, presenting with painless, rubbery enlargement of cervical, axillary, and inguinal lymph node stations.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Pulmonary basilar rales are auscultated across bilateral lower lung zones on chest physical examination during acute schistosomiasis, reflecting schistosomula capillary migration and reactive hypersensitivity alveolitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Periorbital angioedema is visible on physical examination of the head and face in acute Katayama syndrome, manifesting as sudden bilateral soft-tissue swelling around the eyelids due to immune-complex mediated vascular permeability.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Flaccid paraplegia is found on neurological examination in spinal cord schistosomiasis, characterized by acute lower extremity hypotonia, flaccid weakness, and loss of patellar and Achilles deep tendon reflexes.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Sensory level T11-L1 is mapped on physical sensory examination in spinal neuroschistosomiasis, identifying a crisp dermatomal sensory loss to pinprick and temperature below the lower trunk and lower extremities.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Neurogenic urinary retention is identified on physical examination as a tense, percussion-dull suprapubic mass from autonomic bladder denervation resulting from schistosomal conus medullaris granulomas.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Vulvar granulomatous nodules are identified on gynecological physical exam in female genital schistosomiasis, appearing as irregular, firm, painless or tender raised mucosal nodules on the vulva and introitus.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Cervical contact friability is demonstrated on physical speculum exam in female genital schistosomiasis, where gentle touching of the ectocervix with a cotton swab induces immediate capillary bleeding.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Testicular granulomatous swelling is palpable on scrotal physical examination in male genital schistosomiasis, presenting as a firm, non-tender nodular induration of the testis or spermatic cord.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Papilledema is observed on fundoscopic examination in patients with cerebral neuroschistosomiasis, indicating severely elevated intracranial pressure from space-occupying egg granulomas and cerebral edema.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Nystagmus is detected on physical cranial nerve testing in neuroschistosomiasis when granulomatous inflammation and mass effect disrupt vestibular or cerebellar brainstem pathways.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Jacksonian seizure march is observed during clinical bedside examination in cerebral schistosomiasis japonica, manifesting as clonic twitches starting in a hand or foot and marching sequentially up the affected limb.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Severe conjunctival pallor is noted on eye inspection during admission physical exam, indicating profound microcytic hypochromic anemia resulting from unremitting gastrointestinal or urogenital egg-induced bleeding.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Fever rigors paroxysms are documented on bedside physical triage in acute Katayama syndrome, presenting with teeth-chattering rigors, piloerection, and rapid temperature spikes up to 40-41 degrees Celsius.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Right upper quadrant tenderness is found on abdominal palpation during acute and subacute schistosomiasis, produced by acute inflammatory periportal cellular infiltration stretching Glisson's capsule.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Peripheral edema is demonstrated on physical examination as dependent bilateral pretibial pitting edema, secondary to nephrotic range proteinuria or severe protein-losing colonic enteropathy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Smooth liver margin is a crucial negative physical exam differentiator in hepatosplenic schistosomiasis, where abdominal palpation reveals a smooth, firm liver edge devoid of cirrhotic macronodules despite massive portal hypertension.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urogenital schistosomiasis exhibits terminal-spined urine eggs on admission urine microscopy, identified via polycarbonate filter filtration of daytime urine (10:00 to 14:00) as large transparent ova (110-170 x 40-70 µm) with a sharp apical terminal spine pathognomonic of S. haematobium.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Intestinal schistosomiasis exhibits lateral-spined stool eggs on admission fecal examination, demonstrating large golden-brown oval ova (114-180 x 45-70 µm) equipped with a prominent, rigid lateral spine pathognomonic of Schistosoma mansoni.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Asian intestinal schistosomiasis exhibits lateral-knobbed stool eggs on admission microscopy, displaying small subglobular ova (70-100 x 50-70 µm) bearing an inconspicuous rudimentary lateral spine or knob characteristic of Schistosoma japonicum.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Acute Katayama schistosomiasis exhibits high peripheral eosinophilia on admission complete blood count, with eosinophils frequently exceeding 20% to 50% of the differential and absolute eosinophil counts exceeding 3,000 to 8,000 cells/µL.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Chronic schistosomiasis exhibits persistent chronic eosinophilia on admission CBC, typically displaying mild-to-moderate sustained eosinophilia of 5% to 15% (500 to 1,500 cells/µL) driven by continuous tissue egg deposition.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Schistosomiasis exhibits microcytic hypochromic anemia on admission laboratory triage, showing marked reductions in hemoglobin, hematocrit, and MCV (<80 fL) secondary to chronic unremitting blood loss in feces or urine.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis exhibits hypersplenism-induced thrombocytopenia on admission CBC, with platelet counts falling to 40,000-100,000/µL due to excessive splenic pooling and destruction in the massively enlarged spleen.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis exhibits hypersplenism-induced leukopenia on admission triage, displaying decreased total white blood cell counts secondary to splenic trapping without intrinsic bone marrow suppression.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urogenital schistosomiasis exhibits urinalysis microscopic hematuria on admission dipstick and sediment microscopy, identifying persistent microscopic red blood cells in >90% of active Schistosoma haematobium infections.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urogenital schistosomiasis exhibits urinalysis proteinuria on admission reagent test strips, reflecting local urothelial inflammatory exudation alongside potential schistosomal immune-complex glomerular basement membrane injury.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Intestinal schistosomiasis exhibits urine POC-CCA positivity on bedside rapid triage, where a lateral-flow cassette test detects gut proteoglycans of active adult Schistosoma mansoni worms in urine with high sensitivity within 20 minutes.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis exhibits normal serum albumin (>3.5-4.0 g/dL) on admission liver chemistry panels, confirming that hepatocellular protein synthetic capacity is preserved despite massive portal hypertension.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis exhibits a normal prothrombin time and normal INR on admission coagulation profiles, distinguishing pure presinusoidal schistosomal portal block from cirrhotic hepatocellular synthetic failure.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis exhibits normal serum bilirubin on admission liver panels, confirming the absence of hepatocellular necrosis or primary biliary obstruction in uncomplicated Symmers fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
