relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Chronic schistosomiasis exhibits polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia on serum protein electrophoresis, driven by sustained B-cell activation and antibody production against continuous parasitic tegumental and egg antigens.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Schistosomiasis exhibits markedly elevated serum IgE concentrations on admission serology, resulting from vigorous interleukin-4 and interleukin-13 stimulation characteristic of the host Th2 helminthic immune response.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Acute Katayama fever exhibits high levels of circulating immune complexes on admission immunological testing, correlating with severe serum sickness-like clinical manifestations including urticaria, fever, and pulmonary infiltrates.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Advanced urogenital schistosomiasis exhibits elevated serum creatinine on admission basic metabolic panels, indicating post-renal azotemia and renal parenchymal impairment caused by bilateral ureteric obstruction.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Chronic urogenital schistosomiasis exhibits elevated blood urea on admission biochemistry, reflecting decreased renal excretion secondary to chronic downstream ureterovesical outflow obstruction.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Early and travelers' schistosomiasis exhibits positive schistosome serology on admission laboratory evaluation, providing critical diagnostic confirmation before egg excretion commences or in low-burden non-immune individuals.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Schistosoma japonicum and mansoni infection exhibits positive stool miracidial hatching on specialized parasitological evaluation, where eggs hatch in deionized water under light, releasing motile miracidia visible to the naked eye.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Intestinal schistosomiasis exhibits rectal snip egg granulomas on fresh mucosal tissue exam, where an unstained rectal biopsy compressed between slides reveals embedded lateral-spined eggs and surrounding granulomatous reactions.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urogenital schistosomiasis exhibits bladder biopsy egg granulomas on histopathological examination, showing foreign body granulomas, multinucleated giant cells, and terminal-spined ova embedded in the submucosa.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis displays ultrasound periportal cuffing on bedside POCUS liver ultrasound, visualized as thickened, hyperreflective echogenic collars encircling intrahepatic portal vein branches (>4-6 mm wall thickness).

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis demonstrates the ultrasound pipestem sign on point-of-care abdominal imaging, characterized by thick echogenic collars resembling clay pipestems in longitudinal view and doughnuts in transverse view.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis displays main portal vein dilation on bedside abdominal ultrasound, with main trunk portal vein diameter measuring >12 to 14 mm secondary to chronic downstream intrahepatic vascular resistance.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis displays patent hepatic veins with normal triphasic Doppler flow on bedside ultrasound, confirming a presinusoidal lesion and definitively excluding Budd-Chiari post-hepatic venous outflow obstruction.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Urogenital schistosomiasis displays ultrasound bladder wall thickening on pelvic POCUS, where the bladder wall demonstrates irregular or concentric thickening >5 mm with loss of normal mucosal smoothness.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Urogenital schistosomiasis displays ultrasound bladder pseudopolyps on pelvic sonography, appearing as multiple hyperechoic exophytic nodular or polypoid masses projecting from the bladder floor into the lumen.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Urogenital schistosomiasis displays sonographic hydroureter on bedside urinary ultrasound, demonstrated as persistent fluid distension and tubular dilation of the ureteral lumen proximal to stenotic distal ureterovesical granulomas.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Urogenital schistosomiasis displays sonographic hydronephrosis on point-of-care renal ultrasound, identified by pelvicalyceal separation, caliceal clubbing, and cortical thinning from chronic retrograde urinary stasis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Chronic urogenital schistosomiasis displays bladder rim calcification on plain abdominal and pelvic radiographs, seen as a thin, curvilinear radio-opaque perimeter resembling the cranial outline of a fetal head.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Acute Katayama fever displays chest X-ray reticulonodular infiltrates on admission imaging, manifesting as bilateral diffuse interstitial and micronodular opacities corresponding to schistosomula pulmonary migration and immune pneumonitis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Spinal neuroschistosomiasis displays spinal MRI cord enlargement on neuroimaging, showing focal expansion, conus medullaris tumefaction, and hyperintense T2/STIR intramedullary signal intensity.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Spinal neuroschistosomiasis displays spinal MRI nodular enhancement on contrast-enhanced T1 sequences, demonstrating characteristic heterogeneous nodular and flame-shaped enhancement along the cauda equina and lower cord.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Cerebral neuroschistosomiasis displays brain CT hyperdense granulomas on unenhanced cranial imaging, showing small hyperdense punctate or nodular lesions with marked surrounding hypodense white-matter vasogenic edema.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Cerebral neuroschistosomiasis displays brain MRI ring enhancement on T1 contrast-enhanced imaging, characterized by multiple clustered ring-like and nodular enhancing granulomas with central necrotic or hypointense cores.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Intestinal schistosomiasis displays barium enema mucosal granularity on contrast radiography, presenting with fine mucosal irregularities, erosions, and multiple filling defects corresponding to inflammatory colonic pseudopolyps.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis requires exposure to infested freshwater immersion, where skin contact with lakes, rivers, or canals containing intermediate snail hosts permits free-swimming cercariae to initiate percutaneous infection.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis transmission is strongly associated with freshwater recreational swimming, where prolonged water immersion in warm, stagnant or slow-flowing lakes and streams exponentially increases cercarial penetration risk.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis transmission is driven by occupational agricultural wading, where farmers, irrigation canal maintainers, and rice workers endure daily unprotected lower-extremity immersion in infested irrigation waters.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis transmission is heavily promoted by freshwater artisanal fishing, where fishermen experience continuous repeated skin contact with snail-rich shorelines, leading to sustained high adult worm burdens.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis transmission frequently occurs through domestic water washing, where women and girls washing household clothes or collecting water along riverbanks suffer repeated cercarial skin penetration.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis is epidemiologically linked to sub-Saharan Africa endemicity, where poverty, inadequate water infrastructure, and widespread snail habitats result in more than 90% of the world's clinical bilharzia burden.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis transmission is classically anchored in the Nile River basin, where extensive irrigation canals, dams, and agricultural floodplains sustain high densities of Bulinus and Biomphalaria snails.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis japonica is epidemiologically linked to the Yangtze River basin, where seasonal marshland flooding around Dongting and Poyang lakes supports massive Oncomelania snail populations and bovine reservoirs.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis is epidemiologically linked to the Mekong River basin, where rocky river stretches in Cambodia and Laos support the specific intermediate host Neotricula aperta transmitting Schistosoma mekongi.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis is frequently acquired via Lake Malawi immersion, an internationally recognized tourist hotspot where eco-travelers engaging in swimming or scuba diving acquire acute urogenital bilharzia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis transmission is intensely prevalent across the Lake Victoria exposure zone, where dense lakeside communities experience severe hyperendemic transmission of Schistosoma mansoni.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosoma mansoni transmission strictly requires exposure to environments harboring the Biomphalaria snail host, which acts as the mandatory intermediate host for miracidial asexual replication and cercarial shedding.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosoma haematobium transmission strictly requires water bodies harboring the Bulinus snail host, an aquatic mollusc that releases infective fork-tailed cercariae into warm still or slow-flowing waters.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosoma japonicum transmission strictly depends on freshwater marshlands harboring the amphibious Oncomelania snail host, essential for larval replication and cercarial production in East Asia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Schistosomiasis infection is initiated via percutaneous cercarial penetration, where microscopic free-swimming cercariae shed by snails actively burrow through unbroken human epidermis using proteolytic glandular secretions.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Zoonotic Schistosoma japonicum utilizes the water buffalo reservoir as a major domestic mammalian amplifier, with a single infected buffalo producing millions of viable eggs daily to contaminate freshwater ecosystems.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] School-age children represent the quintessential high-risk host group for schistosomiasis, demonstrating the highest water contact frequencies, peak egg excretion loads, and highest rates of reinfection.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Non-immune international travelers represent a uniquely vulnerable host group who, upon first freshwater exposure, develop severe, stormy acute Katayama fever syndrome due to unmodulated immune-complex reactions.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Irrigation canal workers represent an occupational high-risk host group who suffer continuous daily water immersion, predisposing them to cumulative heavy worm burdens and early Symmers fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Schistosomiasis exhibits a cercarial dermatitis incubation period of just a few hours up to 48 hours post-immersion, during which initial cutaneous penetration triggers immediate local histamine release and itchy papules.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Acute schistosomiasis exhibits a Katayama syndrome incubation period of 2 to 8 weeks post-exposure, corresponding to the time required for migrating schistosomula to mature into paired adults and initiate oviposition.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Chronic schistosomiasis exhibits a prolonged incubation period ranging from months to 5-15 years, as cumulative granuloma formation and progressive tissue fibrosis gradually produce obstructive uropathy or Symmers fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Schistosomiasis is ruled out by zero freshwater contact, because transmission strictly requires cutaneous contact with natural freshwater bodies harboring snail intermediate hosts shedding infective cercariae.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Schistosomiasis is ruled out by exclusively saltwater immersion, because intermediate host snails (Biomphalaria, Bulinus, Oncomelania) cannot survive in marine saline environments or chlorinated municipal pools.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute Katayama schistosomiasis is ruled out by hyperacute 24-hour fever following water exposure, because schistosome maturation and oviposition-induced immune complex hypersensitivity require an obligatory 2 to 8 week incubation window.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute Katayama fever is ruled out by the absence of eosinophilia on admission CBC, because acute schistosomal immune-complex hypersensitivity uniformly provokes striking, intense peripheral blood eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Active urogenital Schistosoma haematobium infection is ruled out by negative urinalysis microhematuria across repeated test strips, as active mucosal egg extrusion produces detectable micro- or macrohematuria in >90-95% of patients.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Advanced urogenital schistosomiasis is ruled out by a normal bladder ultrasound, where normal wall thickness (<3 mm), smooth contours, and absence of hydroureter effectively exclude chronic schistosomal fibro-obstructive cystopathy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Urogenital schistosomiasis is ruled out by purulent urethral discharge, which indicates acute bacterial or sexually transmitted urethritis (Neisseria gonorrhoeae), as bilharzia causes hematuria and mucosal sandy patches without purulent exudates.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Schistosoma haematobium cystopathy is ruled out by early micturition hematuria (initial hematuria), which points to anterior urethral pathology rather than trigonal or bladder wall egg extrusion that characteristically produces terminal hematuria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Uncomplicated urogenital schistosomiasis is ruled out by continuous painful hematuria with severe flank colic, which typically indicates acute obstructing nephrolithiasis, renal papillary necrosis, or invasive renal parenchymal malignancy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Pure schistosomal hepatosplenic disease is ruled out by severe hepatocellular failure, because schistosomal Symmers fibrosis causes presinusoidal portal block while sparing lobular hepatocytes and maintaining normal hepatic synthetic function.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Schistosomal Symmers periportal fibrosis is ruled out by cirrhotic hepatic nodularity, which indicates true end-stage cirrhosis (viral or alcoholic) rather than the smooth capsule and periportal fibrous collaring of schistosomiasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Schistosomiasis in returned travelers is ruled out by negative schistosome serology at >=3 months post-exposure, as commercially validated antibody assays against egg and worm antigens demonstrate >95% sensitivity in non-endemic travelers.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Patent intestinal schistosomiasis is ruled out by negative Kato-Katz exams across multiple serial samples (>=3-4 distinct specimens), effectively excluding moderate-to-heavy Schistosoma mansoni or japonicum egg excretion.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Patent urogenital schistosomiasis is ruled out by negative midday urine filtrations across multiple consecutive days, as peak daytime excretion renders serial 10 mL polycarbonate membrane filtration highly sensitive.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Schistosomiasis is ruled out by rapid antibiotic response, because Schistosoma trematodes are intrinsically refractory to all antibacterial agents, and immediate defervescence indicates alternative bacterial infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute primary schistosomiasis is ruled out as the sole acute diagnosis by a positive blood bacterial culture, which establishes acute bacteremic sepsis or enteric typhoid fever as the primary cause of fever.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Advanced schistosomal portal hypertension as the cause of bleeding varices is ruled out by the absence of splenomegaly, because severe presinusoidal schistosomal block invariably induces prominent congestive splenomegaly.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Urogenital schistosomiasis is ruled out by isolated unilateral nephrolithiasis in the absence of bladder wall calcification, microhematuria, or travel history, establishing primary idiopathic urinary tract lithiasis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Hepatosplenic schistosomiasis is ruled out by diffuse intrahepatic duct dilation on imaging, which points to liver fluke disease (Clonorchis, Opisthorchis) or biliary tract obstruction, as schistosomiasis spares the biliary tree.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Advanced hepatosplenic schistosomiasis is ruled out by severe primary thrombocytosis, because portal congestion and splenic pooling characteristically produce moderate-to-severe thrombocytopenia rather than thrombocytosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute Katayama fever is ruled out by marked absolute neutrophilia with bandemia and zero eosinophils, which strongly points to acute invasive bacterial sepsis or pyogenic peritonitis rather than helminthic hypersensitivity.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Intestinal schistosomiasis is ruled out by acute watery secretory diarrhea without blood or mucus, as schistosomal gut disease typically causes chronic mucoid hematochezia, tenesmus, and colonic ulceration.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from bacterial urinary infection because bacterial UTI presents with dysuria throughout urination, significant pyuria, positive nitrite/leukocyte esterase, positive urine bacterial culture, and rapid clearance with antibiotics, whereas urogenital schistosomiasis causes painless terminal hematuria, eosinophilia, terminal-spined eggs, and total refractoriness to antibacterial therapy.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from urothelial bladder carcinoma because transitional cell carcinoma occurs in older smokers with continuous gross hematuria and papillary exophytic lesions without mural calcification, whereas schistosomal bladder cancer occurs in younger exposed patients, demonstrates squamous histology, exhibits bladder rim calcification, and reveals terminal-spined eggs on biopsy.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from decompensated hepatic cirrhosis because true cirrhosis features diffuse parenchymal nodularity, small shrunken liver, impaired hepatocellular synthesis (hypoalbuminemia, prolonged PT/INR, jaundice, asterixis), whereas hepatosplenic schistosomiasis causes pure presinusoidal portal block with normal liver synthetic function, smooth liver contours, and ultrasound pipestem fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from acute malaria because malaria exhibits intraerythrocytic parasites on Giemsa blood smears, severe thrombocytopenia without eosinophilia, hemolytic anemia, and rapid defervescence with artemisinins, whereas acute schistosomiasis (Katayama) features urticaria, marked eosinophilia (>20-50%), negative malaria films, and responds to corticosteroids.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) because kala-azar causes chronic undulating fevers, profound pancytopenia without eosinophilia, and intracellular Leishman-Donovan amastigotes on bone marrow aspirate, whereas hepatosplenic schistosomiasis is afebrile, features peripheral eosinophilia, and exhibits Symmers periportal fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from enteric typhoid fever because typhoid features step-ladder fever, relative bradycardia (Faget sign), rose spots, neutropenia without eosinophilia, and positive blood cultures for Salmonella enterica, whereas acute Katayama schistosomiasis displays urticaria, prominent cough, striking eosinophilia, and negative bacterial cultures.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from acute viral hepatitis because viral hepatitis causes marked hepatocellular necrosis with massive transaminase elevations (ALT/AST >1,000 U/L), direct hyperbilirubinemia, and positive viral serologies, whereas schistosomiasis causes mild transaminitis, normal bilirubin, marked eosinophilia, and ultrasound periportal collaring.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from amebic colitis because amebiasis produces discrete flask-shaped colonic ulcers, trophozoites with ingested erythrocytes on wet mount, positive stool amebic antigen, and responds to metronidazole, whereas intestinal schistosomiasis reveals lateral-spined eggs on stool Kato-Katz and responds to praziquantel.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from amebic liver abscess because amebic abscess presents with high fever, right upper quadrant pain, a focal cystic necrotic cavity on ultrasound containing chocolate-brown 'anchovy-sauce' pus, and positive amebic serology, whereas schistosomiasis displays diffuse periportal pipestem fibrosis without discrete abscess cavities.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from inflammatory bowel disease because Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis lack parasitic ova, display crypt architectural distortion and continuous mucosal friability on biopsy, and require immunosuppression, whereas schistosomal colitis shows viable lateral-spined eggs in mucosal snips and resolves with praziquantel.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from renal tuberculosis because genitourinary TB presents with sterile pyuria, acidic urine, positive acid-fast bacilli on urine culture/GeneXpert, and beaded ureters on urography, whereas urogenital schistosomiasis causes painless terminal hematuria, eosinophiluria, and terminal-spined eggs on urine filtration.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from acute leptospirosis because leptospirosis produces intense bilateral conjunctival suffusion, severe gastrocnemius calf tenderness, elevated creatine kinase, and positive microscopic agglutination testing, whereas acute schistosomiasis lacks conjunctival suffusion and features prominent peripheral eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from acute dengue fever because dengue has a short incubation (3-7 days), presents with retro-orbital headache, breakbone arthralgias, severe leukopenia, hemoconcentration, and positive NS1 antigen without eosinophilia, whereas Katayama fever has a 2-8 week incubation and striking eosinophilia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis (EGPA) because EGPA is an autoimmune necrotizing vasculitis presenting with adult-onset asthma, peripheral neuropathy (mononeuritis multiplex), and positive p-ANCA antibodies, whereas acute schistosomiasis follows freshwater exposure, lacks p-ANCA, and resolves after praziquantel.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from fascioliasis because Fasciola is acquired via ingestion of raw aquatic plants (watercress) and displays hypodense branching parenchymal tunnels on CT and large unspined operculated eggs on stool exam, whereas schistosomiasis is acquired percutaneously and displays periportal pipestem fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from clonorchiasis because Clonorchis infection results from eating raw cyprinid fish, parasitizes intrahepatic bile ducts causing biliary dilatation and recurrent cholangitis, whereas schistosomiasis is acquired percutaneously, parasitizes mesenteric/vesical venules, spares bile ducts, and causes portal fibrosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from multiple sclerosis because spinal MS features central demyelination with oligoclonal bands in CSF and periventricular white matter Dawson's fingers on brain MRI, whereas spinal neuroschistosomiasis causes acute transverse myelitis at T11-L1 with peripheral eosinophilia and responds to praziquantel.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from cerebral high-grade glioma because glioblastoma presents as an infiltrating, solitary, necrotic malignant mass with butterfly spread across the corpus callosum on MRI, whereas cerebral schistosomiasis japonica produces multiple clustered nodular granulomas with eosinophilia that regress with corticosteroids and praziquantel.

entities.name: Scrub Typhus
entities.description: Acute life-threatening zoonotic febrile illness caused by Orientia tsutsugamushi and transmitted by larval trombiculid mites (chiggers), characterized by disseminated endothelial microvascular infection, perivascular cuffing vasculitis, and potential multiorgan failure.

entities.name: Acute Febrile Illness
entities.description: Abrupt onset of high spiking remittent or continuous fever (39-40.5 C) accompanied by violent chills and prostration.

entities.name: Noncardiogenic Pulmonary Edema
entities.description: Extravasation of fluid into alveolar spaces secondary to systemic endothelial permeability breakdown without elevated capillary wedge pressure.

entities.name: Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome
entities.description: Severe life-threatening hypoxemic respiratory failure characterized by bilateral diffuse alveolar infiltrates and refractory hypoxia.

entities.name: Interstitial Pneumonitis
entities.description: Mononuclear inflammatory cell infiltration and perivascular cuffing within pulmonary interalveolar septa.

entities.name: Acute Kidney Injury
entities.description: Rapid decline in glomerular filtration rate with rising serum creatinine and oliguria secondary to septic vasculitis.

entities.name: Acute Tubular Necrosis
entities.description: Destruction of renal tubular epithelial cells induced by severe ischemic hypoperfusion and systemic microcirculatory collapse.

entities.name: Acute Interstitial Nephritis
entities.description: Direct peritubular capillary vasculitis and lymphocytic infiltration within the renal parenchymal interstitium.

entities.name: Aseptic Meningoencephalitis
entities.description: Central nervous system infection causing encephalic dysfunction, altered consciousness, delirium, and meningismus.

entities.name: Aseptic Meningitis
entities.description: Inflammatory irritation of the leptomeninges without pyogenic bacteria, causing headache, photophobia, and positive meningeal signs.

entities.name: Encephalopathy
entities.description: Global brain dysfunction presenting with drowsiness, psychomotor agitation, confusion, or coma.

entities.name: Infectious Myocarditis
entities.description: Inflammation of cardiac myocytes and myocardial interstitial microvasculature leading to arrhythmias and systolic impairment.

entities.name: Cardiogenic Shock
entities.description: Severe circulatory failure caused by depressed intrinsic myocardial contractility and left ventricular pump failure.

entities.name: Septic Shock
entities.description: Persistent arterial hypotension requiring vasopressors to maintain MAP >= 65 mmHg despite adequate fluid resuscitation.

entities.name: Multiorgan Dysfunction Syndrome
entities.description: Simultaneous progressive physiological failure of multiple vital organ systems resulting from systemic microvascular angiitis.

entities.name: Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation
entities.description: Systemic consumptive coagulopathy characterized by microvascular thrombosis, thrombocytopenia, and bleeding diathesis.

entities.name: Acute Pericarditis
entities.description: Inflammation of the pericardial sac layers producing positional retrosternal chest pain and pericardial friction rubs.

entities.name: Pericardial Effusion
entities.description: Accumulation of exudative fluid within the pericardial cavity secondary to serosal endothelial permeability leak.

entities.name: Generalized Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlargement of multiple non-contiguous peripheral lymph node basins across cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions.

entities.name: Splenomegaly
entities.description: Pathological enlargement of the spleen resulting from lymphoid hyperplasia and reticuloendothelial clearance of infected cells.

entities.name: Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlargement of the liver caused by sinusoidal endothelial swelling, Kupffer cell activation, and perivascular inflammation.

entities.name: Acute Hepatitis
entities.description: Hepatic inflammation characterized by sinusoidal endothelial infection, focal hepatocyte necrosis, and elevated transaminases.

entities.name: Canalicular Cholestasis
entities.description: Impairment of bile excretion secondary to periportal inflammation and sinusoidal endothelial swelling.

entities.name: Gastrointestinal Mucosal Hemorrhage
entities.description: Extensive bleeding from the stomach or intestine caused by submucosal vasculitis, petechiae, and mucosal ulcerations.

entities.name: Multiple Gastric Ulcers
entities.description: Diffuse shallow mucosal erosions and ulcerations throughout the gastric mucosa identified on endoscopy.

entities.name: Acute Pancreatitis
entities.description: Acute inflammation of the pancreas marked by elevated serum amylase/lipase and severe epigastric pain.

entities.name: Severe Frontal Cephalalgia
entities.description: Excruciating, incapacitating frontal or retro-orbital headache caused by cerebral endothelial activation and intracranial vasculitis.

entities.name: Retro-Orbital Pain
entities.description: Deep aching orbital discomfort aggravated by eye movement secondary to local ocular microvascular inflammation.

entities.name: Generalized Myalgia
entities.description: Widespread muscle aches, tenderness, and stiffness involving the back, neck, thighs, and calves.

entities.name: Peripheral Polyneuropathy
entities.description: Peripheral nerve trunk dysfunction caused by ischemia of the vasa nervorum secondary to systemic vasculitis.

entities.name: Acute Transient Deafness
entities.description: Sudden onset of reversible bilateral or unilateral sensorineural hearing impairment.

entities.name: Tinnitus
entities.description: Subjective sensation of ringing, buzzing, or hissing sound in the ears accompanying cochlear microvasculitis.

entities.name: Cranial Nerve Palsy
entities.description: Peripheral cranial nerve dysfunction, most frequently involving cranial nerves VII, VI, or VIII.

entities.name: Cerebral Angiitis
entities.description: Inflammation and mononuclear cuffing of cerebral microvessels and arterioles.

entities.name: Generalized Seizures
entities.description: Paroxysmal motor convulsive activity provoked by severe cortical inflammation, cerebral edema, or high fever.

entities.name: Oliguria
entities.description: Marked reduction in daily urinary output (<400 mL/day or <0.5 mL/kg/h) signaling severe renal impairment.

entities.name: Pleuritic Chest Pain
entities.description: Sharp thoracic pain intensified by inspiration, coughing, or deep breathing secondary to pleural inflammation.

entities.name: Exudative Pleural Effusion
entities.description: Protein-rich fluid accumulation in the pleural space caused by increased pulmonary microvascular permeability.

entities.name: Hypovolemic Hypotension
entities.description: Depressed blood pressure resulting from extensive plasma extravasation into extravascular compartments.

entities.name: Metabolic Lactic Acidosis
entities.description: Elevated blood lactate (>2.0-4.0 mmol/L) with acidemia resulting from inadequate tissue microcirculatory oxygen delivery.

entities.name: Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis
entities.description: Life-threatening hyperinflammatory cytokine storm syndrome characterized by uncontrolled macrophage activation and hemophagocytosis.

entities.name: Necrotic Black Eschar
entities.description: Pathognomonic skin crust resembling a cigarette burn with a black necrotic center surrounded by an erythematous halo.

entities.name: Groin Cutaneous Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic black cigarette-burn crust located in the inguinal crease, scrotum, or perineum.

entities.name: Axillary Inoculation Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic feeding lesion located deep within the moist axillary skin folds.

entities.name: Inframammary Fold Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic black chigger feeding crust concealed under the breast tissue along brassiere compression lines.

entities.name: Waistband Inoculation Eschar
entities.description: Necrotic cutaneous crust located around the beltline, umbilical fold, or lower abdomen.

entities.name: Perineal Inoculation Eschar
entities.description: Painless necrotic black crust situated on the perineal or perianal skin folds.

entities.name: Regional Tender Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Painful, tender enlargement of the sentinel lymph node chain anatomically draining the cutaneous eschar.

entities.name: Sensorineural Hearing Loss
entities.description: Acute reversible cochlear or acoustic nerve sensory hearing deficit appearing during acute infection.

entities.name: Centrifugal Maculopapular Exanthem
entities.description: Transient erythematous maculopapular rash developing on the trunk and spreading centrifugally to limbs.

entities.name: Bulbar Conjunctival Suffusion
entities.description: Prominent bilateral bulbar conjunctival erythema and vascular engorgement without purulent discharge.

entities.name: Subconjunctival Hemorrhage
entities.description: Focal scleral extravasation of blood resulting from severe microvascular capillary disruption.

entities.name: Relative Bradycardia
entities.description: Pulse-temperature dissociation (Faget sign) where pulse rate is inappropriately low for the degree of fever.

entities.name: Meningismus
entities.description: Clinical signs of meningeal irritation including nuchal rigidity, Kernig sign, and Brudzinski sign.

entities.name: Palpable Splenic Tip
entities.description: Soft, slightly tender splenic margin palpated beneath the left costal margin on deep inspiration.

entities.name: Tender Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Enlarged liver with smooth edge exhibiting tenderness on manual palpation.

entities.name: Facial Flushing
entities.description: Prominent plethoric erythema over the cheeks, forehead, and periorbital tissues during early high fever.

entities.name: Cutaneous Petechiae
entities.description: Non-blanching pinpoint intradermal hemorrhages on the trunk and extremities reflecting microvascular fragility.

entities.name: Fine Basilar Crackles
entities.description: High-pitched end-inspiratory crackles auscultated over the lower posterior lung fields.

entities.name: Postauricular Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Enlarged, tender lymph nodes located behind the mastoid process.

entities.name: Inguinal Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Painful, tender enlargement of superficial inguinal lymph nodes in the groin basin.

entities.name: Erythematous Maculopapular Papule
entities.description: Initial painless, non-pruritic erythematous papule or vesicle marking the early chigger feeding site.

entities.name: Altered Mental Status
entities.description: Acute delirium, confusion, psychomotor slowing, or obtundation during high-grade fever.

entities.name: Peripheral Edema
entities.description: Pitting edema involving the pretibial regions and ankles resulting from hypoalbuminemia and capillary leak.

entities.name: Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Yellow discoloration of the sclera indicating elevated conjugated and total bilirubin.

entities.name: Tachypnea
entities.description: Elevated respiratory rate (>20-24 breaths/minute) signaling respiratory distress or metabolic compensation.

entities.name: Dry Cough
entities.description: Persistent non-productive cough reflecting bronchial perivascular inflammation.

entities.name: Resting Tachycardia
entities.description: Inappropriate heart rate elevation (>100 bpm) at rest signaling sepsis compensation or myocarditis.

entities.name: Hypotensive Shock
entities.description: Severe drop in systolic blood pressure (<90 mmHg) accompanied by cold clammy extremities.

entities.name: Mild Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: White blood cell count mildly elevated between 10,000 and 14,000/uL with neutrophilic predominance.

entities.name: Normal Leukocyte Count
entities.description: Total white blood cell count within normal reference range (4,000-10,000/uL) despite high fever.

entities.name: Prominent Bandemia
entities.description: Presence of immature non-segmented neutrophils (band forms >10%) on manual differential blood count.

entities.name: Moderate Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count depressed between 50,000 and 100,000/uL on admission complete blood count.

entities.name: Severe Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count severely depressed below 30,000-50,000/uL indicating multiorgan microvascular failure.

entities.name: Moderate Transaminitis
entities.description: Serum AST and ALT elevations 2- to 5-fold above the upper limit of normal.

entities.name: Disproportionate AST Elevation
entities.description: Serum aspartate aminotransferase level exceeding alanine aminotransferase level (AST/ALT ratio > 1).

entities.name: Elevated Alkaline Phosphatase
entities.description: Mild-to-moderate elevation of serum alkaline phosphatase (1.5- to 3-fold ULN).

entities.name: Mild Conjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Total bilirubin elevated between 1.5 and 4.0 mg/dL with direct fraction predominance.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Serum creatinine elevated above baseline (>1.4-2.0 mg/dL) at initial admission triage.

entities.name: Elevated Blood Urea
entities.description: Blood urea nitrogen elevated above normal limits reflecting acute azotemia and tissue catabolism.

entities.name: Hypoalbuminemia
entities.description: Serum albumin depressed below 3.0-3.5 g/dL resulting from systemic capillary hyperpermeability.

entities.name: Elevated C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: Serum C-reactive protein markedly increased (>50-100 mg/L) at hospital presentation.

entities.name: Elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation
entities.description: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate elevated above 40-60 mm/hr indicating acute vascular inflammation.

entities.name: Extreme Hyperferritinemia
entities.description: Serum ferritin level markedly elevated above 1,000-5,000 ng/mL.

entities.name: Elevated Serum Lactate
entities.description: Arterial or venous lactate elevated (>2.0-4.0 mmol/L) reflecting microcirculatory hypoperfusion.

entities.name: Elevated Creatine Kinase
entities.description: Serum creatine phosphokinase elevated above normal limits indicating myopathic injury.

entities.name: Elevated Troponin T
entities.description: Cardiac troponin I or T detectable or elevated above reference cutoffs.

entities.name: Prolonged Prothrombin Time
entities.description: Prothrombin time / INR elevated beyond reference limits indicating coagulopathy.

entities.name: Elevated D-Dimer
entities.description: Serum D-dimer markedly increased reflecting fibrin degradation and microvascular thrombosis.

entities.name: Microscopic Hematuria
entities.description: Urinalysis demonstrating microscopic red blood cells (>5 RBCs/high-power field).

entities.name: Mild Proteinuria
entities.description: Urinary dipstick protein 1+ to 2+ (30 to 100 mg/dL) without gross nephrotic range loss.

entities.name: Granular Urinary Casts
entities.description: Muddy brown coarse granular casts on urinary sediment examination.

entities.name: CSF Lymphocytic Pleocytosis
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid white cell count mildly elevated (10-100 cells/uL) with mononuclear predominance.

entities.name: Elevated CSF Protein
entities.description: Cerebrospinal fluid protein elevated between 60 and 200 mg/dL.

entities.name: Rapid Defervescence Response
entities.description: Complete fever defervescence and symptomatic resolution occurring within 24 to 48 hours of starting doxycycline.

entities.name: Reticulonodular Interstitial Infiltrates
entities.description: Chest radiography showing bilateral reticular and fine reticulonodular interstitial opacities.

entities.name: Bilateral Basal Infiltrates
entities.description: Chest radiography demonstrating bibasilar patchy airspace opacities and peribronchovascular thickening.

entities.name: Kerley B Lines
entities.description: Horizontal peripheral linear septal opacities at the lateral lung bases on plain chest radiograph.

entities.name: Bilateral Pleural Effusions
entities.description: Blunting of bilateral costophrenic sulci on chest radiography or fluid stripes on ultrasound.

entities.name: POCUS Splenomegaly
entities.description: Bedside point-of-care ultrasound confirming spleen bipolar length greater than 12 cm.

entities.name: POCUS Hepatomegaly
entities.description: Bedside sonographic confirmation of liver craniocaudal dimension exceeding 15 cm with normal echotexture.

entities.name: Acalculous Gallbladder Thickening
entities.description: Bedside ultrasound showing gallbladder wall edema (>3 mm) without intraluminal calculi or sludge.

entities.name: Ground-Glass Opacities
entities.description: High-resolution chest CT showing bilateral patchy ground-glass attenuation without architectural distortion.

entities.name: Interlobular Septal Thickening
entities.description: Chest CT imaging demonstrating smooth interstitial septal thickening throughout dependent pulmonary zones.

entities.name: Preserved Biliary Ducts
entities.description: Bedside abdominal sonography confirming normal caliber of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts.

entities.name: Diffuse Myocardial Hypokinesia
entities.description: Bedside echocardiography revealing global left ventricular systolic dysfunction without focal wall motion defects.

entities.name: Minimal Pericardial Effusion
entities.description: Echocardiographic detection of a small circumferential fluid layer without hemodynamic chamber collapse.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium Mite Larva
entities.description: Microscopic six-legged larval stage of trombiculid mites (chiggers), the exclusive vector and reservoir.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium deliense
entities.description: Predominant species of trombiculid mite vector responsible for transmission in tropical Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium akamushi
entities.description: Classical mite vector species distributed across Japan and temperate East Asia.

entities.name: Leptotrombidium fletcheri
entities.description: Trombiculid mite vector species adapted to rubber plantations and tropical secondary vegetation.

entities.name: Secondary Scrub Vegetation
entities.description: Regrowth brush, grassland, and transitional scrub forming localized focal 'scrub typhus islands'.

entities.name: Tsutsugamushi Triangle
entities.description: Vast geographic endemic zone encompassing Asia-Pacific, from Pakistan to Japan and northern Australia.

entities.name: Agricultural Rice Fields
entities.description: Cultivated wet or dry paddy fields serving as common sites for chigger bite exposure during farming.

entities.name: Overgrown Riverbanks
entities.description: Moist riparian vegetation along streams and irrigation ditches supporting high chigger larval density.

entities.name: Monsoon Season
entities.description: Annual period of heavy rainfall and high humidity that promotes larval chigger emergence.

entities.name: Deforested Land Clearings
entities.description: Cleared forest margins undergoing secondary vegetative regrowth where mite colonies proliferate.

entities.name: Wild Rodent Reservoirs
entities.description: Small field mammals (Rattus and Apodemus species) that serve as hosts for chigger feeding and maintenance.

entities.name: Agricultural Field Workers
entities.description: Farmers, planters, and weeders working in close direct physical contact with scrub vegetation.

entities.name: Military Field Troops
entities.description: Armed forces personnel undergoing field bivouacking, tactical maneuvers, or jungle patrols.

entities.name: Forestry Laborers
entities.description: Loggers, woodcutters, and forest rangers entering dense secondary brush and woodland areas.

entities.name: Outdoor Recreational Campers
entities.description: Hikers, campers, and trekkers sitting, resting, or sleeping on bare ground or grassy clearings.

entities.name: Rural Endemic Inhabitants
entities.description: Long-term residents of rural villages bordering bushland, riverbanks, or unmanaged scrub vegetation.

entities.name: Squatting Agricultural Posture
entities.description: Working in a low squatting position in dry fields, which brings groin and waistline close to soil.

entities.name: Elderly Rural Populations
entities.description: Older rural individuals who experience higher disease severity, complications, and mortality.

entities.name: Pregnant Women
entities.description: Expectant mothers infected during pregnancy at risk for preterm birth, miscarriage, and maternal morbidity.

entities.name: Ten-Day Incubation Period
entities.description: Typical median incubation interval of 10 to 12 days between chigger bite inoculation and acute fever.

entities.name: Six-Day Minimal Incubation
entities.description: Shortest documented incubation timeframe of 6 days following high-inoculum chigger bite.

entities.name: Twenty-One-Day Maximal Incubation
entities.description: Upper clinical latency boundary of 21 days from rural chigger exposure to acute fever onset.

entities.name: Zero Human Transmission
entities.description: Absence of direct person-to-person spread via respiratory droplets, bodily fluids, or casual contact.

entities.name: Doxycycline Refractoriness
entities.description: Persistence of high fever beyond 48 to 72 hours of therapeutic oral or IV doxycycline.

entities.name: Azithromycin Refractoriness
entities.description: Failure of clinical improvement within 72 hours of appropriate therapeutic azithromycin administration.

entities.name: Profound Leukopenia
entities.description: Marked reduction in total white blood cell count (<3,000/uL) typical of severe acute arboviral infection.

entities.name: Critical Phase Hemoconcentration
entities.description: Rapid rise in hematocrit >= 20% coinciding with fever defervescence, hallmark of dengue plasma leakage.

entities.name: Purulent Cutaneous Ulcer
entities.description: Skin ulceration producing gross pus, fluctuance, or foul exudate incompatible with dry rickettsial eschar.

entities.name: Gross Pyuria
entities.description: Urine filled with clumps of neutrophils and bacterial rods (>10^5 CFU/mL) indicating bacterial UTI.

entities.name: Intraerythrocytic Parasitemia
entities.description: Microscopic visualization of Plasmodium ring forms, trophozoites, or schizonts in peripheral blood smear.

entities.name: Extreme Direct Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia (>15-25 mg/dL) with deep bronze icterus typical of severe Weil disease.

entities.name: Absence Endemic Exposure
entities.description: Zero lifetime travel or residence in known scrub typhus endemic geographic regions or rural brush habitats.

entities.name: Gram-Positive Blood Bacteremia
entities.description: Automated blood culture positivity yielding staphylococci, streptococci, or enterococci within 24-48 hours.

entities.name: Cavitary Pulmonary Lesions
entities.description: Thick-walled cavitary lesions or necrotic lung breakdown on plain chest radiograph or CT imaging.

entities.name: Centripetal Vesicular Rash
entities.description: Pruritic exanthem appearing in successive crops of teardrop vesicles on an erythematous base (varicella pattern).

entities.name: Prominent Splenic Infarction
entities.description: Wedge-shaped hypoechoic splenic parenchymal infarction on abdominal ultrasound or contrast-enhanced CT.

entities.name: Immediate One-Day Incubation
entities.description: Fever and constitutional symptoms developing within less than 24 to 48 hours of initial outdoor brush exposure.

entities.name: Prolonged Multi-Month Incubation
entities.description: Latency period exceeding 30 to 60 days between rural travel return and acute febrile illness onset.

entities.name: Purulent Conjunctival Discharge
entities.description: Copious thick yellow or green purulent ocular drainage and crusting of the eyelids.

entities.name: Marked Generalized Lymphadenopathy Absence
entities.description: Complete absence of lymph node enlargement in a patient presenting with high fever and non-specific rash.

entities.name: Isolated Unconjugated Hyperbilirubinemia
entities.description: Elevated indirect bilirubin with normal direct bilirubin and normal liver transaminases.

entities.name: Beta-Lactam Responsiveness
entities.description: Rapid clinical cure and fever defervescence following administration of ampicillin, ceftriaxone, or meropenem.

entities.name: Fluoroquinolone Responsiveness
entities.description: Prompt resolution of fever within 24-48 hours of ciprofloxacin or levofloxacin monotherapy.

entities.name: Marked Eosinophilia
entities.description: Absolute eosinophil count >1,500/uL on differential complete blood count.

entities.name: Normal C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: Serum C-reactive protein within strictly normal limits (<5 mg/L) during severe acute febrile illness.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Mosquito-borne arboviral illness characterized by retro-orbital pain, leukopenia, and defervescence plasma leak.

entities.name: Severe Dengue
entities.description: Severe dengue virus infection marked by plasma leakage, severe hemorrhage, shock, and pleural effusions at defervescence.

entities.name: Leptospirosis
entities.description: Zoonotic spirochetal infection transmitted by rodent urine in floodwaters, causing severe calf pain and jaundice.

entities.name: Severe Leptospirosis
entities.description: Weil disease presenting with catastrophic triad of deep jaundice, oliguric renal failure, and pulmonary hemorrhage.

entities.name: Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Protozoan infection caused by Plasmodium falciparum, characterized by cyclic paroxysms and intraerythrocytic rings.

entities.name: Vivax Malaria
entities.description: Benign tertian malaria caused by Plasmodium vivax presenting with 48-hour paroxysmal rigors and splenomegaly.

entities.name: Murine Typhus
entities.description: Flea-borne rickettsiosis caused by Rickettsia typhi associated with commensal rats in urban and port environments.

entities.name: Typhoid Fever
entities.description: Enteric fever caused by Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi presenting with stepladder fever and rose spots.

entities.name: Melioidosis
entities.description: Saprophytic environmental bacterial infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei in tropical soils.

entities.name: Spotted Fever Rickettsiosis
entities.description: Tick-borne rickettsial disease caused by Rickettsia rickettsii or R. conorii presenting with centripetal petechiae.

entities.name: Infectious Mononucleosis
entities.description: Epstein-Barr virus infection presenting with exudative tonsillopharyngitis, fatigue, and atypical lymphocytosis.

entities.name: Primary HIV Infection
entities.description: Acute retroviral seroconversion illness presenting with fever, maculopapular rash, and painful aphthous ulcers.

entities.name: Meningococcal Disease
entities.description: Fulminant invasive Neisseria meningitidis infection causing purpura fulminans and purulent meningitis.

entities.name: Japanese Encephalitis
entities.description: Mosquito-borne flavivirus causing acute encephalitis with parkinsonian features and thalamic lesions.

entities.name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia
entities.description: Bacterial lung parenchyma infection typically caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae with lobar consolidation.

entities.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
entities.description: Rodent-borne viral zoonosis causing rapid noncardiogenic pulmonary edema with immunoblasts and hemoconcentration.

entities.name: Cutaneous Anthrax
entities.description: Zoonotic infection caused by Bacillus anthracis spores presenting with painless black eschar and massive gelatinous edema.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute febrile illness presents abruptly with high remittent or continuous fever, rigors, and debilitating constitutional prostration.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Noncardiogenic pulmonary edema arises from diffuse microvascular capillary leakage and endothelial injury in the pulmonary circulation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute respiratory distress syndrome develops during the second week of untreated illness due to catastrophic alveolar-capillary barrier breakdown.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Interstitial pneumonitis manifests with non-productive cough, tachypnea, and fine bilateral crepitations caused by septal endothelial inflammation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute kidney injury occurs in 20-40% of hospitalized patients due to a combination of renal hypoperfusion and microvascular endothelial injury.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute tubular necrosis complicates severe scrub typhus shock, causing oliguric renal failure with characteristic granular muddy brown casts.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute interstitial nephritis represents direct Orientia-mediated peritubular endothelial inflammation leading to sterile pyuria and azotemia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Aseptic meningoencephalitis presents with neck stiffness, headache, confusion, and lymphocytic cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Aseptic meningitis results from microvascular leptomeningeal inflammation manifesting with nuchal rigidity and mononuclear CSF pleocytosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Encephalopathy occurs in severe scrub typhus secondary to cerebral microvascular perivascular cuffing and toxic cytokine release.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Infectious myocarditis manifests with chest discomfort, conduction abnormalities, sinus tachycardia, or cardiogenic shock.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cardiogenic shock complicates fulminant scrub typhus myocarditis, leading to hypotension refractory to fluid administration.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Septic shock develops in severe disseminated vasculitis due to profound systemic vasodilatation and capillary leakage.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Multiorgan dysfunction syndrome combines pulmonary, renal, hepatic, and hematological failure, carrying high untreated mortality.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Disseminated intravascular coagulation results from widespread endothelial injury, presenting with petechiae, mucosal bleeding, and prolonged PT/INR.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute pericarditis arises from serosal microvascular involvement and can accompany infectious myocarditis as perimyocarditis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pericardial effusion is detectable on bedside echocardiography as an anechoic fluid stripe in up to 10-25% of complicated cases.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Generalized lymphadenopathy reflects systemic reticuloendothelial proliferation following initial localized sentinel node enlargement.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Splenomegaly is present in 30-50% of patients and is readily identified by palpation or bedside ultrasound.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hepatomegaly manifests as a smooth, tender liver edge palpable 2 to 4 cm below the right costal margin.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute hepatitis develops in over 80% of scrub typhus cases, causing mild-to-moderate transaminase elevations and mild hepatomegaly.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Canalicular cholestasis presents with mild conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and elevated serum alkaline phosphatase without biliary dilation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Gastrointestinal mucosal hemorrhage occurs in severe scrub typhus manifesting as hematemesis, melena, or occult fecal blood loss.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Multiple gastric ulcers develop secondary to microvascular thrombosis and mucosal ischemia in severe systemic infection.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute pancreatitis occurs rarely as a manifestation of peripancreatic microvascular ischemia and systemic endothelial inflammation.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Severe frontal cephalalgia is nearly universal (90-95%) in acute scrub typhus, often described as throbbing and resistant to common analgesics.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Retro-orbital pain accompanies acute cephalalgia and conjunctival suffusion during the early bacteremic phase.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Generalized myalgia reflects diffuse intramuscular capillary angiitis and systemic cytokine release.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Peripheral polyneuropathy presents as symmetrical sensory loss, paresthesias, or motor weakness during prolonged or convalescent disease.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Acute transient deafness develops in 20-35% of scrub typhus patients due to eighth cranial nerve or cochlear microvasculitis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Tinnitus serves as a valuable early diagnostic clue preceding or accompanying sensorineural hearing loss in scrub typhus.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cranial nerve palsy can manifest as facial nerve paresis, abducens palsy, or auditory impairment resulting from focal microvascular ischemia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Cerebral angiitis leads to focal neurological deficits, confusion, and localized ischemic brain changes on neuroimaging.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Generalized seizures can occur in pediatric or severe adult cases complicated by acute meningoencephalitis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Oliguria indicates worsening acute kidney injury and hypoperfusion in patients developing multiorgan failure.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Pleuritic chest pain arises from localized pleuritis and peripheral pulmonary interstitial infiltrates.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Exudative pleural effusion frequently accompanies interstitial pneumonitis in scrub typhus, appearing bilaterally or unilaterally.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hypovolemic hypotension reflects profound capillary leakage and hypoalbuminemia before full septic shock ensues.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Metabolic lactic acidosis serves as a hallmark of severe microvascular hypoperfusion and impending cardiovascular collapse.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis is a recognized severe complication manifested by bicytopenia, extreme hyperferritinemia, and splenomegaly.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] The pathognomonic necrotic black eschar at the chigger feeding site confirms scrub typhus with high diagnostic specificity.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Groin cutaneous eschar is the most common anatomical site in male patients, requiring diligent genital examination.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Axillary inoculation eschar represents a primary feeding site, especially frequent in children and women.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Inframammary fold eschar is a classic presentation in adult female patients along tight clothing boundaries.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Waistband inoculation eschar occurs where clothing constriction impedes chigger migration, inducing bite site feeding.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Perineal inoculation eschar is frequently overlooked unless a systematic, whole-body skin exam is conducted.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Regional tender lymphadenopathy draining the primary eschar site appears early and guides detection of hidden lesions.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Sensorineural hearing loss occurring in an acute febrile illness is an invaluable pathognomonic diagnostic clue for scrub typhus.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Centrifugal maculopapular exanthem appears on days 4 to 6 on the trunk, spreading outward and fading within several days.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Bulbar conjunctival suffusion without purulence reflects ocular microvascular endothelial dilation and occurs in >50% of patients.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Subconjunctival hemorrhage frequently accompanies acute conjunctival suffusion and photophobia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Relative bradycardia is observed in a subset of scrub typhus patients during sustained high temperature.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Meningismus indicates leptomeningeal inflammation, signaling CNS involvement that mandates CSF analysis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Palpable splenic tip reflects acute reticuloendothelial lymphoid expansion during systemic bacteremic dissemination.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Tender hepatomegaly is palpable below the right costal margin, correlating with acute hepatitis and sinusoidal inflammation.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Facial flushing accompanied by conjunctival injection gives the characteristic toxic typhus facies in early disease.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Cutaneous petechiae indicate underlying microvascular endothelial leakage and progressive thrombocytopenia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Fine basilar crackles indicate interstitial pulmonary edema and inflammatory septal thickening.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Postauricular lymphadenopathy acts as a regional sentinel node when the chigger bite is located on the scalp or neck.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Inguinal lymphadenopathy is prominent when the primary eschar is located on the lower extremities, perineum, or genitalia.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Erythematous maculopapular papule precedes necrotic crusting and ulceration to form the mature eschar.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Altered mental status reflects cerebral microvascular perivascular cuffing and toxic encephalopathy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Peripheral edema occurs during second-week complications due to microvascular permeability and plasma third-spacing.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Scleral icterus appears in severe icteric presentations with hepatic sinusoidal swelling and canalicular cholestasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Tachypnea serves as an early physical exam indicator of impending interstitial pneumonitis or metabolic acidosis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Dry cough is present in up to 50% of scrub typhus cases, reflecting early interstitial lung involvement.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Resting tachycardia develops as a compensatory response to capillary leakage, fever, and myocardial involvement.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Hypotensive shock indicates advanced capillary third-spacing and systemic endothelial dysfunction.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mild neutrophilic leukocytosis is a common admission finding, distinguishing scrub typhus from viral illnesses like dengue.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Normal leukocyte count is observed in nearly half of scrub typhus presentations, accompanied by a toxic left shift.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Prominent bandemia reflects acute bone marrow release of immature myeloid precursors during acute bacteremic stress.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Moderate thrombocytopenia occurs in 50-70% of scrub typhus patients due to endothelial adhesion and platelet consumption.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Severe thrombocytopenia correlates strongly with disseminated intravascular coagulation, ARDS, and higher mortality.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Moderate transaminitis occurs in >80% of patients, serving as a reliable admission biomarker for scrub typhus.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Disproportionate AST elevation reflects combined hepatocellular and myopathic microvascular injury in acute infection.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated alkaline phosphatase reflects portal triad inflammation and pericholangitic endothelial swelling.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mild conjugated hyperbilirubinemia reflects intrahepatic canalicular cholestasis rather than overt biliary tree obstruction.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated serum creatinine indicates acute renal dysfunction secondary to microvascular peritubular injury and prerenal azotemia.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated blood urea occurs concurrently with creatinine rise, marking acute kidney impairment.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hypoalbuminemia reflects systemic capillary leakage and negative acute phase reactant status, correlating with disease severity.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated C-reactive protein is universally present, sharply distinguishing scrub typhus from dengue and other viral fevers.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation reflects intense humoral and cellular systemic inflammatory vasculitis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Extreme hyperferritinemia indicates intense reticuloendothelial macrophage activation and severe systemic inflammatory response.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated serum lactate signals tissue hypoxemia and anaerobic metabolism in complicated scrub typhus shock.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated creatine kinase confirms skeletal muscle and myocardial microvascular inflammatory injury.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated troponin T reflects active myocyte necrosis from underlying scrub typhus infectious myocarditis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Prolonged prothrombin time indicates hepatic synthesis impairment and consumptive microvascular coagulopathy.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated D-dimer confirms extensive fibrin formation and secondary fibrinolysis across inflamed endothelial beds.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Microscopic hematuria reflects glomerular capillary endothelial injury and acute interstitial nephritis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Mild proteinuria is present in 30-50% of admissions, reflecting increased glomerular basement membrane permeability.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Granular urinary casts confirm ischemic or toxic acute tubular necrosis in patients with rising serum creatinine.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] CSF lymphocytic pleocytosis mirrors viral meningitis findings, accompanied by normal CSF glucose.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated CSF protein reflects blood-brain barrier disruption from cerebral microvascular endothelial inflammation.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Rapid defervescence response within 24-48 hours of initiating doxycycline is a cardinal diagnostic therapeutic hallmark.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Reticulonodular interstitial infiltrates on admission chest X-ray reflect septal edema and inflammatory infiltration.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Bilateral basal infiltrates indicate progressive dependent pulmonary microvascular leakage and pneumonitis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Kerley B lines denote thickened, fluid-engorged interlobular septa secondary to noncardiogenic capillary leak.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Bilateral pleural effusions demonstrate systemic serosal microvascular permeability leak in severe presentations.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] POCUS splenomegaly confirms acute reticuloendothelial hyperplasia and excludes splenic abscess or infarction.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] POCUS hepatomegaly demonstrates smooth, diffusely enlarged liver without focal parenchymal lesions.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Acalculous gallbladder thickening reflects generalized microvascular endothelial leak and hypoalbuminemia.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Ground-glass opacities on chest CT correspond to alveolar-capillary barrier leakage and early alveolar flooding.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Interlobular septal thickening confirms pulmonary lymphatic engorgement and interstitial fluid accumulation.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Preserved biliary ducts on ultrasound exclude extrahepatic biliary obstruction in patients with jaundice.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Diffuse myocardial hypokinesia on echocardiogram indicates widespread infectious myocarditis.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Minimal pericardial effusion frequently coexists with myocarditis as perimyocarditis on bedside POCUS.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Bite of microscopic larval Leptotrombidium trombiculid mites (chiggers) transmits Orientia tsutsugamushi during tissue feeding.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leptotrombidium deliense is the primary vector in agricultural habitats across South and Southeast Asia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leptotrombidium akamushi transmits classical summer-autumn scrub typhus in river valleys of East Asia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Leptotrombidium fletcheri colonizes plantation and scrub terrain in Malaysia and the Philippines.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Secondary scrub vegetation and brush borders provide the microenvironment where vector mite populations concentrate.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] The Tsutsugamushi Triangle defines the classical geographic endemic zone where over one billion individuals are at risk.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Agricultural rice fields represent major transmission foci where farming activities bring workers into contact with chiggers.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
