relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Falciparum Malaria, which presents with cyclical rigors, high intraerythrocytic parasitemia on peripheral blood smear, rapid therapeutic clearance with intravenous artesunate, and lacks human-to-human body fluid infectivity.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, day-1 leukocytosis, direct hyperbilirubinemia, calf tenderness, penicillin response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Leptospirosis, which features marked day-1 neutrophilic leukocytosis, deep direct hyperbilirubinemia, severe calf muscle tenderness, and prompt bactericidal response to intravenous penicillin or ceftriaxone.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, step-ladder fever, positive blood culture, lack of early DIC, normal platelets early
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Typhoid Fever, which manifests step-ladder fever, rose spots, relative bradycardia, and positive blood cultures for Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi, lacking profound early thrombocytopenia and fulminant DIC.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, purpura fulminans, high procalcitonin, ceftriaxone response, CSF pleocytosis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Meningococcemia, which presents with explosive purpura fulminans, neutrophilic cerebrospinal fluid pleocytosis, rapid response to third-generation cephalosporins, and elevated procalcitonin (> 10 ng/mL).

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, focal pyogenic source, high procalcitonin, rapid response to antibiotics
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Acute Bacterial Sepsis, which demonstrates identifiable focal pyogenic sources (pneumonia, pyelonephritis), marked procalcitonin elevation, and hemodynamic stabilization upon targeted antibacterial administration.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, inoculation eschar, doxycycline response, centripetal rash, intracellular bacteria
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Rickettsial Disease (e.g., epidemic typhus, Rocky Mountain spotted fever), which characteristically features an inoculation eschar, centripetal rash, and rapid therapeutic response within 48 hours to oral or intravenous doxycycline.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, ALT > AST, absence of consumptive DIC, absence of severe early shock
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Acute Viral Hepatitis (hepatitis A, B, or E), where transaminitis is heavily ALT-predominant (ALT >> AST), whereas VHF features profound AST-dominant transaminitis (AST:ALT > 3:1 to 5:1) with severe thrombocytopenia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, fecal leukocytes, fluoroquinolone response, absence of endothelial shock
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Shigellosis, which causes acute inflammatory dysentery with high fecal leukocytes and mucosal ulceration responding to fluoroquinolones, without systemic endothelial destruction, DIC, or transaminitis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, localized right lower quadrant signs, normal platelet count, intact coagulation
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Acute Appendicitis, which causes localized right lower quadrant peritoneal signs with normal platelets and coagulation, whereas VHF abdominal pain represents diffuse mucosal ischemia and microvascular hemorrhage.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, schistocytes, normal PT aPTT, ADAMTS13 deficiency, plasma exchange response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP), which exhibits prominent microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with abundant schistocytes and normal PT/aPTT, unlike the consumptive DIC with prolonged coagulation tests in VHF.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, isolated thrombocytopenia, normal liver enzymes, intact coagulation, afebrile
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP), which presents with isolated immune-mediated thrombocytopenia with entirely normal liver enzymes, normal clotting times, and absence of systemic toxic fever.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Faget sign, Councilman bodies, 17D vaccine protection, Flaviviridae
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with other filovirus and bunyavirus VHFs, Yellow Fever is an endemic flavivirus distinguished by Faget sign (marked sphygmothermic dissociation), midzonal hepatic Councilman bodies, deep early jaundice, and prevention via the live-attenuated 17D vaccine.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, exudative pharyngitis, 8th-nerve deafness, Mastomys reservoir, ribavirin response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with filovirus infections, Lassa Fever is an arenavirus endemic to West Africa featuring prominent exudative pharyngitis, retrosternal pain, eighth-nerve sensorineural deafness, and clinical responsiveness to early intravenous ribavirin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Hyalomma tick vector, livestock exposure, severe backache, ribavirin sensitivity
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with mosquito-borne or bat-borne VHFs, CCHF is a tick-borne nairovirus associated with Hyalomma ticks and livestock contact across Eurasia, presenting with extreme lumbosacral pain and responsive to ribavirin therapy.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, Rousettus bat reservoir, up to 88% mortality, lack of ribavirin response, Filoviridae
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with bunyavirus and arenavirus fevers, Marburg Virus Disease is a filovirus linked to Rousettus fruit bat caves and direct body fluid contact, characterized by up to 88% case fatality and complete lack of response to ribavirin.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, predominant pulmonary failure, lack of overt bleeding, New World rodents
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with pantropic hemorrhagic fevers, HPS presents primarily with non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema, severe hypoxia, hemoconcentration, and minimal hemorrhagic diathesis following New World rodent excreta inhalation.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, suppurative buboes, safety-pin Gram stain, Yersinia pestis, aminoglycoside response
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Contrasted with Plague (bubonic/septicemic Yersinia pestis), which presents with acutely suppurative regional lymph nodes (buboes), Gram-negative bipolar safety-pin bacilli on microscopy, and prompt clinical cure with aminoglycosides or doxycycline.

entities.name: Zika Virus
entities.description: An acute mosquito-borne arboviral disease caused by Zika virus (flavivirus), characterized by a mild self-limiting illness with low-grade fever, pruritic maculopapular exanthem, bilateral non-purulent conjunctivitis, and migratory polyarthralgia, with critical potential for severe neurotropic and teratogenic complications including Guillain-Barré syndrome and Congenital Zika Syndrome.

entities.name: Acute Zika Fever
entities.description: A benign, self-limiting acute systemic viral illness lasting 2 to 7 days characterized by low-grade fever, pruritic maculopapular rash, non-purulent conjunctivitis, and migratory polyarthralgia.

entities.name: Asymptomatic Infection
entities.description: Subclinical viral infection without overt symptoms occurring in approximately 75% to 80% of infected immunocompetent individuals who nevertheless develop neutralizing antibodies and can transmit the virus.

entities.name: Congenital Microcephaly
entities.description: Severe neurodevelopmental cranial reduction where infant head circumference is greater than 3 standard deviations below the mean for gestational age and sex, resulting from ZIKV targeting neural progenitor cells.

entities.name: Fetal Ventriculomegaly
entities.description: Pathological enlargement and dilation of the lateral cerebral ventricles occurring ex-vacuo due to massive destruction of fetal periventricular brain parenchyma.

entities.name: Intracranial Calcifications
entities.description: Coarse or punctate mineralized deposits situated characteristically at the corticomedullary junction, basal ganglia, and periventricular zones following dystrophic necrosis of fetal brain tissue.

entities.name: Simplified Gyral Pattern
entities.description: Abnormal cerebral cortical development characterized by pachygyria, lissencephaly, and polymicrogyria secondary to disrupted neurogenesis and impaired neuronal migration.

entities.name: Cerebral Cortical Thinning
entities.description: Marked reduction in cortical thickness and volume caused by premature apoptosis and cell cycle arrest in radial glial and cortical neural progenitor populations.

entities.name: Congenital Arthrogryposis
entities.description: Multiple congenital joint contractures affecting distal extremities (talipes equinovarus, knee and elbow flexion contractures) arising secondary to in utero fetal hypokinesia and spinal motor neuron loss.

entities.name: Chorioretinal Macular Atrophy
entities.description: Ocular congenital lesion featuring focal pigmentary mottling, retinal pigment epithelium atrophy, and sharply demarcated chorioretinal scarring localized to the central macula.

entities.name: Optic Nerve Hypoplasia
entities.description: Underdevelopment and pallor of the optic disc, double-ring sign, and abnormal cup-to-disc ratio resulting in permanent visual impairment in congenital Zika cases.

entities.name: Sensorineural Hearing Loss
entities.description: Congenital bilateral or unilateral auditory deficit caused by viral injury to the auditory nerve or cochlear structures in prenatally exposed infants.

entities.name: Fetal Demise
entities.description: In utero death of the developing embryo or fetus across any trimester of gestation precipitated by severe placental insufficiency and disseminated fetal viral infection.

entities.name: Spontaneous Miscarriage
entities.description: Early involuntary termination of pregnancy prior to 20 weeks of gestation triggered by acute syncytiotrophoblast destruction and intense intervillositis.

entities.name: Preterm Birth
entities.description: Delivery of a neonate prior to 37 completed weeks of gestation stimulated by acute intrauterine inflammatory signaling and placental insufficiency.

entities.name: Intrauterine Growth Restriction
entities.description: Pathological reduction in estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age due to compromised uteroplacental vascular perfusion.

entities.name: Fetal Hydrops
entities.description: Severe fetal pathological fluid accumulation in at least two serosal compartments (ascites, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, subcutaneous edema) driven by severe viral infection.

entities.name: Guillain-Barré Syndrome
entities.description: An acute autoimmune post-infectious demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy developing 1 to 3 weeks after acute infection, characterized by ascending flaccid paralysis and areflexia.

entities.name: Ascending Flaccid Paralysis
entities.description: Progressive, symmetrical loss of motor function commencing in the lower extremities and advancing cephalad to involve upper limbs, trunk, and cranial nerves.

entities.name: Acute Transverse Myelitis
entities.description: Focal inflammatory demyelination spanning one or more spinal cord segments presenting with rapidly evolving paraparesis, sensory level deficit, and sphincter dysfunction.

entities.name: Acute Meningoencephalitis
entities.description: Direct invasion and inflammation of meninges and brain parenchyma in adults or children presenting with fever, altered mental status, meningismus, and focal neurological signs.

entities.name: Cranial Nerve Palsy
entities.description: Unilateral or bilateral neuropathy affecting cranial nerves, most commonly peripheral facial nerve (CN VII) palsy and ocular motor paresis (CN III, VI).

entities.name: Acute Flaccid Myelitis
entities.description: Sudden onset of asymmetric or symmetric flaccid limb weakness with diminished reflexes attributed to selective viral inflammation of spinal cord anterior horn cells.

entities.name: Migratory Polyarthralgia
entities.description: Transient, non-erosive joint discomfort shifting between small and medium peripheral joints, notably wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, ankles, and knees.

entities.name: Periarticular Tenosynovitis
entities.description: Inflammation of synovial sheaths surrounding flexor and extensor tendons of the wrist and ankle, causing dorsal hand and foot swelling without joint destruction.

entities.name: Generalized Myalgia
entities.description: Diffuse skeletal muscle pain and soreness commonly localized to the back, calves, and shoulders during the acute viremic phase.

entities.name: Retro-Orbital Pain
entities.description: Mild to moderate dull retrobulbar ache aggravated by lateral or superior eye movement, distinctively milder than the agonizing retro-orbital pain of dengue.

entities.name: Frontal Cephalea
entities.description: Throbbing or dull persistent frontal and holocranial headache presenting as one of the earliest prodromal symptoms.

entities.name: Constitutional Asthenia
entities.description: Profound fatigue, physical exhaustion, and generalized malaise that typically accompanies the acute phase and may linger for 1 to 2 weeks post-defervescence.

entities.name: Transient Anorexia
entities.description: Loss of appetite often accompanied by mild dysgeusia or nausea during the acute febrile and eruptive stages.

entities.name: Autonomic Dysreflexia
entities.description: Hemodynamic instability, fluctuating blood pressures, cardiac arrhythmias, and diaphoresis arising from autonomic neuropathy in post-Zika Guillain-Barré syndrome.

entities.name: Neonatal Dysphagia
entities.description: Severe impairment of sucking and swallowing coordination in neonates with congenital Zika syndrome, leading to aspiration pneumonia and feeding failure.

entities.name: Neonatal Hypertonia
entities.description: Generalized marked muscular rigidity and hyperreflexia appearing in infancy secondary to extensive bilateral corticospinal tract and motor cortex injury.

entities.name: Talipes Equinovarus
entities.description: Congenital clubfoot deformity involving unilateral or bilateral ankle inversion and plantarflection secondary to fetal immobilization and neurogenic muscle imbalance.

entities.name: Infantile Seizures
entities.description: Early-onset intractable epileptic spasms and focal clonic seizures resulting from extensive cortical dysgenesis and subcortical calcifications.

entities.name: Bilateral Facial Diplegia
entities.description: Bilateral lower motor neuron facial weakness presenting with inability to close eyes, smile, or puff cheeks in Guillain-Barré syndrome variants.

entities.name: Peripheral Paresthesias
entities.description: Tingling, prickling, or numbness affecting distal fingers and toes that precedes or accompanies motor weakness in GBS.

entities.name: Diaphragmatic Weakness
entities.description: Respiratory muscle insufficiency and neuromuscular ventilatory failure requiring mechanical ventilation in 15% to 30% of post-Zika GBS cases.

entities.name: Posterior Cervical Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Mild to moderate non-tender or minimally tender enlargement of posterior cervical and retroauricular lymph nodes.

entities.name: Mild Diarrhea
entities.description: Transient loose watery stools or abdominal discomfort occurring in a subset of patients during the early viremic phase.

entities.name: Intense Cutaneous Pruritus
entities.description: Severe, distressing itching of the skin associated with the descending maculopapular rash, often disturbing sleep.

entities.name: Low-Grade Fever
entities.description: Core body temperature elevation between 37.5°C and 38.5°C that lacks the high-spiking chills or rigors of dengue or malaria.

entities.name: Maculopapular Exanthem
entities.description: Erythematous, finely morbilliform or papular cutaneous eruption that erupts within the first 24 to 48 hours of illness.

entities.name: Centrifugal Rash Distribution
entities.description: Rapid outward progression of the exanthem starting on the face and neck and spreading downward across the trunk and extremities to the palms and soles.

entities.name: Palmar Erythematous Macules
entities.description: Discrete, non-blanching or blanching pink macules distributed over the palmar surfaces of both hands.

entities.name: Plantar Erythematous Macules
entities.description: Punctate erythematous macular lesions distributed across the plantar aspects of both feet.

entities.name: Bulbar Conjunctival Hyperemia
entities.description: Bilateral diffuse engorgement of superficial scleral and episcleral vessels without purulent exudate or discharge.

entities.name: Palpebral Conjunctival Injection
entities.description: Bilateral vascular congestion of tarsal conjunctival surfaces without pseudomembranes or cobblestoning.

entities.name: Periarticular Hand Puffiness
entities.description: Soft tissue non-pitting edema localized around the dorsum of the hands, metacarpophalangeal joints, and wrists.

entities.name: Periarticular Foot Puffiness
entities.description: Bilateral diffuse swelling around the malleoli, Achilles tendons, and dorsum of feet without true intra-articular effusion.

entities.name: Non-Erosive Joint Tenderness
entities.description: Palpation tenderness over peripheral joint lines without warmth, erythema, bony enlargement, or joint destruction.

entities.name: Preserved Joint Mobility
entities.description: Full or near-full passive and active range of joint motion despite subjective joint soreness, unlike the crippling joint locking of chikungunya.

entities.name: Severe Craniofacial Disproportion
entities.description: Dramatically reduced cranial neurocranium volume contrasting with a normal-sized viscerocranium and facial skeleton in neonates.

entities.name: Redundant Scalp Rugae
entities.description: Exaggerated transverse skin folds and wrinkling on the posterior occipital scalp (cutis gyrata-like) due to rapid collapse of the fetal brain vault.

entities.name: Depressed Cranial Vault
entities.description: Overlapping cranial sutures and prominent occipital bone projection created by loss of brain parenchymal volume in utero.

entities.name: Premature Fontanelle Closure
entities.description: Early or complete synostotic closure of anterior and posterior fontanelles at or shortly after birth in severely affected infants.

entities.name: Infantile Generalized Spasticity
entities.description: Marked bilateral increase in muscle tone with clasp-knife rigidity and sustained ankle clonus in neonates with congenital Zika syndrome.

entities.name: Hyporeflexic Tendon Reflexes
entities.description: Diminished or completely absent deep tendon reflexes (patellar, Achilles, brachioradialis) in patients presenting with post-Zika Guillain-Barré.

entities.name: Ascending Symmetrical Weakness
entities.description: Progressive, bilateral loss of lower limb power (Medical Research Council grade 0-3/5) advancing symmetrically upward.

entities.name: Suboccipital Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Discrete, non-tender, mobile enlargement of lymph nodes located beneath the occipital protuberance.

entities.name: Palpable Posterior Cervical Nodes
entities.description: Palpable enlargement of superficial posterior cervical chain lymph nodes measuring 0.5 to 1.5 cm in diameter.

entities.name: Palatal Mucosal Enanthem
entities.description: Faint erythematous macules or non-hemorrhagic stippling on the soft palate and uvula without ulceration.

entities.name: Brisk Capillary Refill
entities.description: Rapid return of microvascular blood flow (<2 seconds) following digital compression, confirming intact peripheral perfusion.

entities.name: Absence of Ecchymoses
entities.description: Absence of cutaneous purpura, hematomas, or spontaneous subcutaneous bleeding on comprehensive skin examination.

entities.name: Absence of Petechiae
entities.description: Lack of pinpoint microvascular hemorrhagic lesions on flexural surfaces, distinguishing the rash from dengue petechiae.

entities.name: Normal Spleen Palpation
entities.description: Impapable splenic edge beneath the left costal margin during deep inspiration.

entities.name: Normal Hepatic Span
entities.description: Normal liver percussion span (6 to 12 cm) without tender hepatomegaly or Murphy sign on right upper quadrant examination.

entities.name: Clear Pulmonary Auscultation
entities.description: Normal vesicular breath sounds bilaterally without adventitious crackles, wheezing, rhonchi, or pleural friction rubs.

entities.name: Normal Arterial Pressure
entities.description: Normal systolic and diastolic blood pressure with wide pulse pressure (>20 mmHg), ruling out decompensated dengue shock syndrome.

entities.name: Normal Leukocyte Count
entities.description: Total peripheral white blood cell count remains within normal reference limits (4,000–10,000/µL) throughout early acute infection.

entities.name: Mild Leukopenia Pattern
entities.description: Peripheral white blood cell count moderately depressed between 3,500 and 5,000/µL without severe neutropenia.

entities.name: Absence of Agranulocytosis
entities.description: Absolute neutrophil count remains well above critical cytopenic thresholds (>1,500/µL), preserving antibacterial defenses.

entities.name: Preserved Platelet Count
entities.description: Platelet count remains above 150,000/µL without spontaneous mucosal hemorrhage or petechiae.

entities.name: Mild Thrombocytopenia Pattern
entities.description: Platelet count moderately decreased between 100,000 and 150,000/µL that promptly normalizes upon defervescence.

entities.name: Stable Hematocrit Concentration
entities.description: Baseline hematocrit remains stable within physiological limits without hemoconcentration.

entities.name: Normal Serum Albumin
entities.description: Serum albumin concentration remains within normal limits (3.5–5.0 g/dL), reflecting intact vascular endothelial barrier function.

entities.name: Mild Transaminase Elevation
entities.description: Serum aspartate aminotransferase and alanine aminotransferase levels mildly elevated, typically less than twice upper limit of normal.

entities.name: Normal Serum Bilirubin
entities.description: Total serum bilirubin remains under 1.2 mg/dL, ruling out intrahepatic cholestasis or acute hemolysis.

entities.name: Normal Serum Creatinine
entities.description: Serum creatinine remains within baseline limits (<1.2 mg/dL), indicating preserved glomerular filtration.

entities.name: Normal Blood Urea
entities.description: Blood urea nitrogen levels remain normal without prerenal azotemia or dehydration.

entities.name: Mild CRP Elevation
entities.description: C-reactive protein is normal or mildly increased (10–30 mg/L), distinguishing from severe invasive bacterial infections.

entities.name: Negative Blood Smear
entities.description: Light microscopy examination of thick and thin blood films reveals complete absence of intraerythrocytic Plasmodium parasites.

entities.name: Serum ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: Reverse transcriptase PCR of acute serum detects ZIKV RNA up to 10 to 11 days post-symptom onset.

entities.name: Urine ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: Real-time RT-PCR demonstrates persistent shedding of viral RNA in urine for up to 2 to 3 weeks after onset.

entities.name: Semen ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: Detection of viral genome in male seminal fluid by RT-PCR for several months after initial clinical recovery.

entities.name: Saliva ZIKV RT-PCR
entities.description: RT-PCR identification of ZIKV RNA in oral saliva samples during the acute phase of illness.

entities.name: Amniotic Fluid RT-PCR
entities.description: Molecular detection of viral RNA in amniotic fluid obtained via prenatal diagnostic amniocentesis.

entities.name: ZIKV IgM Seropositivity
entities.description: Specific anti-ZIKV immunoglobulin M antibodies detected via MAC-ELISA starting 3 to 8 days post-onset.

entities.name: PRNT Confirmatory Neutralization
entities.description: Plaque reduction neutralization testing demonstrating at least 4-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers against ZIKV compared to DENV.

entities.name: Flavivirus Serologic Cross-Reactivity
entities.description: Broad cross-reactivity observed on IgM and IgG immunoassays in secondary flavivirus infections.

entities.name: Albuminocytological Dissociation
entities.description: CSF analysis demonstrating elevated protein concentration with normal white cell count (<5/µL) in post-Zika GBS.

entities.name: CSF ZIKV Detection
entities.description: Direct identification of viral RNA in cerebrospinal fluid by RT-PCR in cases of meningoencephalitis or myelitis.

entities.name: Thin Gallbladder Wall
entities.description: Bedside gallbladder ultrasound reveals thin wall (<3 mm) without subserosal edema, striations, or pericholecystic fluid.

entities.name: Absence of Ascites
entities.description: Point-of-care abdominal sonography demonstrates no free fluid in Morison pouch, spleno-renal recess, or pelvis.

entities.name: Absence of Hemoconcentration
entities.description: Serial hematocrit determinations show no upward drift or hemoconcentration ≥20% above baseline.

entities.name: Absence of Pleural-Effusion
entities.description: Bedside lung ultrasound demonstrates normal pleural sliding and complete absence of anechoic pleural effusions or B-lines.

entities.name: Normal Pericardial POCUS
entities.description: Subcostal echocardiographic window reveals normal pericardial space without anechoic fluid strip or cardiac tamponade.

entities.name: Subcortical Intracranial Calcifications
entities.description: Non-contrast cranial CT reveals dense punctate calcifications clustered at the corticomedullary junction and basal ganglia.

entities.name: Fetal Ventriculomegaly Ultrasound
entities.description: Obstetric neurosonography demonstrates prominent dilatation of the lateral ventricular atria exceeding 10 mm.

entities.name: Severe Microcephaly Biometry
entities.description: Prenatal ultrasound biometry reveals head circumference falling more than 3 standard deviations below gestational mean.

entities.name: Pachygyria Neuroimaging Pattern
entities.description: Fetal or neonatal brain MRI demonstrates reduced sulcation, shallow sylvian fissures, and pachygyria.

entities.name: Corpus Callosum Dysgenesis
entities.description: Neuroimaging reveals hypoplasia or complete agenesis of the corpus callosum with colpocephaly.

entities.name: Cerebellar Hypoplasia Neuroimaging
entities.description: Sonography or MRI reveals disproportionately small cerebellar hemispheres and vermis with mega cisterna magna.

entities.name: Fetal Arthrogryposis Ultrasound
entities.description: High-resolution obstetric ultrasound visualizes persistent fixed hyperextension or flexion contractures of the fetal limbs.

entities.name: Fetal Amniotic Microcephaly
entities.description: Prenatal ultrasound reveals collapsed calvarium, overlapping sutures, and scalp cutis rugae in utero.

entities.name: Demyelinating Polyradiculoneuropathy Pattern
entities.description: Electrodiagnostic testing shows prolonged distal motor latencies, slowed conduction velocities, and conduction blocks in GBS.

entities.name: Decreased Motor Conduction
entities.description: Markedly reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes on nerve conduction studies indicative of axonal injury in GBS.

entities.name: Aedes Aegypti Mosquito
entities.description: Primary daytime-biting domestic vector mosquito adapted to human dwellings and artificial water containers.

entities.name: Aedes Albopictus Mosquito
entities.description: Secondary day-biting Asian tiger mosquito capable of transmitting ZIKV in more temperate suburban zones.

entities.name: Diurnal Vector Feeding
entities.description: Daytime biting behavior with peaks of feeding activity during early morning and late afternoon hours.

entities.name: Tropical Americas Endemicity
entities.description: Widespread transmission throughout Latin America and the Caribbean during major pandemic waves.

entities.name: Caribbean Island Exposure
entities.description: Intense local mosquito-borne transmission across Caribbean island nations and territories.

entities.name: Pacific Island Endemicity
entities.description: Major historical epidemic outbreaks documented across Micronesia (Yap Island) and French Polynesia.

entities.name: Southeast Asian Endemicity
entities.description: Endemic baseline transmission and episodic outbreaks across tropical nations of Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Sub-Saharan African Endemicity
entities.description: Ancestral enzootic forest cycles and sporadic human infections across Central and West Africa.

entities.name: Unprotected Sexual Contact
entities.description: Venereal human-to-human transmission via vaginal, anal, or oral intercourse without barrier protection.

entities.name: Infectious Seminal Shedding
entities.description: Prolonged presence of infectious viral particles in male semen lasting weeks to months post-recovery.

entities.name: Transplacental Vertical Transmission
entities.description: Direct vertical transmission of virus from infected maternal bloodstream across the placenta to the fetus.

entities.name: First Trimester Pregnancy
entities.description: Early gestational stage characterized by peak embryonic vulnerability to severe neurodestructive malformations.

entities.name: Second Trimester Pregnancy
entities.description: Mid-gestational stage where infection leads to cortical dysgenesis, calcifications, and growth restriction.

entities.name: Third Trimester Pregnancy
entities.description: Late gestational stage where maternal infection may cause placental insufficiency, IUGR, or preterm birth.

entities.name: Contaminated Blood Transfusion
entities.description: Iatrogenic acquisition of virus through infusion of unscreened platelets or packed erythrocytes from a viremic donor.

entities.name: Solid Organ Transplantation
entities.description: Transmission of virus via transplantation of kidneys, liver, or heart harvested from an infected donor.

entities.name: Laboratory Biohazard Exposure
entities.description: Accidental percutaneous needle puncture or mucosal splash in research laboratories handling live ZIKV.

entities.name: Three-To-Fourteen Day Incubation
entities.description: Interval between viral inoculation via mosquito bite or sexual contact and initial symptom manifestation.

entities.name: Typical Incubation Window
entities.description: Most common incubation interval of 3 to 7 days observed in clinical cohort studies.

entities.name: Sylvatic Primate Reservoirs
entities.description: Enzootic transmission maintaining viral reservoirs in wild forest monkeys and arboreal mosquitoes in Africa.

entities.name: International Tropical Traveler
entities.description: Non-immune individuals traveling to regions of active endemic arboviral transmission.

entities.name: Artificial Water Containers
entities.description: Domestic water storage cisterns, unsealed buckets, and discarded tires providing breeding sites for Aedes larvae.

entities.name: Vascular Plasma Leakage
entities.description: Pathological hyperpermeability leading to pleural effusions, ascites, or hemoconcentration with hematocrit rise >=20%.

entities.name: Severe Hemoconcentration
entities.description: Significant elevation of hematocrit >=20% above baseline reflecting acute intravascular volume loss.

entities.name: Profound Thrombocytopenia
entities.description: Platelet count falling below 50,000/µL accompanied by bleeding manifestations.

entities.name: Spontaneous Mucosal Hemorrhage
entities.description: Overt hemorrhagic diathesis such as epistaxis, hematemesis, melena, or gross hematuria.

entities.name: Hypovolemic Circulatory Shock
entities.description: Cardiovascular collapse with narrow pulse pressure (<=20 mmHg), profound hypotension, and delayed refill.

entities.name: Crippling Destructive Arthritis
entities.description: Severe disabling polyarthritis causing extreme joint immobility and inability to ambulate.

entities.name: Incapacitating Morning Stiffness
entities.description: Protracted inflammatory morning stiffness lasting more than 60 minutes indicating severe synovitis.

entities.name: Continuous High-Grade Pyrexia
entities.description: Sustained temperature elevations exceeding 39.5°C to 40.0°C with severe shaking chills.

entities.name: Prolonged Persistent Pyrexia
entities.description: Fever persisting continuously for more than 7 to 10 days.

entities.name: Purulent Conjunctival Exudate
entities.description: Copious yellowish purulent eye discharge, crusting, and matted eyelids.

entities.name: Severe Photophobia
entities.description: Intense ocular pain and intolerance of light suggesting anterior uveitis, keratitis, or measles.

entities.name: Buccal Koplik Spots
entities.description: Pathognomonic pinpoint bluish-white papules on an erythematous base on the buccal mucosa in measles.

entities.name: Prominent Respiratory Coryza
entities.description: Severe paroxysmal coughing, purulent rhinorrhea, and upper airway catarrh.

entities.name: Tender Retroauricular Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Prominent tender lymph node enlargement behind the pinna and base of skull typical of rubella.

entities.name: Malarial Paroxysmal Rigors
entities.description: Periodic paroxysms of severe shaking chills, teeth chattering, and drenching diaphoresis.

entities.name: Slapped-Cheek Facial Rash
entities.description: Confluent bright fiery erythema of bilateral malar cheeks with circumoral pallor seen in parvovirus B19.

entities.name: Centripetal Vesicular Eruption
entities.description: Pruritic vesicular lesions progressing from macules to papules to fluid-filled teardrop blisters in varicella.

entities.name: Hyperbilirubinemic Scleral Icterus
entities.description: Marked direct hyperbilirubinemia, clinical jaundice, and dark urine indicating hepatic failure or biliary stasis.

entities.name: Oliguric Renal Failure
entities.description: Severe reduction in urine output with acute elevation of serum creatinine and urea in Weil disease.

entities.name: Inoculation Cutaneous Eschar
entities.description: Cigarette-burn necrotic skin lesion with surrounding erythematous halo pathognomonic of scrub typhus.

entities.name: Massive Splenomegaly
entities.description: Significant enlargement of the spleen extending well below the left costal margin in visceral leishmaniasis.

entities.name: Severe Agranulocytic Leukopenia
entities.description: Absolute neutrophil count dropping below 500/µL or WBC <2,000/µL indicating severe bone marrow suppression.

entities.name: Dengue Fever
entities.description: Flavivirus infection presenting with high fever, severe breakbone arthralgia, retro-orbital ache, plasma leakage, and thrombocytopenia.

entities.name: Chikungunya Virus Disease
entities.description: Alphavirus infection presenting with abrupt high fever and crippling symmetrical polyarthritis persisting for months.

entities.name: Yellow Fever
entities.description: Flavivirus illness presenting with toxic phase icterus, hematemesis, oliguria, and high mortality rate.

entities.name: Measles Virus Infection
entities.description: Morbillivirus infection characterized by cough, coryza, photophobic conjunctivitis, high fever, and Koplik spots.

entities.name: Rubella Virus Infection
entities.description: Togavirus causing mild fever, maculopapular rash, and prominent tender suboccipital and postauricular lymphadenopathy.

entities.name: Parvovirus B19 Infection
entities.description: Erythrovirus causing slapped-cheek facial rash in children and acute symmetric polyarthritis in adult females.

entities.name: West Nile Encephalitis
entities.description: Flavivirus causing neuroinvasive asymmetric flaccid paralysis, tremor, and parkinsonian features.

entities.name: Mayaro Virus Disease
entities.description: Amazon basin alphavirus presenting with acute fever, disabling chronic polyarthritis, and maculopapular exanthem.

entities.name: Oropouche Fever
entities.description: Orthobunyavirus transmitted by Culicoides midges causing abrupt fever, retro-orbital ache, and frequent symptomatic relapses.

entities.name: Falciparum Malaria
entities.description: Protozoan infection causing paroxysmal fevers, rigors, hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and positive thick film microscopy.

entities.name: Leptospirosis Disease
entities.description: Spirochetal zoonosis causing conjunctival suffusion, intense calf pain, jaundice, and acute oliguric renal failure.

entities.name: Scrub Typhus Infection
entities.description: Orientia infection presenting with necrotic inoculation eschar, high continuous fever, and regional adenopathy.

entities.name: Acute HIV Seroconversion
entities.description: Early retroviral syndrome with high fever, maculopapular rash, oral ulcerations, and generalized adenopathy.

entities.name: Infectious Mononucleosis
entities.description: Epstein-Barr virus illness featuring exudative tonsillitis, cervical lymphadenopathy, and atypical lymphocytosis.

entities.name: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection
entities.description: Congenital herpesvirus infection causing periventricular calcifications, petechial rash, and sensorineural deafness.

entities.name: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
entities.description: Congenital protozoan disease featuring diffuse intracranial calcifications, obstructive hydrocephalus, and chorioretinitis.

entities.name: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
entities.description: Congenital togavirus infection featuring cataracts, sensorineural deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus.

entities.name: Secondary Syphilis
entities.description: Treponemal spirochete disease causing copper-red papulosquamous rash on palms and soles with condyloma lata.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents acutely as a mild self-limiting systemic febrile illness lasting 2 to 7 days characterized by low-grade fever, maculopapular rash, non-purulent conjunctivitis, and peripheral polyarthralgia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests subclinically in approximately 75% to 80% of infected human hosts who remain entirely asymptomatic but capable of transmitting the virus through blood or sexual contact.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes severe congenital microcephaly in infants exposed in utero, characterized by profound disproportion between cranial vault and facial skeleton due to viral destruction of fetal neural progenitor cells.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as asymmetric or symmetric fetal ventriculomegaly on prenatal imaging, resulting from massive cerebral parenchymal volume loss and white matter destruction.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Leads to dystrophic intracranial calcifications predominantly distributed at the corticomedullary junction and basal ganglia in congenital Zika syndrome.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes severe disruption of cerebral cortical development manifesting as a simplified gyral pattern, pachygyria, or lissencephaly on neonatal neuroimaging.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as profound cerebral cortical thinning with reduced neocortical mantle thickness secondary to selective viral tropism for radial glia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes congenital arthrogryposis multiplex with severe non-progressive joint contractures resulting from embryonic motor neuron loss and prolonged fetal akinesia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as focal chorioretinal macular atrophy with severe pigmentary mottling and scarring in infants afflicted with congenital Zika syndrome.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes optic nerve hypoplasia, optic disc pallor, and coloboma in infants following transplacental fetal viral neuroinvasion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Results in sensorineural hearing loss in 5% to 10% of infants with congenital Zika syndrome, requiring routine newborn auditory brainstem evoked response screening.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as intrauterine fetal demise or stillbirth in pregnant women experiencing acute gestational Zika virus infection.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes spontaneous first-trimester miscarriage associated with chronic histiocytic intervillositis and placental villous necrosis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as spontaneous or medically indicated preterm birth occurring at significantly elevated rates among mothers acutely infected during pregnancy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as symmetrical intrauterine growth restriction and low birth weight in infants prenatally exposed to Zika virus.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes non-immune fetal hydrops characterized by generalized subcutaneous edema and serosal cavitary effusions in severe in utero infections.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Triggers post-infectious Guillain-Barré syndrome within 1 to 3 weeks post-infection via molecular mimicry and autoimmune peripheral nerve injury.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as progressive ascending symmetrical flaccid motor weakness in patients developing Zika-associated Guillain-Barré syndrome.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes acute transverse myelitis with motor deficits, sensory level dysfunction, and neurogenic bladder secondary to spinal cord inflammatory demyelination.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acute meningoencephalitis with confusion, seizures, and neck stiffness secondary to neurotropic viral CNS invasion.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as cranial nerve neuropathies, particularly acute peripheral facial palsy and abducens nerve paresis in neuroinvasive disease.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as acute flaccid myelitis characterized by polio-like lower motor neuron limb weakness from viral targeting of anterior horn cells.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as mild to moderate migratory polyarthralgia primarily targeting small peripheral joints of the hands, wrists, knees, and ankles.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as periarticular tenosynovitis producing noticeable soft-tissue puffiness over the dorsum of hands, wrists, and feet.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents with generalized skeletal myalgia and muscle tenderness lasting throughout the acute symptomatic phase of 2 to 7 days.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes mild to moderate retro-orbital pain exacerbated by ocular movement during the acute viremic phase.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as persistent frontal or temporal headache appearing early during the onset of the acute viremic illness.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as marked constitutional asthenia, generalized prostration, and fatigue during and shortly after the acute viral syndrome.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents with transient anorexia, mild nausea, and loss of appetite during the initial days of symptomatic infection.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes autonomic dysfunction and hemodynamic lability including labile blood pressure and tachyarrhythmias in severe Guillain-Barré syndrome.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as neonatal dysphagia with suck-swallow incoordination in infants with congenital Zika encephalopathy.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Causes prominent neonatal hypertonia and pyramidal tract signs progressing to persistent spastic cerebral palsy in Congenital Zika Syndrome.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as severe congenital talipes equinovarus (clubfoot) resulting from fetal neurogenic akinesia and motor neuron destruction.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Precipitates intractable early infantile epileptic seizures and spasms secondary to severe cerebral cortical malformations and scarring.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as bilateral facial diplegia and bifacial weakness in post-infectious neuroinvasive Guillain-Barré syndrome.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as distal peripheral paresthesias and burning sensations in the hands and feet during the early phase of post-Zika GBS.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Leads to diaphragmatic paralysis and acute respiratory failure necessitating mechanical ventilatory support in severe post-Zika GBS.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as mild posterior cervical lymphadenopathy reflecting regional reticuloendothelial response to viral replication.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents with mild watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping in a minority of patients during early symptomatic viremia.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests as intense cutaneous pruritus that uniquely accompanies the descending erythematous maculopapular exanthem.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features mild low-grade fever (37.5°C–38.5°C) lasting 2 to 7 days, contrasting with the high continuous fevers of dengue (>39°C).

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Manifests as an erythematous, finely papular maculopapular exanthem appearing on day 1 or 2 of symptom onset.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Displays a characteristic centrifugal rash distribution commencing on the face and rapidly spreading outward to the limbs, palms, and soles.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates discrete palmar erythematous macules, a distinctive physical sign rarely observed in dengue fever.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals plantar erythematous macules on physical inspection of the soles during the peak of the cutaneous eruption.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Manifests as bilateral bulbar conjunctival hyperemia with pronounced vascular injection occurring in the absence of pus or exudate.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates diffuse bilateral palpebral conjunctival injection without purulent discharge, distinguishing it from bacterial conjunctivitis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits periarticular hand puffiness and soft-tissue swelling over the dorsal metacarpophalangeal joints and wrists.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals soft periarticular foot puffiness and perimalleolar edema without synovial thickening or large joint effusion.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates mild to moderate non-erosive joint tenderness over peripheral joint lines without warmth or severe erythema.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits preserved joint mobility with ability to ambulate and bend digits, contrasting with the crippling immobility of chikungunya.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Displays severe craniofacial disproportion with pronounced cranial collapse and a sloping forehead in congenital Zika syndrome.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Features redundant scalp rugae and corrugated occipital skin folds resulting from premature fetal neurocranial deflation.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates a depressed cranial vault with overlapping cranial bones and a prominent occipital shelf upon newborn physical examination.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals premature fontanelle closure with impalpable or deeply sunken anterior fontanelle at newborn clinical examination.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Shows infantile generalized spasticity, hypertonia, and hyperactive deep tendon reflexes in infants with congenital Zika encephalopathy.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits hyporeflexic tendon reflexes or generalized areflexia on neurological examination of patients with post-infectious GBS.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates ascending symmetrical weakness beginning in distal lower extremities and spreading to proximal muscle groups in GBS.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals mild suboccipital lymphadenopathy on palpation of the posterior neck and base of skull.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates palpable posterior cervical lymph nodes during physical examination of the head and neck.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Elicits faint palatal mucosal enanthem on oropharyngeal inspection without tonsillar exudate or Koplik spots.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Confirms brisk capillary refill under two seconds, establishing hemodynamic stability and absence of dengue-like plasma leakage.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates complete absence of ecchymoses or spontaneous purpura, confirming normal primary and secondary hemostasis.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Confirms absence of petechiae on extremities and palate, helping differentiate Zika exanthem from hemorrhagic arboviruses.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Reveals normal spleen palpation with impalpable left upper quadrant viscera, helping rule out acute malaria.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates normal hepatic span without tender hepatomegaly or right upper quadrant peritoneal signs.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Demonstrates clear pulmonary auscultation bilaterally, ruling out primary viral pneumonitis or pleural effusion.

relationships.keywords: PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN
relationships.description: [PHYSICAL_EXAM_SIGN] Confirms normal arterial pressure with preserved pulse pressure, excluding dengue shock syndrome or hypovolemic collapse.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates normal total leukocyte count (4,000–10,000/µL) on admission complete blood count in most uncomplicated cases.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits mild leukopenia pattern with WBC counts between 3,500 and 5,000/µL without severe neutropenia.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows absence of agranulocytosis or severe absolute neutrophil depletion (<1,000/µL), maintaining host antibacterial defenses.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits preserved platelet count (>150,000/µL) or only minimal platelet reduction in the vast majority of acute presentations.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Displays mild thrombocytopenia pattern (100,000–150,000/µL) that remains self-limiting without mucosal hemorrhage.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Maintains stable hematocrit concentration baseline without serial hemoconcentration or intravascular volume depletion.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates normal serum albumin concentration (3.5–5.0 g/dL), reflecting intact vascular endothelial barrier function.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits mild transaminase elevation with AST and ALT typically less than twice the upper limit of normal.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits normal total serum bilirubin (<1.2 mg/dL), confirming absence of acute hepatic failure or hemolysis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Maintains normal serum creatinine levels (<1.2 mg/dL) indicating preserved glomerular filtration rate.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates normal blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels without prerenal azotemia or dehydration.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits mild C-reactive protein elevation (CRP 10–30 mg/L) or normal baseline levels during acute viral illness.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates negative thick and thin blood smears, definitively excluding intraerythrocytic plasmodial parasites.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Confirms acute diagnosis via serum ZIKV RT-PCR detection of viral RNA up to 10 to 11 days following symptom onset.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits positive urine ZIKV RT-PCR shedding viral RNA for 2 to 3 weeks after onset, offering a longer diagnostic window than serum.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Detects persistent viral RNA via semen ZIKV RT-PCR up to several months post-infection in convalescent males.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Detects viral RNA via saliva ZIKV RT-PCR during the first week of acute disease, especially when venipuncture is difficult.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Confirms congenital transplacental transmission via positive amniotic fluid RT-PCR obtained via diagnostic amniocentesis.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows positive ZIKV IgM ELISA serology emerging 3 to 8 days post-infection and persisting for up to 12 weeks.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates confirmatory neutralization on plaque reduction neutralization testing with at least 4-fold higher titers over dengue.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Exhibits widespread flavivirus serologic cross-reactivity on IgM immunoassays in individuals previously exposed to dengue.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows pathognomonic albuminocytological dissociation on lumbar puncture with markedly elevated CSF protein and normal white cell count in GBS.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Confirms neuroinvasive meningoencephalitis or transverse myelitis through direct CSF ZIKV RT-PCR detection of viral genome.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals thin gallbladder wall (<3 mm) without subserosal edema or striation on bedside point-of-care ultrasonography.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Confirms complete absence of free peritoneal fluid or ascites in the hepatorenal recess (Morison's pouch) and pelvis on POCUS.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates absence of hemoconcentration with serial hematocrit remaining strictly under 20% elevation from baseline.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates absence of pleural effusion, fluid collections, or B-lines on bedside thoracic lung ultrasound.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Confirms normal pericardial space without pericardial effusion or cardiac tamponade physiology on subxiphoid echocardiogram.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Identifies coarse dystrophic subcortical intracranial calcifications concentrated at the corticomedullary junction on fetal/neonatal CT.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals bilateral asymmetrical fetal lateral ventriculomegaly with atrium width exceeding 10 mm on prenatal obstetric ultrasound.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Documents head circumference more than 3 standard deviations below gestational mean on serial obstetric biometry.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates simplified cerebral gyral patterns, shallow sulcation, and pachygyria on postnatal neuroimaging or fetal MRI.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Reveals partial or complete agenesis and dysgenesis of the corpus callosum on cranial neuroimaging in Congenital Zika Syndrome.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Shows cerebellar vermis hypoplasia and enlarged cisterna magna on fetal neurosonography and magnetic resonance imaging.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Identifies persistent fixed joint contractures and bilateral clubfoot on detailed second- and third-trimester prenatal sonography.

relationships.keywords: IMAGING_FINDING
relationships.description: [IMAGING_FINDING] Demonstrates severe cranial collapse and scalp rugae with diminished biparietal diameter on prenatal fetal ultrasound.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Demonstrates prolonged distal motor latencies, slowed conduction velocities, and conduction blocks on electromyography in GBS.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Shows markedly reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes on nerve conduction studies in axonal and demyelinating GBS.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Inoculated predominantly through the bite of infected female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, the primary urban and peridomestic vector.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted by competent secondary vector Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, capable of surviving in temperate and suburban habitats.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired during peak daylight mosquito feeding hours, specifically during early morning and late afternoon hours before dusk.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Linked epidemiologically to residence or travel in endemic tropical regions of South, Central, and North America with active transmission.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired through travel to Caribbean islands and archipelagos harboring widespread established Aedes vector populations.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Linked to travel or residence across Pacific Island nations, including historical epicenter outbreaks on Yap Island and French Polynesia.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Associated with baseline endemic viral circulation and sporadic urban outbreaks across tropical Southeast Asian nations.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Associated with ancestral sylvatic and urban viral lineages across Central and West Africa, where ZIKV was first isolated.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired non-vectorially through unprotected vaginal, anal, or oral intercourse with a partner infected with Zika virus.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted sexually via prolonged shedding of replication-competent infectious virus in human seminal fluid lasting months post-onset.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted hematogenously across the placental syncytiotrophoblast and Hofbauer cells directly into the developing fetal circulation.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Confers the highest clinical risk of severe embryonic neural destruction, microcephaly, and fetal demise upon maternal infection.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Poses substantial risk for fetal neurodevelopmental disruption, cerebral calcifications, ventriculomegaly, and growth restriction.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Remains vulnerable to congenital infection, placental insufficiency, preterm labor, and late-onset subtle neurosensory deficits.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired iatrogenically via transfusion of unscreened platelet units or packed red blood cells from an asymptomatically viremic donor.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Transmitted iatrogenically through solid organ transplantation harvested from an actively viremic allograft donor.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Acquired occupationally via accidental percutaneous needle-stick inoculation or mucocutaneous splash in research laboratories.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Features an intrinsic human incubation period ranging between 3 and 14 days from initial exposure to clinical symptom onset.

relationships.keywords: INCUBATION_PERIOD
relationships.description: [INCUBATION_PERIOD] Typically manifests clinical illness within a median incubation window of 3 to 7 days following vector inoculation.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Maintained in African and Asian jungle sylvatic enzootic cycles between arboreal non-human primates and forest canopy Aedes mosquitoes.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Non-immune international travelers visiting active transmission zones lack background immunity and risk introducing the virus home.

relationships.keywords: EXPOSURE_TO
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Facilitated by domestic artificial water storage receptacles, discarded tires, and flowerpots that serve as primary Aedes larval breeding habitats.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of objective systemic vascular plasma leakage (pleural effusion, ascites, or hemoconcentration) rules out uncomplicated Zika virus.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Serial hematocrit increase of 20% or more above baseline rules out uncomplicated Zika virus and strongly indicates severe dengue.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Platelet count dropping below 50,000/µL rules out uncomplicated Zika virus, pointing toward dengue, severe malaria, or leptospirosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of spontaneous bleeding, epistaxis, hematemesis, melena, or menorrhagia rules out uncomplicated Zika in favor of hemorrhagic fevers.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Hypotension, narrow pulse pressure (≤20 mmHg), cold clammy extremities, or oliguria rules out uncomplicated Zika virus.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Severe, crippling, incapacitating polyarthritis that prevents walking or normal hand grip rules out Zika in favor of Chikungunya.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Severe inflammatory joint stiffness lasting over 1 hour upon waking rules out Zika virus, supporting Chikungunya or autoimmune disease.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Continuous high-grade fever exceeding 39.5°C to 40.0°C rules out the typical low-grade fever profile of Zika virus.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Fever persisting beyond 7 to 10 days rules out uncomplicated acute Zika virus, which reliably defervesces within 2 to 7 days.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Copious purulent or mucopurulent ocular discharge and morning eyelid crusting rules out Zika's non-purulent conjunctivitis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Agonizing photophobia and ocular pain on light exposure rules out uncomplicated Zika, indicating measles, keratitis, or anterior uveitis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of pathognomonic bluish-white pinpoint Koplik spots on the buccal mucosa definitively rules out Zika virus in favor of measles.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Heavy paroxysmal coughing, severe purulent rhinorrhea, and respiratory distress rules out Zika virus in favor of respiratory pathogens.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Prominent, markedly tender posterior auricular and suboccipital adenopathy rules out Zika virus, favoring acute rubella.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Violent teeth-chattering rigors followed by rapid thermal spikes and drenching sweats rules out Zika virus in favor of malaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Confluent fiery erythematous malar facial erythema with circumoral pallor rules out Zika virus, indicating Parvovirus B19.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Cutaneous lesions progressing from papules to pruritic fluid-filled teardrop vesicles on an erythematous base rules out Zika, indicating varicella.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Scleral icterus, overt clinical jaundice, and dark tea-colored urine rules out uncomplicated Zika, indicating yellow fever or leptospirosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute oliguria, severe azotemia, or gross hematuria rules out uncomplicated Zika, pointing toward severe leptospirosis or hantavirus.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of a cigarette-burn black necrotic eschar (tache noire) rules out Zika virus, definitively indicating scrub typhus or rickettsiosis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Palpable moderate-to-massive splenomegaly crossing the midclavicular line rules out Zika virus, pointing toward visceral leishmaniasis or chronic malaria.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Absolute neutrophil count dropping below 500/µL or WBC <2,000/µL rules out uncomplicated Zika virus, suggesting drug toxicity or typhoid.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Dengue Fever, which causes high continuous/biphasic fever (>39°C), agonizing retro-orbital ache, marked leukopenia, profound thrombocytopenia (<50,000/µL), and potential plasma leakage shock at defervescence, unlike Zika's mild fever, early rash, and non-purulent conjunctivitis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Chikungunya Virus Disease, which causes abrupt high-spiking fever and incapacitating, severe symmetrical polyarthritis with prominent swelling and morning stiffness that persists for months, whereas Zika causes mild, transient, non-erosive polyarthralgia.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Yellow Fever, which progresses to a severe toxic phase with high fever, jaundice, black vomit (hematemesis), acute kidney injury, and high mortality, contrasting sharply with the benign self-limited course of uncomplicated Zika.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Measles Virus Infection, which is characterized by a prominent catarrhal prodrome with high fever, severe cough, coryza, photophobic conjunctivitis, and pathognomonic buccal Koplik spots, all of which are absent in Zika virus.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Rubella Virus Infection, which features prominent tender suboccipital and postauricular lymphadenopathy and lacks the prominent conjunctival hyperemia, mosquito-borne kinetics, and profound fetal brain parenchymal necrosis seen in Zika.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Parvovirus B19 Infection, which causes classic slapped-cheek erythema in children and acute symmetric polyarthropathy mimicking rheumatoid arthritis in adult females, lacking tropical vector exposure, conjunctival hyperemia, and seminal transmission.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from West Nile Encephalitis, which causes asymmetric acute flaccid poliomyelitis-like paralysis and coarse tremors, contrasting with Zika's symmetrical ascending Guillain-Barré polyradiculoneuropathy and characteristic teratogenic fetal syndrome.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Mayaro Virus Disease, an Amazonian alphavirus that causes high fever and debilitating chronic polyarthritis lasting several months, in contrast to Zika's transient 2 to 7 day mild polyarthralgia and non-purulent conjunctivitis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Oropouche Fever, an orthobunyavirus that presents with high fever, severe headache, photophobia, and frequent debilitating clinical relapses occurring 1 to 2 weeks later, whereas Zika resolves uneventfully without biphasic relapses.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Falciparum Malaria, which presents with cyclical paroxysmal rigors, high fevers, hemolytic anemia, splenomegaly, and intraerythrocytic rings on blood smear, contrasting with Zika's normal CBC, self-limiting course, and rash.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Leptospirosis Disease, which follows freshwater rodent urine exposure and causes profound conjunctival suffusion without discharge, severe calf tenderness, jaundice, and acute oliguric renal failure (Weil's syndrome), absent in Zika.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Scrub Typhus Infection, which features a pathognomonic necrotic eschar at the chigger bite site, regional lymphadenopathy, high spiking fever, and elevated transaminases that rapidly responds to doxycycline, unlike viral Zika.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Acute HIV Seroconversion, which causes high fever, painful mucocutaneous oral/genital ulcers, exudative pharyngitis, generalized lymphadenopathy, and high viral RNA load, lacking Zika's conjunctival hyperemia and mosquito epidemiology.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Infectious Mononucleosis, which presents with severe exudative tonsillitis, prominent cervical adenopathy, splenomegaly, and atypical lymphocytosis on blood smear, whereas Zika features non-exudative pharynx and no atypical lymphocytosis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection, which typically causes periventricular calcifications, petechiae (blueberry muffin rash), and hepatosplenomegaly, contrasting with Zika's corticomedullary junction calcifications, craniofacial collapse, and arthrogryposis.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Congenital Toxoplasmosis, which presents with the classic Sabin tetrad of diffuse parenchymal calcifications, hydrocephalus, and chorioretinitis, whereas Zika causes severe microcephaly, craniosynostotic vault collapse, and simplified gyri.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Congenital Rubella Syndrome, which features the Gregg triad of dense cataracts, sensorineural deafness, and patent ductus arteriosus, whereas Congenital Zika lacks congenital cardiac structural defects and cataracts.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from Secondary Syphilis, which causes widespread copper-red maculopapular lesions on palms and soles, condyloma lata, generalized non-tender adenopathy, and positive treponemal serology, lacking the acute febrile and conjunctival presentation of Zika.
